title: X は Y です (X is Y / Topic & Copula)
meaning: Identify or describe a topic: as for X, it is Y.
connection: X は noun です; noun です is enough when the topic is understood.
nuance: は is written は but pronounced わ when it marks the topic. It tells the listener what the statement is about; it is not simply a replacement for the English subject. If both speakers already know the topic, omit it: 学生です can mean I am a student, she is a student, or they are students, depending on context. Japanese nouns generally do not require a/an and do not automatically change for plural number. です makes the noun predicate polite and non-past; it does not change with person or number. Do not append です to an ordinary finite verb such as 行くです. Adjectives have their own patterns, introduced later: 静かです and 高いです, but not 静かだです or 高いだです. Use a name/title rather than repeatedly translating English you as あなた.
keyTakeaway: State the topic only when needed; put the identifying noun before polite です.

sentences.japanese: 私はアリゾナ大学の学生です。
sentences.english: I am a student at the University of Arizona.
sentences.literal: I topic University-of-Arizona's student am.
sentences.nuanceNote: Standard polite self-identification.

sentences.japanese: 私は会社員です。
sentences.english: I am an office worker.
sentences.nuanceNote: は marks what the statement is about; 会社員です identifies that topic politely.

sentences.japanese: 学生ですか。はい、学生です。
sentences.english: Are you a student? Yes, I am.
sentences.nuanceNote: Neither sentence needs 私 or あなた when the context supplies who is being discussed.

sentences.japanese: 二人とも学生です。
sentences.english: Both people are students.
sentences.useLabel: Nouns do not mark number automatically
sentences.nuanceNote: 学生 itself does not change into a plural form; 二人とも supplies the number information.

sentences.japanese: 私はカリフォルニア大学の留学生です。
sentences.english: I am an international student at the University of California.
sentences.nuanceNote: Standard polite self-introduction formula.

sentences.japanese: スミスさんは学生ですか。はい、（私は）学生です。
sentences.english: Are you a student, Smith-san? Yes, I am.
sentences.nuanceNote: Once the topic is established by conversational context, Japanese naturally omits the pronoun.

sentences.japanese: 昼ご飯は食べましたが、朝ご飯は食べませんでした。
sentences.english: I ate lunch, but as for breakfast, I didn't eat.
sentences.nuanceNote: は marks contrast between two parallel contextual topics.

quiz.question: スミスさん（　　）イギリス人です。
quiz.translation: Smith-san is British.
quiz.grammarFocus: Topic particle は
quiz.ruleHint: X は noun です; noun です is enough when the topic is understood.

explanations.reason: Correct! は marks Smith-san as the topic being identified as British.
Incorrect. を marks direct objects of action verbs.
Incorrect. に marks destination, time, or location of existence.
Incorrect. へ marks direction of movement.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 36 (PDF p. 44). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 質問の「か」 (Question Sentence Marker 〜ですか)
meaning: Make a polite question with sentence-final か.
connection: Nですか; question word + ですか
nuance: Add か to a polite statement without English-style inversion. For an information question, keep the unknown item in its usual position: 専攻は何ですか asks what the major is. Answer with the requested information; はい/いいえ alone fits a yes/no question, not what/when. Known topics may be omitted. 何 is なん immediately before です; other contexts have なに or fixed readings. Japanese polite questions commonly end in 。 rather than requiring ?.
keyTakeaway: Statement + か asks a question; a question word asks for specific information.

sentences.japanese: 専攻は何ですか。「日本語です。」
sentences.english: What is your major? 'It is Japanese.'
sentences.literal: Major topic what is question? Japanese is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Interrogative 何 directly takes ですか.

sentences.japanese: 田中さんは先生ですか。いいえ、学生です。
sentences.english: Is Tanaka a teacher? No, Tanaka is a student.
sentences.nuanceNote: か turns the polite statement into a question without changing the word order.

sentences.japanese: 専攻は何ですか。経済です。
sentences.english: What is your major? Economics.
sentences.useLabel: Question word in its normal position
sentences.nuanceNote: 何 replaces the unknown identifying noun. Its reading before です is なん.

quiz.question: 今何時（　　）。「午後二時です。」
quiz.translation: What time is it now? 'It is 2:00 PM.'
quiz.grammarFocus: Question particle か
quiz.ruleHint: Nですか; question word + ですか

explanations.reason: Correct! ですか forms a standard polite question asking the time.
でした is a past statement ending, not the present question ですか.
Incorrect. でして is te-form of copula.
Incorrect. ですね seeks confirmation ('isn't it?'), not an open inquiry.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 36 (PDF p. 44). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: Noun1 の Noun2 (Noun Modification, Possession & Affiliation)
meaning: Particle の connects two nouns where Noun1 modifies, describes, or possesses Noun2 ('Noun1's Noun2' or 'Noun2 of Noun1').
connection: Noun1 (Modifier/Owner) + の + Noun2 (Main item)
nuance: MODIFIER FIRST: Japanese strictly places the modifier before の: 日本の大学 (Japanese university), 私の友達 (my friend).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Owner/Category] の [Item]. The main noun is ALWAYS at the end!

sentences.japanese: たけしさんはさくら大学の学生です。
sentences.english: Takeshi-san is a student of Sakura University.
sentences.literal: Takeshi topic Sakura-University's student is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Affiliation: Sakura University modifies student.

sentences.japanese: これは姉のかばんです。
sentences.english: This is my older sister's bag.
sentences.nuanceNote: The possessor comes before の; the possessed item comes after it.

sentences.japanese: 日本語の先生は山田さんです。
sentences.english: The Japanese-language teacher is Yamada.
sentences.nuanceNote: の can identify a field or category, not only ownership.

sentences.japanese: 友達の大学の図書館は大きいです。
sentences.english: The library at my friend's university is large.
sentences.useLabel: Several links in a noun phrase
sentences.nuanceNote: The head noun is 図書館; each preceding の phrase narrows what library is meant.

quiz.question: これは私の母（　　）写真です。
quiz.translation: This is a photo of my mother.
quiz.grammarFocus: Possessive / Attribute particle の
quiz.ruleHint: Noun1 (Modifier/Owner) + の + Noun2 (Main item)

explanations.reason: Correct! の connects the subject of the photo (母) to the photo itself (写真).
Incorrect. に marks indirect objects, destinations, or specific time.
Incorrect. を marks direct objects of action verbs.
Incorrect. と means 'and' or 'with'.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 36 (PDF p. 44). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 時間と年齢 (Telling Time with 〜時・〜分 and Age with 〜歳)
meaning: Formulas for hours (〜時 / じ), minutes (〜分 / ふん・ぷん), and age (〜歳 / さい) including critical phonological irregularities.
connection: Number + 時 (Hour) | Number + 分 (Minutes) | Number + 歳 (Age)
nuance: Hours: 四時よじ、七時しちじ、九時くじ. Minutes include 一分いっぷん、三分さんぷん、四分よんぷん、六分ろっぷん、八分はっぷん、十分じゅっぷん／じっぷん. Ages include 一歳いっさい、八歳はっさい、十歳じゅっさい／じっさい and 二十歳はたち. 何時なんじ asks the time; 何歳なんさい or おいくつ asks age. 半 after the hour means half past. Learn the actual counter reading rather than deriving it mechanically from the independent number.
keyTakeaway: Learn standard time readings: 四時よじ、七時しちじ、九時くじ. 七時 can also be read ななじ to avoid ambiguity in some contexts. 二十歳 is はたち; counter sound changes need separate practice.

sentences.japanese: 今、午前九時半です。私は十九歳です。
sentences.english: Right now, it is 9:30 AM. I am nineteen years old.
sentences.literal: Now AM 9-hour-half is. I 19-years-old am.
sentences.nuanceNote: 九時 is read くじ; 半 means half past.

sentences.japanese: 今、四時です。会議は九時からです。
sentences.english: It is four now. The meeting starts at nine.
sentences.nuanceNote: 四時 is よじ and 九時 is くじ; the counter combination has a conventional reading.

sentences.japanese: 電車は八時十分に出ます。
sentences.english: The train leaves at ten past eight.
sentences.nuanceNote: 十分 as ten minutes is じゅっぷん/じっぷん, not the adjective 十分じゅうぶん meaning sufficient.

sentences.japanese: 妹は二十歳です。
sentences.english: My younger sister is twenty.
sentences.nuanceNote: Age 二十歳 is normally はたち; do not mechanically read the kanji one by one.

quiz.question: 会議は午後（　　）から始まります。
quiz.translation: The meeting starts from 4:00 PM.
quiz.grammarFocus: Irregular hour reading 四時 (よじ)
quiz.ruleHint: Number + 時 (Hour) | Number + 分 (Minutes) | Number + 歳 (Age)

explanations.reason: Correct! 4 o'clock is strictly read as よじ (yoji).
Incorrect. よんじ is a common learner error but does not exist in standard Japanese.
四時 has the conventional reading よじ. The general number reading し does not carry over to this counter combination; do not invent an etymological reason.
Incorrect. ななじ is 7, not 4.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 36 (PDF p. 44). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: Genki I: Time (時・分) & Age (歳) Reading Matrix
table.subtitle: The foundational number transformations and phonetic traps in Lesson 1.

rows.label: Hours (〜時: じ)
cells: 1時(いちじ), 2時(にじ), 3時(さんじ), 5時(ごじ), 6時(ろくじ), 8時(はちじ), 10時(じゅうじ), 11時(じゅういちじ), 12時(じゅうにじ)
⚠️ 4時 = よじ (NOT よんじ/しじ), 7時 = しちじ (sometimes ななじ), 9時 = くじ (NOT きゅうじ)
何時 (なんじ)? Example: 今、何時ですか。(What time is it now?)
rows.note: Trap alert: 4:00, 7:00, 9:00 have unique readings that JLPT tests frequently.

rows.label: Minutes (〜分: ふん/ぷん)
cells: Unvoiced ふん: 2分(にふん), 5分(ごふん), 7分(ななふん), 9分(きゅうふん)
Geminate / Voiced ぷん: 1分(いっぷん), 3分(さんぷん), 4分(よんぷん), 6分(ろっぷん), 8分(はっぷん/はちふん), 10分(じゅっぷん/じっぷん)
何分 (なんぷん)? Half past = 半 (はん): 1時半 (1:30)
rows.note: Mnemonic: 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10 は半濁音の「ぷん」になります。

rows.label: Age (〜歳: さい)
cells: 2歳(にさい), 3歳(さんさい), 4歳(よんさい), 5歳(ごさい), 6歳(ろくさい), 7歳(ななさい), 9歳(きゅうさい)
⚠️ 1歳 = いっさい, 8歳 = はっさい, 10歳 = じゅっさい (じっさい), 20歳 = はたち (二十歳)
何歳 (なんさい)? Polite: おいくつですか。
rows.note: 20歳 は「はたち（二十歳）」と読み、後ろに「さい」は付きません。

rows.label: Telephone & School Year
cells: 学年: 1年生(いちねんせい), 2年生(にねんせい), 3年生(さんねんせい), 4年生(よねんせい ⚠️)
Telephone hyphens are read as の: 090-1234-5678 (ぜろきゅうぜろ の いちにさんよん の...)
何年生 (なんねんせい)? / 電話番号は何番 (なんばん)?
rows.note: 4th year student is よねんせい (NOT よんねんせい).

title: これ・それ・あれ・どれ (Thing Demonstrative Pronouns)
meaning: Standalone pronouns indicating physical things relative to speaker and listener: これ (near speaker), それ (near listener), あれ (far from both), どれ (which one).
connection: これ / それ / あれ / どれ + は / が / を (Standalone Pronouns)
nuance: STANDALONE RULE: これ/それ/あれ/どれ stand alone as independent nouns and cannot directly modify a noun (require この/その/あの/どの). DISTANCE: これ refers to items near the speaker, それ near the listener, and あれ far from both. QUESTION WORD: Question word どれ cannot take topic particle は; it must take subject particle が (e.g. どれがあなたのペンですか). SOCIAL CONSTRAINT: Avoid using the れ-series words (これ, それ, あれ) to refer to people in their earshot (e.g. introducing someone with 「これは友達のメアリーさんです」 is impolite; use 「この人」 or their name directly).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: これ/それ/あれ/どれ stand ALONE. こ (me), そ (you), あ (far away), ど (which?).

sentences.japanese: これは日本のペンです。あれはアメリカのペンです。
sentences.english: This is a Japanese pen. That one over there is an American pen.
sentences.literal: This topic Japan's pen is. That-over-there America's pen is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Spatial contrast between proximal and distal items.

sentences.japanese: これは私のスマートフォンです。
sentences.english: This is my smartphone.
sentences.nuanceNote: これ stands alone and refers to an item near the speaker in the basic physical-distance use.

sentences.japanese: あれは何ですか。古い時計です。
sentences.english: What is that over there? It is an old clock.
sentences.nuanceNote: あれ refers to something distant from both participants in this physical context.

sentences.japanese: 山田さんの傘はどれですか。これです。
sentences.english: Which umbrella is Yamada's? This one.
sentences.nuanceNote: どれ asks for a choice among items; the answer can be another standalone demonstrative.

quiz.question: 指さした物について質問します。「（　　）は誰の傘ですか。」
quiz.translation: Pointing at an object: Whose umbrella is this?
quiz.grammarFocus: Demonstrative pronoun それ
quiz.ruleHint: これ / それ / あれ / どれ + は / が / を (Standalone Pronouns)

explanations.reason: これ stands alone and refers to the indicated object.
この requires a following noun; このは is not this construction.
ここで marks an action location and cannot identify an umbrella here.
ここに marks a location of existence, not the indicated object.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 56 (PDF p. 64). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: この・その・あの・どの + Noun (Pre-Noun Demonstrative Modifiers)
meaning: Demonstrative determiners that must immediately precede and specify a noun: この (this N), その (that N near you), あの (that N over there), どの (which N).
connection: この / その / あの / どの + Noun
nuance: ADNOMINAL MODIFIERS: Unlike これ which stands alone, この/その/あの/どの CANNOT stand alone (「このは私の」 ❌ is ungrammatical; must be 「この時計は私の」). PEOPLE REFERENCE: You can use この/その/あの plus a noun to refer respectfully to people (e.g. あの学生、この方). QUESTION WORD: Because どの is a question word, it cannot take particle は; it must be followed by が (e.g. どの学生が日本人ですか).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: この・その・あの・どの MUST be glued to a following Noun!

sentences.japanese: あの時計はいくらですか。「三千円です。」
sentences.english: How much is that watch over there? 'It is 3,000 yen.'
sentences.literal: That watch-over-there how-much is? 3000-yen is.
sentences.nuanceNote: あの directly modifies noun 時計.

sentences.japanese: この本は私のです。
sentences.english: This book is mine.
sentences.nuanceNote: この modifies 本. In the predicate, 私の can stand for my book because the item is understood.

sentences.japanese: どのかばんが好きですか。あの赤いかばんが好きです。
sentences.english: Which bag do you like? I like that red bag over there.
sentences.nuanceNote: どの and あの each modify a following noun phrase; どれ/あれ stand alone instead.

quiz.question: 「その辞書」の意味になる形を選んでください。すみません、（　　）辞書を見せてください。
quiz.translation: Choose the form meaning that dictionary: Please show me that dictionary.
quiz.grammarFocus: Pre-noun determiner その
quiz.ruleHint: この / その / あの / どの + Noun

explanations.reason: その directly modifies 辞書.
それ is a standalone pronoun.
そこ means a place and does not directly modify 辞書.
その already modifies a noun; do not add の.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 56 (PDF p. 64). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: ここ・そこ・あそこ・どこ (Place Demonstrative Pronouns)
meaning: Demonstrative locational nouns indicating places: ここ (here), そこ (there near you), あそこ (over there), どこ (where).
connection: ここ / そこ / あそこ / どこ + は / に / で
nuance: PHONETIC IRREGULARITY: Notice the pattern: こ, そ, but あそこ (NOT あこ ❌)! Interrogative is どこ.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Note the irregularity: ここ, そこ, あそこ (with -そ- in the middle!), どこ.

sentences.japanese: 図書館はどこですか。「あそこです。」
sentences.english: Where is the library? 'It is over there.'
sentences.literal: Library topic where is? Over-there is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Inquiring place with どこ; answering with distant place あそこ.

sentences.japanese: ここで写真を撮ってもいいですか。
sentences.english: May I take photos here?
sentences.nuanceNote: ここ is a place noun; で marks it as the location of the action.

sentences.japanese: 郵便局はあそこにあります。
sentences.english: The post office is over there.
sentences.nuanceNote: あそこに marks the place where the post office exists, rather than an action location.

quiz.question: お手洗いは（　　）ですか。「あちらのエレベーターの隣です。」
quiz.translation: Where is the restroom? 'It is next to the elevator over there.'
quiz.grammarFocus: Locational interrogative どこ
quiz.ruleHint: ここ / そこ / あそこ / どこ + は / に / で

explanations.reason: Correct! どこ is the place interrogative meaning 'where'.
Incorrect. どれ means 'which item among 3+'.
Incorrect. だれ means 'who'.
Incorrect. どう means 'how'.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 56 (PDF p. 64). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 助詞「も」 (Inclusive Particle 'Also / Too')
meaning: Indicates inclusion: equates the predicate for a new topic to that of a previously mentioned entity ('X is also Y').
connection: Noun + も (Directly replaces は, が, or を!)
nuance: In basic also constructions, も usually replaces は, が or を; it follows particles such as に and で. Literary/emphatic をも exists, so do not treat the beginner replacement rule as a ban in every register.
keyTakeaway: In basic also constructions, も usually replaces は, が or を; it follows particles such as に and で. Literary/emphatic をも exists, so do not treat the beginner replacement rule as a ban in every register.

sentences.japanese: メアリーさんはアメリカ人です。ロバートさんもアメリカ人です。
sentences.english: Mary is an American. Robert is also an American.
sentences.literal: Mary topic American is. Robert also American is.
sentences.nuanceNote: も replaces は to establish shared national identity.

sentences.japanese: 兄は学生です。私も学生です。
sentences.english: My older brother is a student. I am a student too.
sentences.nuanceNote: も replaces the topic は while adding the same description for another person.

sentences.japanese: 京都へ行きました。奈良にも行きました。
sentences.english: I went to Kyoto. I also went to Nara.
sentences.nuanceNote: も follows に, retaining the destination relation. Do not remove every particle mechanically.

quiz.question: 私（　　）学生です。田中さんと同じです。
quiz.translation: I am a student too, like Tanaka.
quiz.grammarFocus: Particle も replacing direct object
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + も (Directly replaces は, が, or を!)

explanations.reason: も adds me to the group: also a student.
を is an object marker, not the topic/addition here.
に does not form this copula sentence.
で cannot form this copula sentence here.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 56 (PDF p. 64). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: じゃないです / じゃありません (Negative Copula: Is Not)
meaning: Polite non-past negative form of copula です: 'is not / am not / are not'.
connection: Noun / な-adj + じゃないです (Conversational) / じゃありません (Formal)
nuance: REGISTER DIFFERENCE: じゃないです is standard colloquial speech. じゃありません is more conservative polite speech. ではありません is formal and preferred in writing. NOUN RESTRICTION: This pattern only negates nouns (and な-adjectives). It CANNOT negate い-adjectives (e.g. 「高いじゃないです」 ❌ is ungrammatical; must be 「高くないです」). SHORT ANSWER RESTRICTION: In negative replies, です and じゃない cannot stand alone without the predicate noun (say 「いいえ、日本人じゃないです」, NOT 「いいえ、じゃないです」 ❌).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Negative of です is じゃないです (or じゃありません). Connects to nouns and な-adjectives.

sentences.japanese: 山田さんは留学生じゃありません。先生です。
sentences.english: Yamada-san is not an international student. He is a teacher.
sentences.literal: Yamada topic international-student is-not. Teacher is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Polite denial of category followed by affirmative correction.

sentences.japanese: 私は先生じゃありません。学生です。
sentences.english: I am not a teacher. I am a student.
sentences.nuanceNote: A noun predicate uses じゃありません or じゃないです; ありません alone is not the negative of this noun identity sentence.

sentences.japanese: この町は静かじゃないです。今日は寒くないです。
sentences.english: This town is not quiet. It is not cold today.
sentences.nuanceNote: The な-adjective uses じゃない; the い-adjective uses くない. These are different conjugation patterns.

quiz.question: 私は一年生（　　）。三年生です。
quiz.translation: I am not a first-year student. I am a third-year student.
quiz.grammarFocus: Negative copula じゃありません
quiz.ruleHint: Noun / な-adj + じゃないです (Conversational) / じゃありません (Formal)

explanations.reason: Correct! じゃありません (or じゃないです) is the polite negative copula for nouns.
Incorrect. ありません is for inanimate existence (there isn't), not noun identity.
Incorrect. ないでした is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. でした is past affirmative ('was').

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 56 (PDF p. 64). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: だれの・ね・よ
meaning: Whose; seeking agreement; offering information.
connection: だれの + N; sentence + ね / よ
nuance: だれの asks for the owner/possessor (だれの + Noun); the repeated noun can be omitted after の in the answer (「田中さんのです」). SENTENCE PARTICLES: ね seeks listener confirmation or shared agreement ('right?'). よ presents information the listener is unaware of or asserts confidence ('I tell you / you know'). Their force also depends on rising vs falling pitch.
keyTakeaway: だれの + N; sentence + ね / よ

sentences.japanese: これはだれのノートですか。私のですよ。
sentences.english: Whose notebook is this? It is mine.

sentences.japanese: これはだれの傘ですか。田中さんのです。
sentences.english: Whose umbrella is this? It is Tanaka's.
sentences.nuanceNote: だれの asks for the possessor; the repeated noun 傘 can be omitted after の in the answer.

sentences.japanese: 今日は暑いですね。この部屋は涼しいですよ。
sentences.english: It is hot today, isn't it? This room is cool, you know.
sentences.nuanceNote: ね invites shared recognition; よ offers information. Their effect also depends on tone and context.

quiz.question: A:「これは（　　）傘ですか。」 B:「田中さんの傘ですよ。」
quiz.translation: A: 'Whose umbrella is this?' B: 'It's Tanaka's umbrella, you know.'
quiz.grammarFocus: だれの (Whose) + よ
quiz.ruleHint: だれの + Noun asks about ownership/possession.

explanations.reason: Correct! だれの modifies 傘 to ask 'whose umbrella'.
Incorrect. どれ means 'which one' (among three or more) and does not ask for personal ownership.
Incorrect. どこの asks for place, country of origin, or company.
Incorrect. だれ lacks particle の needed to modify the following noun 傘.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 56 (PDF p. 64). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ます / 〜ません (Polite Non-Past Affirmative & Negative)
meaning: The standard polite verbal ending for present habitual actions and future actions: 〜ます (affirmative) and 〜ません (negative).
connection: Verb stem (ます-stem) + ます / ません
nuance: NON-PAST INCLUDES FUTURE: Japanese has only two grammatical tenses: past and non-past. 食べます means 'I eat (habitually)' OR 'I will eat (future)'.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-stem + ます = Present habit OR future plan. Negative = 〜ません.

sentences.japanese: 私は毎朝コーヒーを飲みますが、お茶は飲みません。
sentences.english: I drink coffee every morning, but I do not drink tea.
sentences.literal: I every-morning coffee drink but, tea drink-not.
sentences.nuanceNote: Habitual affirmative and negative actions.

sentences.japanese: 毎朝、六時に起きます。
sentences.english: I get up at six every morning.
sentences.nuanceNote: Non-past ます describes a regular habit here.

sentences.japanese: 明日は家で勉強します。図書館には行きません。
sentences.english: Tomorrow I will study at home. I will not go to the library.
sentences.nuanceNote: The same non-past form can describe future plans; ません negates the verb politely.

quiz.question: 今日は休みなので、会社には行き（　　）。
quiz.translation: It is a day off, so I will not go to the office.
quiz.grammarFocus: Polite non-past negative 〜ません
quiz.ruleHint: Verb stem (ます-stem) + ます / ません

explanations.reason: The polite negative of 行きます is 行きません.
Plain negative is 行かない, not 行きない.
行きなく is not a valid conjugation.
行きまない is not a valid conjugation.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 82 (PDF p. 90). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ませんか (Polite Invitation: Won't You? / Would You Like To?)
meaning: Invites the listener to do an activity together politely: 'Won't you...? / Would you like to...?'
connection: V-stem (ます-stem) + ませんか
nuance: POLITE INVITATION: Present negative question 〜ませんか functions as a standard polite invitation ('Won't you...? / What do you say to...?'). Affirmative 〜ますか is merely a factual question, NOT an invitation. REFUSAL ETIQUETTE: In Japanese, polite refusal trails off with 「ちょっと…」 ('it is slightly inconvenient / impossible') rather than a blunt 「いいえ」. DIRECTION PERSPECTIVE: English 'I am coming!' is Japanese 「今行きます!」 (movement toward the listener is 行く, not 来る).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-stem + ませんか = The golden Japanese polite invitation! (一緒に食べませんか = Won't you eat with me?).

sentences.japanese: 今度の週末、一緒に美術館へ行きませんか。「ええ、ぜひ！」
sentences.english: Won't you go to the art museum together this coming weekend? 'Yes, by all means!'
sentences.literal: This-time's weekend, together art-museum go-won't-you? Yes, definitely!
sentences.nuanceNote: Warm invitation paired with enthusiastic agreement.

sentences.japanese: 一緒に昼ご飯を食べませんか。いいですね。食べましょう。
sentences.english: Would you like to have lunch together? That sounds good. Let's eat.
sentences.nuanceNote: ませんか invites; ましょう accepts/proposes proceeding.

sentences.japanese: 今夜、映画を見ませんか。すみません、今夜はちょっと。
sentences.english: Would you like to watch a movie tonight? Sorry, tonight is a bit difficult.
sentences.nuanceNote: A refusal can be softened by context and a trailing ちょっと; it does not need a blunt negative response.

quiz.question: 少し疲れましたね。喫茶店でお茶を（　　）ませんか。
quiz.translation: We've gotten a bit tired, haven't we? Won't you drink some tea at a cafe?
quiz.grammarFocus: Polite invitation 〜ませんか with verb stem
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem (ます-stem) + ませんか

explanations.reason: Correct! 飲む stem is 飲み, connecting to ませんか (飲みませんか).
Incorrect. 飲む is dictionary form; cannot connect to ませんか.
Incorrect. 飲んで is te-form.
Incorrect. 飲ま is negative stem.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 82 (PDF p. 90). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 動詞の活用・語順・助詞
meaning: Verb groups, word order and core particles.
connection: Topic は; object を; destination に/へ; action location で; companion と; predicate last
nuance: VERB CONJUGATION GROUPS: (1) Ru-verbs: drop る and append ます/ません (食べる→食べます). (2) U-verbs: shift final u-row sound to i-row and append ます/ません (飲む→飲みます). CRITICAL EXCEPTION: 帰る (かえる) ends in -eru but is an U-verb (conjugates to 帰ります / 帰りません, NOT かえます ❌!). (3) Irregular verbs: する→します, 来る (くる)→来ます (きます). PARTICLES: を (direct object, pronounced 'o'), で (location where action takes place), に/へ (goal/direction of movement, へ pronounced 'e'). WORD ORDER: Flexible noun-particle ordering, but the finite verb predicate MUST remain at the sentence end.
keyTakeaway: Topic は; object を; destination に/へ; action location で; companion と; predicate last

sentences.japanese: 私は図書館で日本語を勉強します。
sentences.english: I study Japanese at the library.

sentences.japanese: 学校に行きます。学校で日本語を勉強します。
sentences.english: I go to school. I study Japanese at school.
sentences.nuanceNote: に marks the destination; で marks where the studying occurs.

sentences.japanese: 本を読みます。テレビを見ます。宿題をします。
sentences.english: I read a book. I watch television. I do homework.
sentences.nuanceNote: 読む is an u-verb, 見る a ru-verb, and する irregular; their polite stems are formed differently.

sentences.japanese: 毎晩図書館で日本語を勉強します。
sentences.english: I study Japanese in the library every night.
sentences.nuanceNote: 勉強する is an irregular compound verb (勉強します).

sentences.japanese: 食べる→食べます、見る→見ます、起きる→起きます。
sentences.english: Eat -> eat (polite); see -> see (polite); wake up -> wake up (polite).
sentences.nuanceNote: Ru-verbs drop final る and attach ます without vowel alternation.

sentences.japanese: 書く→書きます、話す→話します、待つ→待ちます。
sentences.english: Write -> write (polite); speak -> speak (polite); wait -> wait (polite).
sentences.nuanceNote: U-verbs shift the final u-vowel to the corresponding i-vowel before ます.

sentences.japanese: する→します、くる（来る）→きます（来ます）。
sentences.english: Do -> do (polite); come -> come (polite).
sentences.nuanceNote: Irregular verbs する and くる conjugate with stem changes.

quiz.question: 私は毎晩、図書館（　　）日本語を勉強します。
quiz.translation: I study Japanese at the library every night.
quiz.grammarFocus: Particle で (Location of Action)
quiz.ruleHint: Place + で marks the location where an active event takes place.

explanations.reason: Correct! で marks 図書館 as the place where the dynamic action of studying occurs.
Incorrect. に marks static location of existence (with います/あります) or destination of movement.
Incorrect. を marks direct objects (already used in 日本語を).
Incorrect. へ marks direction of travel towards a destination.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 82 (PDF p. 90). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: Genki I: The Three Verb Groups & Polite Conjugation Matrix
table.subtitle: Ru-verbs (一段), U-verbs (五段), and Irregular verbs (変格) in Lesson 3.

rows.label: Group 2: Ru-Verbs (一段動詞)
cells: Ends in る preceded by an /i/ or /e/ sound (e.g. 食べる, 見る, 起きる: 直前が「い段」または「え段」)
Simply DROP る to obtain the stem (食べ-, 見-, 起き-)
食べます / 食べません, 見ます / 見ません
Regular behavior: stems are stable across all conjugations.
rows.note: Drop る, add ます/ません.

rows.label: Group 1: U-Verbs (五段動詞)
cells: Ends in any basic -u syllable: う, つ, る, む, ぶ, ぬ, く, ぐ, す
Shift the final -u sound to the corresponding -i sound (u→i, tsu→chi, ru→ri, ku→ki, mu→mi, su→shi)
行く → 行きます / 行きません, 飲む → 飲みます, 話す → 話します, 待つ → 待ちます
⚠️ LOOKS LIKE RU BUT IS AN U-VERB: 帰る（かえります）, 入る（はいります）, 知る（しります）, 走る（はしります）!
rows.note: Golden Rule: If a verb ends in -aru, -oru, -uru, it is ALWAYS an U-verb. If it ends in -iru or -eru, check if it is one of the classic Godan exceptions like 帰る.

rows.label: Group 3: Irregular Verbs (不規則動詞)
cells: Only TWO verbs in the entire Japanese language: する (to do) and 来る (くる, to come)
Stems undergo complete vowel mutation: する → し-, くる → き-
します / しません, 来ます (きます) / 来ません (きません)
Compound suru-verbs follow this pattern: 勉強する → 勉強します, 案内する → 案内します
rows.note: 来（く）る は活用によって「来（き）ます」と読みが変化します。

title: 時間のに・頻度の副詞
meaning: When and how often an action happens.
connection: Clock/calendar time + に; 毎日 / 今日 usually without に; あまり / 全然 + negative
nuance: TIME MARKER に: Days of the week (日曜日に) and numerical clock times (七時に、十時半に) strictly require に. RELATIVE TIME BAN: Relative time expressions (今日、明日、昨日、毎日、毎晩、いつ) DO NOT take に (saying 「明日に」 ❌ is ungrammatical; must be 「明日」). NEGATIVE POLARITY ADVERBS: 全然 (not at all / never) and あまり (not often / not much) strictly require a negative verb ending (e.g. 「全然見ません」、「あまり勉強しません」).
keyTakeaway: Clock/calendar time + に; 毎日 / 今日 usually without に; あまり / 全然 + negative

sentences.japanese: 日曜日に泳ぎますが、平日はあまり泳ぎません。
sentences.english: I swim on Sundays, but do not swim much on weekdays.

sentences.japanese: 七時に起きます。明日は八時に起きます。
sentences.english: I get up at seven. Tomorrow I will get up at eight.
sentences.nuanceNote: Clock times take に; relative 明日 normally stands without it.

sentences.japanese: よく映画を見ますが、テレビはあまり見ません。
sentences.english: I often watch films, but I do not watch much television.
sentences.nuanceNote: よく gives high frequency; あまり with a negative gives low frequency/degree.

quiz.question: 毎朝七時（　　）起きますが、日曜日はあまり早く起きません。
quiz.translation: I get up at seven every morning, but on Sundays I don't get up very early.
quiz.grammarFocus: Time particle に + あまり + Negative
quiz.ruleHint: Specific numerical clock times take に; relative times like 毎朝 do not.

explanations.reason: Correct! Specific point in time (七時) takes particle に.
Incorrect. で marks means or action location, not clock time.
Incorrect. を marks direct objects.
Incorrect. へ marks direction of movement.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 82 (PDF p. 90). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ました・〜ませんでした・〜でした (Polite Past Tense of Verbs & Copula)
meaning: Past tense for verbs (〜ました / 〜ませんでした) and noun/adjectival predicates (〜でした / 〜じゃありませんでした).
connection: Verb stem + ました / ませんでした | Noun / な-adj + でした / じゃありませんでした
nuance: COPULA PAST NEGATIVE REGISTERS: じゃありませんでした is conservative polite speech; じゃなかったです is colloquial conversational polite; ではありませんでした is formal and preferred in writing. (Never use 「じゃないでした」 ❌). VERB PAST: Verb stem + ました (affirmative past) and ませんでした (negative past).
keyTakeaway: Standard polite past negative forms include じゃありませんでした and じゃなかったです. Do not use じゃないでした as the standard conjugation.

sentences.japanese: 昨日は雨でした。私はどこへも行きませんでした。
sentences.english: Yesterday was rainy. I did not go anywhere.
sentences.literal: Yesterday rain was. I anywhere go-past-neg.
sentences.nuanceNote: Past state of weather and past negation of activity.

sentences.japanese: 昨日は勉強しました。でも、運動はしませんでした。
sentences.english: Yesterday I studied, but I did not exercise.
sentences.nuanceNote: Verb stems take ました or ませんでした.

sentences.japanese: 昨日は休みでした。今日は休みじゃありません。
sentences.english: Yesterday was a day off. Today is not.
sentences.nuanceNote: でした is the noun-predicate past; it is not attached after an ordinary dictionary verb.

quiz.question: 昨夜は十二時まで日本語を（　　）。とても眠かったです。
quiz.translation: Last night I studied Japanese until 12 o'clock. I was very sleepy.
quiz.grammarFocus: Verb past tense 〜ました
quiz.ruleHint: Verb stem + ました / ませんでした | Noun / な-adj + でした / じゃありませんでした

explanations.reason: Correct! 勉強する past form is 勉強しました.
Incorrect. 勉強します is present/future non-past.
Incorrect. 勉強でした uses copula past without verb inflection.
Incorrect. 勉強しでした is ungrammatical hybrid.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 102 (PDF p. 110). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 位置の名詞 (Spatial Postpositions: 上・下・前・後ろ・中・隣・近く・間)
meaning: Spatial relational nouns indicating position relative to a reference point: X の [上/下/前/後ろ/中/隣/間] に.
connection: Reference Noun + の + [上 / 下 / 前 / 後ろ / 中 / 隣 / 近く / 間] + に
nuance: SPATIAL FORMULA: X は Y の [位置] にあります/います. Adjacent vs Nearby: 隣 (となり) is strictly for items of the SAME category side-by-side (two people or two buildings). For different categories (e.g. a bag next to a desk), use そば, よこ, or 近く. DYNAMIC ACTION AT LOCATION: When a dynamic action takes place at a location, the particle shifts from に to で (e.g. 「ホテルの前でメアリーさんを待ちました」 - I waited for Mary in front of the hotel).
keyTakeaway: 隣 identifies an adjacent neighbor; 近く means nearby. 間 places something between reference points. Do not infer an object's position from a sentence that provides no spatial context.

sentences.japanese: 猫が机の下で寝ています。銀行は郵便局と本屋の間にあります。
sentences.english: A cat is sleeping under the desk. The bank is between the post office and bookstore.
sentences.literal: Cat desk-under sleeping-is. Bank post-office and bookstore's between exists.
sentences.nuanceNote: Relational location followed by action/existence verbs.

sentences.japanese: 机の上に本があります。
sentences.english: There is a book on the desk.
sentences.nuanceNote: 机の上 is the location noun phrase; に marks the location of existence.

sentences.japanese: 銀行は駅と学校の間にあります。
sentences.english: The bank is between the station and the school.
sentences.nuanceNote: AとBの間 identifies the two reference points for between.

quiz.question: 鍵はかばん（　　）中にあります。
quiz.translation: The key is inside the bag.
quiz.grammarFocus: Spatial noun 中 (inside)
quiz.ruleHint: Reference Noun + の + [上 / 下 / 前 / 後ろ / 中 / 隣 / 近く / 間] + に

explanations.reason: A reference noun connects to 中 with の.
を does not modify 中.
が does not modify 中 here.
と does not express inside the bag.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 102 (PDF p. 110). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: あります・います
meaning: Existence and possession.
connection: Place に + thing が ある; person/animal が いる
nuance: ANIMATE VS INANIMATE: Use います for living, moving beings (people, animals) and あります for inanimate objects and plants. LOCATION PARTICLE に VS で: The stationary location of existence takes に (あそこにマクドナルドがあります). CRITICAL EXCEPTION: When あります means an event takes place, the location takes で (e.g. 「明日、京都でお祭りがあります」 - There will be a festival in Kyoto tomorrow!). POSSESSION CONTRAST: 「テレビがありません」 means I do not have/own a TV (negative of あります), whereas 「テレビじゃありません」 means It is not a TV (negative of です).
keyTakeaway: Place に + thing が ある; person/animal が いる

sentences.japanese: 庭に猫がいます。木もあります。
sentences.english: There is a cat in the garden. There is also a tree.

sentences.japanese: 教室に学生がいます。机もあります。
sentences.english: There are students in the classroom. There are desks too.
sentences.nuanceNote: Use いる for people/animals and ある for things in these basic existence statements.

sentences.japanese: 辞書はどこにありますか。かばんの中にあります。
sentences.english: Where is the dictionary? It is in the bag.
sentences.useLabel: Ask where an identified thing is
sentences.nuanceNote: The identified dictionary is the topic; the question asks for its location.

sentences.japanese: 兄弟がいますか。姉が一人います。
sentences.english: Do you have any siblings? I have one older sister.
sentences.nuanceNote: いる can describe having a family member, not just physical presence at a location.

quiz.question: あそこに大きい木が（　　）、木の下に可愛い猫が（　　）。
quiz.translation: Over there is a big tree, and under the tree is a cute cat.
quiz.grammarFocus: あります (Inanimate) vs います (Animate)
quiz.ruleHint: Inanimate objects (木, 机) take あります; living people and animals (猫, 学生) take います.

explanations.reason: Correct! 木 is an inanimate plant (あります) and 猫 is a living animal (います).
Incorrect. Inverts animate and inanimate verbs of existence.
Incorrect. Animate living animals like 猫 require います.
Incorrect. Inanimate objects like 木 require あります.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 102 (PDF p. 110). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 時間・数量・と
meaning: Duration, quantities, also and together with.
connection: Duration without に; N と N; person と + action; quantity + も
nuance: DURATION BARE NOUN: Time duration (一時間、三時間半) is expressed with a bare noun without particle に (「一時間待ちました」; saying 「一時間に待ちました」 ❌ is ungrammatical). PARTICLE と: (1) Connects two nouns (日本語と英語). (2) Marks companion / together with (友達と行きます). PARTICLE も COMBINATIONS: も replaces は, が, を; but combines with に, へ, で (e.g. 京都へ行きました。大阪へも行きました。カフェでも本を読みました。).
keyTakeaway: Duration without に; N と N; person と + action; quantity + も

sentences.japanese: 友達と三時間話しました。
sentences.english: I talked with a friend for three hours.

sentences.japanese: 三時に図書館へ行って、三時間勉強しました。
sentences.english: I went to the library at three and studied for three hours.
sentences.nuanceNote: 三時に is a clock time; 三時間 is a duration, without に in this construction.

sentences.japanese: パンと卵を買いました。友達と買い物に行きました。
sentences.english: I bought bread and eggs. I went shopping with a friend.
sentences.nuanceNote: と lists noun items in the first sentence and marks a companion in the second.

quiz.question: 昨日は図書館で友達と（　　）日本語を勉強しました。
quiz.translation: Yesterday I studied Japanese with a friend for three hours at the library.
quiz.grammarFocus: Duration of time (No に)
quiz.ruleHint: Time spans/durations (三時間, 二日間) function adverbially and do NOT take particle に.

explanations.reason: Correct! Duration counters attach directly without particle に.
Incorrect. に marks point in time (三時に), never duration of time.
Incorrect. の requires a following noun to modify.
Incorrect. で specifies a time limit for completion, not simple duration spent.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 102 (PDF p. 110). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 好き（な） / 嫌い（な） (Expressing Likes and Dislikes with が)
meaning: Like or dislike something. In the basic construction, the liked item takes が; contrast can use は.
connection: [Person] は [Item] が 好きです / 嫌いです (Adjectival predicates)
nuance: GRAMMATICAL CATEGORY: 好き and 嫌い are な-adjectives taking が for the liked/disliked item: 「私はNが好きです」. CONTRAST REPLACEMENT: When contrasting two items, は replaces が (e.g. 「野菜は好きですが、肉は嫌いです」). INTENSIFIED FORMS: 大好き and 大嫌い are preferred over とても好き. NEUTRAL FORM: 「好きでも嫌いでもないです」 (neither like nor dislike). NOUN MODIFIERS: Take な before nouns (好きな本、嫌いな食べ物).
keyTakeaway: Basic pattern: Nが好き／嫌いです. When nominalizing an action, keep its object: 本を読むのが好きです.

sentences.japanese: 私は辛い食べ物が大好きですが、甘いお菓子はあまり好きじゃありません。
sentences.english: I love spicy food, but I don't like sweet snacks very much.
sentences.literal: I spicy food like-very but, sweet snacks not-very like-not.
sentences.nuanceNote: Target of affection marked with が.

sentences.japanese: 魚が好きです。でも、肉はあまり好きじゃありません。
sentences.english: I like fish, but I do not like meat very much.
sentences.nuanceNote: が marks the liked item in the basic pattern; は can contrast another item.

sentences.japanese: 好きな食べ物は何ですか。
sentences.english: What food do you like?
sentences.nuanceNote: 好き behaves as a な-adjective before the following noun.

quiz.question: ロバートさんは日本の歴史（　　）とても好きです。
quiz.translation: Robert-san likes Japanese history very much.
quiz.grammarFocus: Object marker が with 好き
quiz.ruleHint: [Person] は [Item] が 好きです / 嫌いです (Adjectival predicates)

explanations.reason: Correct! Target of 好き requires particle が.
Incorrect. を is an English calque trap; 好き is an adjective, not a transitive verb.
Incorrect. に indicates direction/time.
Incorrect. で indicates location/means.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 128 (PDF p. 136). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ましょう / 〜ましょうか (Volitional Suggestion: Let's / Shall We?)
meaning: Proposes action enthusiastically: 〜ましょう ('Let's do it!') or offers assistance/mutual decision: 〜ましょうか ('Shall we do it? / Shall I help?').
connection: V-stem (ます-stem) + ましょう / ましょうか
nuance: TWO USES OF 〜ましょうか: 1) Suggesting mutual action ('Shall we take a break?'). 2) Offering personal assistance ('Shall I carry your bag?').
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-stem + ましょう = Let's do it! V-stem + ましょうか = Shall we? / Shall I help?

sentences.japanese: 荷物が重そうですね。手伝いましょうか。「ありがとうございます！」
sentences.english: Your luggage looks heavy. Shall I help you? 'Thank you so much!'
sentences.literal: Luggage heavy-looks. Shall-I-help? Thank-you!
sentences.nuanceNote: Offering courteous assistance to someone in need.

sentences.japanese: そろそろ帰りましょう。
sentences.english: Let's go home soon.
sentences.nuanceNote: ましょう proposes an action to undertake together.

sentences.japanese: 荷物を持ちましょうか。
sentences.english: Shall I carry your luggage?
sentences.nuanceNote: ましょうか can offer the speaker's action, not just ask what both people will do.

quiz.question: 雨が止みましたね。公園を少し（　　）ましょう。
quiz.translation: The rain has stopped, hasn't it? Let's take a walk in the park for a bit.
quiz.grammarFocus: Suggestion 〜ましょう with verb stem
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem (ます-stem) + ましょう / ましょうか

explanations.reason: Correct! 散歩する stem is 散歩し + ましょう (散歩しましょう = Let's take a walk).
Incorrect. 散歩する is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 散歩して is te-form.
Incorrect. 散歩した is past form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 128 (PDF p. 136). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: い形容詞・な形容詞
meaning: Adjective predicates, past forms and noun modification.
connection: い: 高い→高くない→高かった→高くなかった; な: 静かだ / 静かなN
nuance: CONJUGATION MATRICES: (1) い-adjectives: drop final い -> くないです (present negative), かったです (past affirmative), くなかったです (past negative). More formal negative variants use くありません and くありませんでした. (2) な-adjectives: conjugate like noun predicates -> じゃないです / じゃありません (present negative), でした (past affirmative), じゃなかったです / じゃありませんでした (past negative). IRREGULAR いい: Changes base to よ in all inflections: よくないです、よかったです、よくなかったです. Compounds like かっこいい follow this (かっこよくないです); but かわいい is a regular い-adj (かわいくないです). NOUN MODIFICATION: い-adjectives precede nouns directly (面白い映画); な-adjectives take な (きれいな写真、にぎやかな町). PEOPLE VS PLACES: 忙しい is strictly for PEOPLE. For busy/lively places, use にぎやか（な） (e.g. 「東京はにぎやかです」).
keyTakeaway: い: 高い→高くない→高かった→高くなかった; な: 静かだ / 静かなN

sentences.japanese: 昨日は寒かったです。今日は静かな店で休みます。
sentences.english: It was cold yesterday. Today I will rest in a quiet cafe.

sentences.japanese: 昨日は暑かったです。今日は暑くないです。
sentences.english: It was hot yesterday. It is not hot today.
sentences.nuanceNote: An い-adjective changes its own ending; do not use 暑いでした.

sentences.japanese: 静かな部屋が好きです。この部屋は静かです。
sentences.english: I like quiet rooms. This room is quiet.
sentences.nuanceNote: な links the adjective to a noun; it is not inserted before です.

quiz.question: 昨日の試験は全然（　　）でした。
quiz.translation: Yesterday's exam was not difficult at all.
quiz.grammarFocus: い-Adjective Past Negative (〜くなかった)
quiz.ruleHint: い-adjectives form past negative with 〜くなかった (drop い + くなかった).

explanations.reason: Correct! 難しい becomes 難しくなかった in the past negative, pairing with 昨日の and 全然.
Incorrect. 難しくない is present/non-past tense, clashing with 昨日の.
Incorrect. 難しかった is affirmative, clashing with 全然 which requires negative.
Incorrect. い-adjectives never conjugate with じゃなかった (that is for な-adjectives and nouns).

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 128 (PDF p. 136). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: Genki I: Adjective Conjugation Matrix (Lesson 5)
table.subtitle: い-adjectives vs な-adjectives across Present, Past, Affirmative, and Negative.

rows.label: い-Adjectives (True Adjectives)
cells: 高いです
高くないです / 高くありません (Drop い → くない)
高かったです (Drop い → かった)
高くなかったです / 高くありませんでした (Drop い → くなかった)
Direct attachment: 高い本 (An expensive book)
rows.note: ⚠️ THE IRREGULAR "GOOD": いい は「良い（よい）」から変化します。否定: よくないです, 過去: よかったです, 過去否定: よくなかったです。「いくない」は誤り ❌!

rows.label: な-Adjectives (Adjectival Nouns)
cells: 静かです
静かじゃないです / 静かではありません
静かでした
静かじゃなかったです / 静かではありませんでした
Requires な before noun: 静かな町 (A quiet town)
rows.note: ⚠️ LOOKS LIKE い BUT IS A な-ADJECTIVE: きれい (pretty/clean), 嫌い (きらい, disliked), 有名 (ゆうめい, famous). They take な: きれいな町, 有名な人!

title: 数え方・数量の位置
meaning: Counting objects and people.
connection: Number + appropriate counter; N を + quantity + verb
nuance: Counters depend on the object. General counters include 一つ、二つ、三つ; people include 一人、二人、三人. A quantity can follow the particle without の.
keyTakeaway: Number + appropriate counter; N を + quantity + verb

sentences.japanese: りんごを三つ買いました。
sentences.english: I bought three apples.

sentences.japanese: りんごを二つと、みかんを三つ買いました。
sentences.english: I bought two apples and three mandarins.
sentences.nuanceNote: Quantities can follow を; つ-counter readings are lexical forms such as ふたつ and みっつ.

sentences.japanese: 教室に学生が三人います。先生は一人です。
sentences.english: There are three students in the classroom. There is one teacher.
sentences.nuanceNote: 一人 is ひとり and 三人 is さんにん; learn irregular readings with the counter.

quiz.question: 郵便局で綺麗な切手を（　　）買いました。
quiz.translation: I bought five beautiful stamps at the post office.
quiz.grammarFocus: Flat object counter 〜枚 (まい)
quiz.ruleHint: Flat, thin objects like stamps (切手), paper (紙), and shirts (シャツ) are counted with 〜枚.

explanations.reason: Correct! Stamps (切手) are thin flat items counted with 〜枚 (ごまい).
Incorrect. 〜台 (だい) counts machines, computers, and vehicles.
Incorrect. 〜本 (ほん) counts long cylindrical items like pens and bottles.
Incorrect. 〜匹 (ひき) counts small animals.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 128 (PDF p. 136). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てください (Polite Request: Please Do)
meaning: Politely instructs or requests the listener to perform an action for instruction, guidance, or courtesy: 'Please do X'.
connection: V-て + ください
nuance: REGISTER WARNING: Because ください carries an underlying mild command tone ('do this for me'), saying it to high superiors (professors, boss, clients) can sound overly direct. Use 〜ていただけませんか instead.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-て + ください = Please do X. Connects strictly to te-form!

sentences.japanese: 教科書の三十五ページを開けてください。
sentences.english: Please open your textbook to page 35.
sentences.literal: Textbook's 35-page open please.
sentences.nuanceNote: Standard classroom instructional request.

sentences.japanese: もう一度、説明してください。
sentences.english: Please explain once more.
sentences.nuanceNote: The verb takes its te-form before ください. Directness depends on the relationship and situation.

sentences.japanese: ここに名前を書いてください。
sentences.english: Please write your name here.
sentences.nuanceNote: 書く changes to 書いて; attaching ください does not replace the te-form conjugation.

quiz.question: ここにあなたのお名前と電話番号を（　　）ください。
quiz.translation: Please write your name and phone number here.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-て + ください polite request
quiz.ruleHint: V-て + ください

explanations.reason: Correct! 書く connects via te-form 書いて + ください.
Incorrect. 書く is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 書き is masu-stem.
Incorrect. 書いた is past form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 146 (PDF p. 154). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てもいいですか (Asking for & Granting Permission: May I?)
meaning: Asking for permission: 'May I do X?' (〜てもいいですか). Granting permission: 'You may do X' (〜てもいいです).
connection: V-て + もいいですか / もいいです
nuance: PERMISSION FORMULA: V-て + もいいですか ('May I do X?') / もいいです ('You may do X'). GRANTING PERMISSION: Respond politely with 「はい、いいですよ」 or 「どうぞ」; never say 「*てもいいです」 isolated without the verb. Casual spoken Japanese drops も (e.g. 「これ、食べていい?」).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-て + もいいですか = May I do this? Granting: V-て + もいいですよ.

sentences.japanese: 部屋が少し暑いですね。窓を開けてもいいですか。「ええ、どうぞ。」
sentences.english: The room is a bit hot, isn't it? May I open the window? 'Yes, please go ahead.'
sentences.literal: Room slightly hot is. Window open-even-if good is question? Yes, please.
sentences.nuanceNote: Courteous permission query before altering shared environment.

sentences.japanese: 窓を開けてもいいですか。
sentences.english: May I open the window?
sentences.nuanceNote: てもいいですか asks whether the action is permitted.

sentences.japanese: ここで食べてもいいです。でも、たばこを吸ってはいけません。
sentences.english: You may eat here, but you must not smoke.
sentences.nuanceNote: てもいい grants permission; てはいけない prohibits an action. They are different constructions.

quiz.question: このペンを少しの間、（　　）てもいいですか。
quiz.translation: May I borrow this pen for a brief moment?
quiz.grammarFocus: Permission formula 〜てもいいですか
quiz.ruleHint: V-て + もいいですか / もいいです

explanations.reason: Correct! 借りる is a Ru-verb: stem 借り + てもいいですか (借りてもいいですか).
Incorrect. 借る is an archaic form.
The dictionary form does not attach directly to てもいい; use 借りてもいい.
Incorrect. 借りた is past form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 146 (PDF p. 154). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜から (Stating Reasons / Because - Clause Linker)
meaning: States a subjective explanation or cause: 'Because of X, Y happens' or 'Y happens because of X'.
connection: Sentence 1 (Reason) + から、 Sentence 2 (Conclusion)
nuance: から follows a reason and introduces its consequence. Nouns and な-adjectives take だから in plain non-past affirmative statements, or ですから politely. Verbs and い-adjectives retain their appropriate plain or polite endings. It can introduce requests and intentions, and it can also give factual reasons; subjective is a tendency in the contrast with ので, not a requirement.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Reason] から、[Result]. Unlike English, the reason comes FIRST!

sentences.japanese: 今日は大事なテストがありますから、早く寝ます。
sentences.english: Because I have an important test today, I will go to bed early.
sentences.literal: Today important test have because, early sleep.
sentences.nuanceNote: Reason precedes the resulting decision.

sentences.japanese: 明日は早く起きるから、もう寝ます。
sentences.english: I will go to bed now because I am getting up early tomorrow.
sentences.nuanceNote: A plain verb predicate can precede から.

sentences.japanese: 今日は休みですから、会社へ行きません。
sentences.english: I am not going to work because today is a day off.
sentences.nuanceNote: A polite noun predicate uses ですから; plain speech uses 休みだから.

quiz.question: 明日は朝早く起きます（　　）、今夜はテレビを見ません。
quiz.translation: Because I will wake up early tomorrow morning, I won't watch television tonight.
quiz.grammarFocus: Causal clause linker から
quiz.ruleHint: Sentence 1 (Reason) + から、 Sentence 2 (Conclusion)

explanations.reason: Correct! から links the reason for abstaining from TV.
Incorrect. まで means 'until'.
Incorrect. より indicates comparison.
Incorrect. ほど indicates degree or proportion.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 146 (PDF p. 154). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: て形・順序・禁止
meaning: Connect actions and state prohibitions.
connection: Vて、V; Vてはいけない
nuance: TE-FORM CONJUGATION PARADIGM: (1) Ru-verbs: drop る + て (食べて、起きて). (2) U-verbs by ending: [う・つ・る] -> って (会って、待って、帰って); [む・ぶ・ぬ] -> んで (飲んで、遊んで、死んで); [く] -> いて (書いて), CRITICAL EXCEPTION: 行く -> 行って (NOT いいて ❌!); [ぐ] -> いで (泳いで); [す] -> して (話して). (3) Irregulars: する->して、来る->来て. SEQUENCE OF ACTIONS: Te-form links sequential actions ('I did A, then B'); particle と connects only nouns, never verbs! Final verb establishes tense for whole sentence. PROHIBITION: V-てはいけません expresses strong authoritative prohibition ('You must not do X') used in formal rules and regulations.
keyTakeaway: Vて、V; Vてはいけない

sentences.japanese: 朝ご飯を食べて、学校に行きます。ここで走ってはいけません。
sentences.english: I eat breakfast and go to school. You must not run here.

sentences.japanese: 朝ご飯を食べて、歯を磨いて、家を出ました。
sentences.english: I ate breakfast, brushed my teeth, and left home.
sentences.nuanceNote: Te-forms connect actions; the final predicate supplies the past tense for the sequence.

sentences.japanese: 図書館で大きな声で話してはいけません。
sentences.english: You must not speak loudly in the library.
sentences.nuanceNote: てはいけない states a prohibition, rather than merely recommending against an action.

sentences.japanese: 本を読んで、音楽を聞いて、少し休みました。
sentences.english: I read a book, listened to music, and rested a little.
sentences.nuanceNote: 読む→読んで, 聞く→聞いて. The te-form ending depends on the verb group and final sound.

sentences.japanese: すみませんが、窓を開けてください。
sentences.english: Excuse me, but please open the window.
sentences.nuanceNote: 開ける is Ru-verb: stem 開け + て + ください.

sentences.japanese: 朝起きて、顔を洗って、朝ご飯を食べました。
sentences.english: I woke up in the morning, washed my face, and ate breakfast.
sentences.nuanceNote: The te-form links successive actions in chronological order.

sentences.japanese: 大事な話ですから、静かに聞いてください。
sentences.english: Because this is an important matter, please listen quietly.
sentences.useLabel: Polite request with ください
sentences.nuanceNote: V-て + ください forms a standard polite request.

quiz.question: 図書館の中では大きな声で（　　）はいけません。
quiz.translation: You must not speak in a loud voice inside the library.
quiz.grammarFocus: Prohibition 〜てはいけません
quiz.ruleHint: Verb て-form + はいけません expresses strict prohibition ('must not do').

explanations.reason: Correct! Prohibition attaches to verb te-form: 話して + はいけません.
Incorrect. Dictionary form cannot attach directly to はいけません.
Incorrect. Masu-stem cannot attach directly to はいけません.
Incorrect. Ta-form cannot attach to はいけません.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 146 (PDF p. 154). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: The Te-Form (て形) Conjugation Matrix
table.subtitle: The foundational gateway for ~ている, ~てから, ~てもいい, ~てはいけない, and ~てしまう.

rows.label: Group 1: う・つ・る
cells: 買う, 待つ, 取る
買って, 待って, 取って
買った, 待った, 取った
う・つ・る → って / った (促音便: 小さい「っ」+ て)
rows.note: Classic rhythm: "u, tsu, ru" becomes "tte"

rows.label: Group 1: む・ぶ・ぬ
cells: 飲む, 遊ぶ, 死ぬ
飲んで, 遊んで, 死んで
飲んだ, 遊んだ, 死んだ
む・ぶ・ぬ → んで / んだ (撥音便: 濁音の「で」)
rows.note: Voiced consonants always take で, not て.

rows.label: Group 1: く / ぐ
cells: 書く, 泳ぐ
書いて, 泳いで
書いた, 泳いだ
く → いて, ぐ → いで (イ音便: い + て/で)
rows.note: CRITICAL EXCEPTION: 行く は「いいて」にならず、「行って・行った」と促音便になります。

rows.label: Group 1: す
cells: 話す, 出す
話して, 出して
話した, 出した
す → して / した
rows.note: Behaves cleanly like polite shimasu.

rows.label: Group 2: る (一段動詞)
cells: 食べる, 見る, 起きる
食べて, 見て, 起きて
食べた, 見た, 起きた
る を取って「て・た」を付ける
rows.note: Vowel before る is usually e or i (たべ・み).

rows.label: Group 3: Irregular (変格動詞)
cells: する, 来る
して, 来て
した, 来た
不規則活用: 来る は「来て（きて）・来た（きた）」と読みが変化します。
rows.note: Notice 来る changes reading to 「き」 in て/た form: 来て（きて）, 来た（きた）.

title: 身体の描写 (Describing People's Physical Attributes: 目が大きいです)
meaning: Formula for describing a person's physical features: [Person] は [Body Part] が [Adjective] です ('As for X, their eyes are big').
connection: [Person] は + [Body Part] が + [Adjective] です
nuance: NATURAL PHYSICAL FORMULA: 「[Person] は [Body Part] が [Adjective] です」 is the standard idiom (e.g. 「トムさんは髪が長いです」 - As for Tom, his hair is long). IDIOMATIC COLLOCATIONS: 背が高い (tall), 背が低い (short), 頭がいい (smart/bright), 目がいい/悪い (good/poor eyesight).
keyTakeaway: Personは body-partが adjective is a common way to describe someone. A possessive subject such as メアリーさんの髪は長いです is also grammatical; the two sentences frame the topic differently.

sentences.japanese: 私の妹は目が大きくて、髪が長いです。
sentences.english: My younger sister has big eyes and long hair.
sentences.literal: My younger-sister eyes big-and, hair long-is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Natural Japanese body description framing.

sentences.japanese: 妹は髪が長いです。
sentences.english: My younger sister has long hair.
sentences.nuanceNote: 妹 is the topic; 髪 is the subject of the adjective predicate.

sentences.japanese: 妹の髪は長いです。
sentences.english: My younger sister's hair is long.
sentences.nuanceNote: This is also grammatical. It makes the hair, rather than the person, the explicit topic.

quiz.question: 田中さんは背が（　　）です。
quiz.translation: Tanaka is tall.
quiz.grammarFocus: Physical attribute marker が (背が高い)
quiz.ruleHint: [Person] は + [Body Part] が + [Adjective] です

explanations.reason: 高い is the adjective predicate.
高く is a connective/adverbial form.
高さ means height and would change the construction.
高 alone is not the adjective predicate.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 166 (PDF p. 174). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 形容詞・名詞の「て形」 (Connecting Adjectives & Nouns: 〜くて / 〜で)
meaning: Links multiple qualities or attributes: い-adjectives change final い to くて; な-adjectives and nouns take で.
connection: い-adj (drop い) + くて | な-adj stem + で | Noun + で
nuance: THE II/YOI TE-FORM: いい (good) drops its irregular root and conjugates as よくて (NOT いくて ❌)! な-adjectives take で, exactly like nouns.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: い-adj = 〜くて (いい→よくて). な-adj / Noun = 〜で.

sentences.japanese: この部屋は広くて明るくて、とても静かです。
sentences.english: This room is spacious, bright, and very quiet.
sentences.literal: This room spacious-and bright-and, very quiet-is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Chaining two い-adjectives via くて into a terminal な-adjective.

sentences.japanese: この店は安くて、おいしいです。
sentences.english: This restaurant is cheap and serves tasty food.
sentences.nuanceNote: The first い-adjective changes to くて.

sentences.japanese: 山田さんは親切で、日本語の先生です。
sentences.english: Yamada is kind and is a Japanese-language teacher.
sentences.nuanceNote: で connects the な-adjective predicate to another description.

quiz.question: あのカフェはコーヒーが（　　）、値段も安いです。
quiz.translation: That cafe's coffee is delicious, and the price is also cheap.
quiz.grammarFocus: い-adjective te-form 〜くて
quiz.ruleHint: い-adj (drop い) + くて | な-adj stem + で | Noun + で

explanations.reason: Correct! おいしい drops い + くて = おいしくて.
Incorrect. おいしいで incorrectly applies noun/na-adj で to an い-adj.
Incorrect. おいしくで is ungrammatical.
おいしいくて incorrectly retains the final い; the correct connective form is おいしくて.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 166 (PDF p. 174). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: V-stem + に行く / に来る (Purpose of Movement: Going to Do)
meaning: Expresses the specific purpose of movement: going (行く), coming (来る), or returning (帰る) in order to perform an action.
connection: V-stem (ます-stem) + に + 行く / 来る / 帰る | Activity Noun + に + 行く
nuance: VERB STEM BEFORE に: Drop ます and append に directly: 食べます → 食べに行く, 買いに行きます. If using an activity noun (買い物, 散歩), attach に directly: 買い物に行く.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Masu-stem] に行く = Going to DO X. Purpose particle is STRICTLY に!

sentences.japanese: デパートへ友達の誕生日プレゼントを買いに行きました。
sentences.english: I went to the department store to buy a birthday present for my friend.
sentences.literal: Department-store friend's birthday present buy-in-order-to went.
sentences.nuanceNote: 買う (stem 買い) + に行きました.

sentences.japanese: 図書館へ本を借りに行きます。
sentences.english: I am going to the library to borrow a book.
sentences.nuanceNote: 借り is the polite stem before purpose に; the destination is separately marked with へ.

sentences.japanese: 友達と買い物に行きました。
sentences.english: I went shopping with a friend.
sentences.nuanceNote: An activity noun can attach directly to に; no unnecessary する is inserted.

quiz.question: 週末は図書館へ本を（　　）に行きます。
quiz.translation: On weekends I go to the library to return books.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-stem + に行く purpose of movement
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem (ます-stem) + に + 行く / 来る / 帰る | Activity Noun + に + 行く

explanations.reason: Correct! 返す (to return an item) stem is 返し + に行きます.
Incorrect. 返す is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 返して is te-form.
Incorrect. 返した is past form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 166 (PDF p. 174). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ている：動作・結果
meaning: An ongoing action or a continuing resulting state.
connection: Vて + いる
nuance: TWO SEMANTIC CLASSES: (1) Activity verbs describe action in progress (勉強しています) or occupation/habit (英語を教えています). (2) Change verbs describe a continuing resultant state: 結婚しています (is married, NOT getting married), 座っています (is seated), 知っています (knows), 持っています (owns), 太っています (overweight), 住んでいます (resides in). MOVEMENT RESULT: 行っています (has gone to and is there) and 来ています (has arrived/is visiting), NOT ongoing motion! NEGATIVE FORM OF SHIRU: Strictly 知りません (NEVER 知っていません ❌!). SOCIAL ETIQUETTE: In polite conversation when you lack information, say 「わかりません」; 「知りません」 can sound blunt and dismissive ('I don't know and don't care').
keyTakeaway: Vて + いる

sentences.japanese: 妹は今勉強しています。兄は大阪に住んでいます。
sentences.english: My younger sister is studying now. My older brother lives in Osaka.

sentences.japanese: 今、母は電話で話しています。
sentences.english: My mother is talking on the phone now.
sentences.nuanceNote: 話している describes an ongoing activity.

sentences.japanese: 姉は結婚しています。
sentences.english: My older sister is married.
sentences.nuanceNote: 結婚している normally describes the state resulting from marriage, not an ongoing wedding ceremony.

sentences.japanese: 毎週、近くのプールで泳いでいます。
sentences.english: I swim at a nearby pool every week.
sentences.nuanceNote: ている can also describe a recurring activity, depending on the time expression and context.

sentences.japanese: 姉は東京のIT企業に勤めています。
sentences.english: My older sister is employed at an IT company in Tokyo.
sentences.nuanceNote: 勤めている indicates ongoing occupational employment state.

sentences.japanese: 今、部屋で日本語の文法を勉強しています。
sentences.english: Right now, I am studying Japanese grammar in my room.
sentences.nuanceNote: Activity verbs in 〜ている express an action currently in active progress.

sentences.japanese: 田中さんは窓の近くの席に座っています。
sentences.english: Tanaka-san is seated in the chair near the window.
sentences.nuanceNote: Instantaneous change verbs (座る、結婚する、知る) in 〜ている express a lasting resultant state.

quiz.question: 姉は三年前に結婚して、今は東京に（　　）。
quiz.translation: My older sister got married three years ago, and now lives in Tokyo.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜ている (Resultant State of Living)
quiz.ruleHint: 住む is a verb of instantaneous change; residing in a place is expressed as 住んでいる.

explanations.reason: Correct! Residence is a continuous state resulting from moving: 住んでいます.
Incorrect. 住みます denotes future intention to live, not current residence.
Incorrect. 〜てある is used with transitive verbs for deliberate preparations.
Incorrect. 住み始めます denotes initiating residence in the future.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 166 (PDF p. 174). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 人数を数える
meaning: Counting people using irregular Japanese counters: 一人（ひとり）, 二人（ふたり）, and 四人（よにん）.
connection: 一人（ひとり）、二人（ふたり）、三人（さんにん）、何人（なんにん）
nuance: PEOPLE COUNTER IRREGULARITIES: 一人 (ひとり), 二人 (ふたり), and 四人 (よにん - strictly よにん; saying しにん ❌ or よんにん ❌ is an error). From 3 onwards, regular numeral + にん: 三人 (さんにん), 五人 (ごにん), etc. Interrogative: 何人 (なんにん).
keyTakeaway: 一人（ひとり）、二人（ふたり）、三人（さんにん）、何人（なんにん）

sentences.japanese: 教室に学生が四人います。
sentences.english: There are four students in the classroom.

sentences.japanese: 学生が二人来ました。先生は一人です。
sentences.english: Two students came. There is one teacher.
sentences.nuanceNote: 二人 is ふたり and 一人 is ひとり; these are special person-counter readings.

sentences.japanese: 何人来ますか。四人来ます。
sentences.english: How many people are coming? Four.
sentences.nuanceNote: 何人 is なんにん and 四人 is よにん. The count can follow the particle rather than requiring の.

quiz.question: 昨日のパーティーには留学生が（　　）来ました。
quiz.translation: Four international students came to yesterday's party.
quiz.grammarFocus: People Counter 四人 (よにん)
quiz.ruleHint: Four people is uniquely pronounced よにん (never よんにん or しにん).

explanations.reason: Correct! Four people is pronounced with phonological reduction as よにん.
Incorrect. よんにん is an erroneous phonological pronunciation.
Incorrect. しにん sounds like 'dead person' (死人) and is strictly avoided.
Incorrect. よっつ counts inanimate objects, never people.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 166 (PDF p. 174). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ないでください (Negative Request: Please Do Not)
meaning: Politely requests or instructs someone to refrain from an action: 'Please do not do X'.
connection: V-ない + でください
nuance: NEGATIVE POLITE REQUEST: Formed from the plain negative ない-form + でください. Very common on signs, exams, and courteous instructions (忘れないでください).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-ない + でください = Please don't do X! (Drop nothing from ない).

sentences.japanese: 図書館の中では大声で話さないでください。
sentences.english: Please do not speak in a loud voice inside the library.
sentences.literal: Library inside loud-voice-in speak-not-please.

tokens.reading: はなさないでください

sentences.nuanceNote: 話す negative 話さない + でください.

sentences.japanese: ここで写真を撮らないでください。
sentences.english: Please do not take photographs here.
sentences.nuanceNote: 撮る is an u-verb, so the negative is 撮らない before でください.

sentences.japanese: 心配しないでください。
sentences.english: Please do not worry.
sentences.nuanceNote: する becomes しない; the phrase requests that the action not occur.

quiz.question: まだテスト中ですから、教室から（　　）ないでください。
quiz.translation: Since the test is still ongoing, please do not leave the classroom.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-ない + でください negative request
quiz.ruleHint: V-ない + でください

explanations.reason: Correct! 出る (Ru-verb) negative is 出ない + でください (出ないでください).
Incorrect. 出るない is false conjugation.
Incorrect. 出て is te-form.
Incorrect. 出な is ungrammatical.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 186 (PDF p. 194). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 動詞の「の」名詞化 (Nominalizing Verbs with の: のが好き / 上手 / 下手)
meaning: Turns an action verb into a noun phrase using の, enabling evaluations of preference or skill: V-plain + のが好き / 上手 / 下手.
connection: V-辞書形 + のが [好き / 嫌い / 上手 / 下手 / 得意 / 苦手] です
nuance: Use の to turn an action clause into a noun-like unit: 本を読むのが好きです. The object particle inside the clause remains を. A dictionary-form clause is usual when describing a general preference or skill. This is not a universal prohibition against が following a verb: conjunction が can follow a predicate to mean but in a different construction.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Verb-Dictionary] + のが + 好き / 上手 / 下手! The particle の acts as 'the act of'.

sentences.japanese: 私はギターを弾くのが大好きですが、歌を歌うのはあまり上手ではありません。
sentences.english: I love playing the guitar, but I am not very good at singing songs.
sentences.literal: I guitar play-nominalizer like-very but, songs sing-nominalizer not-very good is-not.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nominalizing musical instruments and singing.

sentences.japanese: 本を読むのが好きです。
sentences.english: I like reading books.
sentences.useLabel: An activity as the liked thing
sentences.nuanceNote: の nominalizes the full clause 本を読む; を remains inside that clause.

sentences.japanese: 姉は料理を作るのが上手です。
sentences.english: My older sister is good at cooking.
sentences.nuanceNote: The whole nominalized activity takes が before the skill adjective.

quiz.question: 母は料理を（　　）のがとても上手です。
quiz.translation: My mother is very good at cooking meals.
quiz.grammarFocus: Nominalization V-辞書形 + の
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 + のが [好き / 嫌い / 上手 / 下手 / 得意 / 苦手] です

explanations.reason: Correct! V-辞書形 作る connects to nominalizer の (作るのが上手).
Incorrect. 作って is te-form.
Incorrect. 作り is masu-stem.
Incorrect. 作った is past form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 186 (PDF p. 194). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 普通形・と思う・と言う
meaning: Plain forms in conversation and quotation.
connection: Plain clause + と思う / と言う; noun/な-adjective + だと
nuance: SHORT FORMS CONJUGATION: (1) Ru-verbs: drop る + ない (食べない). (2) U-verbs: drop -u + anai (書かない); verbs ending in う take わない (会う→会わない, 買う→買わない! NOT ああない ❌). (3) Irregulars: する→しない, 来る (くる)→こない. EXCEPTION: ある is completely replaced by ない! (4) Nouns and な-adjectives: affirmative present takes だ (学生だ, 元気だ). QUOTATION と思う / と言う: Noun / な-adj affirmative strictly requires だ before と (「学生だと思います」, 「元気だと思います」; omitting だ is ungrammatical). THOUGHT NEGATION CONVENTION: In Japanese, negating the inner clause (「〜ないと思います」 - I think X is not so) is far more natural than negating omou itself.
keyTakeaway: Plain clause + と思う / と言う; noun/な-adjective + だと

sentences.japanese: 明日は雨だと思います。友達もそう言っていました。
sentences.english: I think it will rain tomorrow. My friend said so too.

sentences.japanese: 明日は雨が降ると思います。
sentences.english: I think it will rain tomorrow.
sentences.nuanceNote: The clause before と uses an appropriate plain predicate, even though the final 思います is polite.

sentences.japanese: この町は便利だと思います。
sentences.english: I think this town is convenient.
sentences.nuanceNote: A non-past affirmative な-adjective retains だ before quotation と.

sentences.japanese: 田中さんは、明日は来ないと言っていました。
sentences.english: Tanaka said that they would not come tomorrow.
sentences.nuanceNote: The negative plain clause is the content of 言う, not a negative of the reporting verb itself.

quiz.question: 明日は雨が（　　）と思います。
quiz.translation: I think it will rain tomorrow.
quiz.grammarFocus: Quotation / Belief with 〜と思う (Plain form)
quiz.ruleHint: 〜と思う quotes a thought in plain (short) form: Verb 辞書形 / た形 / ない形 + と思う.

explanations.reason: Correct! 〜と思う takes short/plain forms (降る + と思います).
Incorrect. Polite forms like 降ります do not precede と思います in standard speech.
Incorrect. Te-form cannot attach directly to と思います.
Incorrect. Stem form cannot attach directly to と思います.

table.subtitle: The essential informal register for ~と思う, ~と言っていた, and casual conversation.

rows.label: Verbs (動詞)

ない形 (Nai-form): 食べない / 行かない (Note: ある → ない)
た形 (Ta-form): 食べた / 行った
なかった形: 食べなかった / 行かなかった
rows.note: Conjugates like the Te-form (て → た, で → だ).

rows.label: い-Adjectives

Drop です: かわいくない / 高くない
Drop です: かわいかった / 高かった
Drop です: かわいくなかった / 高くなかった
rows.note: Plain form of い-adjectives simply drops です!

rows.label: な-Adjectives & Nouns
cells: だ (Attach だ): 静かだ / 学生だ
じゃない: 静かじゃない / 学生じゃない
だった: 静かだった / 学生だった
じゃなかった: 静かじゃなかった / 学生じゃなかった
rows.note: CRITICAL TRAP: In affirmative present, です becomes だ! (e.g. 日本人だと思う).

title: が・何か・何も
meaning: Identify a subject, something or nothing.
connection: Question-word subject + が; 何か; 何も + negative
nuance: SUBJECT MARKER が: When a question word (だれ, 何, どのN, どれ) is the grammatical subject, it strictly takes が, NEVER は (e.g. 「だれが沖縄に行きましたか」). The reply identifying the specific subject also takes が (「ロバートさんが行きました」). INDEFINITE PRONOUNS: 何か (something / anything in questions) and 何も + negative (not anything / nothing). The particles は, が, and を are routinely omitted after 何か and 何も (e.g. 「何か食べましたか」, 「何も食べませんでした」).
keyTakeaway: Question-word subject + が; 何か; 何も + negative

sentences.japanese: だれが来ますか。私は何も知りません。
sentences.english: Who is coming? I do not know anything.

sentences.japanese: 誰が来ますか。山田さんが来ます。
sentences.english: Who is coming? Yamada is.
sentences.nuanceNote: が identifies the unknown/requested person in this question-answer pair.

sentences.japanese: 何か食べましたか。いいえ、何も食べていません。
sentences.english: Did you eat anything? No, I have not eaten anything.
sentences.nuanceNote: 何か gives an unspecified thing; 何も with a negative means nothing.

quiz.question: お腹が痛かったので、今朝は（　　）食べませんでした。
quiz.translation: Because my stomach hurt, I didn't eat anything this morning.
quiz.grammarFocus: 何も + Negative (Nothing / Not anything)
quiz.ruleHint: 何か takes affirmative sentences ('something'); 何も takes negative predicates ('not anything').

explanations.reason: Correct! 何も pairs with negative verbs (食べませんでした) to mean 'nothing at all'.
Incorrect. 何か means 'something' and pairs with affirmative predicates.
Incorrect. 何が is a question word subject marker ('what is...').
Incorrect. 何を asks 'what did you eat?' in question sentences.

なかった形: 食べなかった / 行かなかった
