title: もう〜ました vs まだ〜ていません (Already Done vs Have Not Yet Done)
meaning: もう〜ました (Action has already been completed). まだ〜ていません (Action has not yet taken place; still in uncompleted state).
connection: もう + Vました; for not yet completed: まだ + Vていません
nuance: ALREADY VS NOT YET: もう + V-ました describes an action already completed. まだ + V-ていません describes an action not yet completed at present. CRITICAL PITFALL: To say you haven't done something yet, you CANNOT say 「まだV-ませんでした」 ❌! Past negative (V-ませんでした) is strictly confined to finished, closed historical timeframes (e.g. 「きのうは宿題をしませんでした」). When stating that an action remains undone at the present moment, Japanese strictly requires 「まだV-ていません」 (e.g. 「まだ宿題をしていません」).
keyTakeaway: For a not-yet-completed event at the present reference point, use まだVていません. Past negation has other uses in a past narrative; it does not inherently mean the speaker never intended to act.

sentences.japanese: 宿題はもう終わりましたか。「いいえ、まだ終わっていません。」
sentences.english: Have you finished your homework already? 'No, I have not finished it yet.'
sentences.literal: Homework already finished? No, still finished-state-not.

tokens.word: まだ終わっていません
tokens.reading: まだおわっていません

sentences.nuanceNote: Canonical pairing of もう with past vs まだ with progressive negative.

sentences.japanese: 宿題はもう終わりましたか。はい、もう終わりました。
sentences.english: Have you finished your homework yet? Yes, I have already finished.
sentences.nuanceNote: もう asks about or confirms completion by the current reference time.

sentences.japanese: 宿題はまだ終わっていません。
sentences.english: I have not finished my homework yet.
sentences.nuanceNote: まだ with a negative ている predicate presents the not-yet-completed state, rather than simply a past non-event.

quiz.question: 昼ご飯はもう食べましたか。「いいえ、まだ（　　）。」
quiz.translation: Did you eat lunch already? 'No, I haven't eaten yet.'
quiz.grammarFocus: まだ + V-ていません (Not yet)
quiz.ruleHint: もう + Vました; for not yet completed: まだ + Vていません

explanations.reason: Correct! まだ takes progressive negative 食べていません ('have not eaten yet').
食べませんでした reports a past non-event; it does not express the intended current not-yet-completed state in this answer.
食べません can express a habit or future decision not to eat; here the intended answer is have not eaten yet.
Incorrect. 食べないでした is ungrammatical.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 210 (PDF p. 218). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 過去の普通形・名詞修飾
meaning: Plain past forms and clauses before nouns.
connection: Vた / Vなかった; plain clause + N
nuance: PAST SHORT FORMS: (1) Verbs: replace て/で with た/だ (食べた、飲んだ、行った、した、きた); negative replaces ない with なかった (食べなかった、行かなかった). (2) い-adjectives: かった / くなかった. (3) な-adjectives and Nouns: だった / じゃなかった (in casual conversation, past だった is preserved, unlike present だ). NOUN MODIFICATION (RELATIVE CLAUSES): Modifying clauses strictly precede nouns without relative pronouns (no who/which/that); the verb inside must be in the short form (e.g. 「あそこで本を読んでいる人」, 「きのう買った本」). NO TENSE BACKSHIFT IN QUOTES: In reported speech (〜と言っていました), Japanese preserves the original utterance tense without English sequence-of-tense shift.
keyTakeaway: Vた / Vなかった; plain clause + N

sentences.japanese: 昨日買った本は面白かったです。
sentences.english: The book I bought yesterday was interesting.

sentences.japanese: 昨日の試験は難しかったと思います。
sentences.english: I think yesterday's exam was difficult.
sentences.useLabel: Past plain form inside a thought
sentences.nuanceNote: The adjective's plain past is inside the quoted content; 思います remains polite and non-past.

sentences.japanese: 昨日買った本を読みました。
sentences.english: I read the book I bought yesterday.
sentences.nuanceNote: 昨日買った modifies 本 directly; do not insert an English-style relative pronoun or unnecessary の.

quiz.question: あそこで眼鏡を（　　）人は、私の日本語の先生です。
quiz.translation: The person wearing glasses over there is my Japanese teacher.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun Modification with Relative Clause (〜ている人)
quiz.ruleHint: Relative clauses modify nouns using plain forms; state of wearing accessories uses 〜ている.

explanations.reason: Correct! Wearing glasses is a continuous state modifying 人: かけている人.
Incorrect. Polite forms (ます) cannot modify a noun in a relative clause.
Incorrect. かけた人 denotes having put on in the past rather than the ongoing state visible over there.
Incorrect. Te-form cannot directly modify a noun.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 210 (PDF p. 218). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜つもりだ / つもりです (Stated Personal Intention: Plan To)
meaning: States a conscious, determined personal intention or plan: 'I intend to / I plan to do X'.
connection: V-辞書形 + つもりだ / つもりです | V-ない形 + つもりだ / つもりです | V-過去形 + つもりでした
nuance: 〜つもりだ / つもりです follows verbs in the present tense short form to describe a conscious personal intention or plan for the future. For negative intentions, attach つもり to the negative short form: V-ない + つもりです (e.g. 明日は大学に来ないつもりです: I plan not to come to school tomorrow; preferred standard pattern), or use V-る + つもりはありません to express a strong lack of intention. Use the past tense 〜つもりでした to describe an original intention that did not materialize (e.g. お寺に行くつもりでしたが、行きませんでした: We planned to visit a temple, but we didn't). SOCIAL RESTRICTION: Asking superiors 〜つもりですか can sound confrontational (demanding their intent); describe third-party intentions with caution (using hearsay or evidential markers like 〜と言っていました or 〜ようです).
keyTakeaway: V-辞書形 + つもりです (plan to do). V-ない + つもりです (plan not to do). 〜つもりでした (intended to do, but plan changed). Never interrogate superiors with 〜つもりですか.

sentences.japanese: 大学を卒業したら、日本の大学院に進学するつもりです。
sentences.english: Upon graduating from college, I intend to advance to graduate school in Japan.
sentences.literal: College graduate-when, Japan's grad-school advance intend.

tokens.meaning: intend to advance to higher education
tokens.reading: しんがくするつもりです

sentences.nuanceNote: Stating personal academic career intent.

sentences.japanese: 来年、日本へ留学するつもりです。
sentences.english: I intend to study abroad in Japan next year.
sentences.nuanceNote: Dictionary verb + つもり states an intention, not a guarantee that the plan will happen.

sentences.japanese: 今日は買わないつもりです。
sentences.english: I intend not to buy it today.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vないつもり expresses an intention not to act. Compare 買うつもりはない, which denies having an intention to buy.

quiz.question: 今年の夏休みは、どこへも旅行に（　　）つもりです。家で勉強します。
quiz.translation: This summer vacation, I intend not to travel anywhere. I will study at home.
quiz.grammarFocus: Negative intention V-ない + つもりだ
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 + つもりです (Affirmative plan) | V-ない + つもりです / つもりはありません (Negative plan)

explanations.reason: Correct! Negative intention connects via ない-form: 行かないつもりです.
Incorrect. 行く indicates affirmative intent to travel.
Incorrect. 行かないで is te-form.
Incorrect. 行った is past form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 230 (PDF p. 238). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 形容詞 + なる (Expressing Change of State: To Become)
meaning: Describes a natural or progressive change of state: 'to become [adjective]' (growing warm, becoming quiet, turning into an adult).
connection: い-adj (drop い) + くなる | な-adj stem + になる | Noun + になる
nuance: The verb なる means 'to become', indicating a transition or change of state over time. Conjugation rules: (1) い-adjectives: drop final 〜い and add 〜くなる (暖かい → 暖かくなる, 寒い → 寒くなる, いい → よくなる). EXPLICIT TEXTBOOK TRAP: Never use な-adj pattern for い-adj (e.g. *暖かになる is strictly ungrammatical). (2) な-adjectives: drop 〜な and add 〜になる (静か[な] → 静かになる, 元気[な] → 元気になる). (3) Nouns: add 〜になる directly (医者になる: become a doctor; 二十歳になる: turn 20). CHANGE DYNAMICS: Describes either an absolute change (暖かくなりました = it has become warm, no longer cold) or a relative change when paired with より (前より日本語が上手になりました = Mary has become better at Japanese than before).
keyTakeaway: い-adj (drop い) + くなる (暖かくなる; いい→よくなる). な-adj + になる (静かになる). Noun + になる (医者になる). Never *暖かになる.

sentences.japanese: 春になって、だんだん暖かくなってきましたね。
sentences.english: Spring has arrived, and it has gradually become warm, hasn't it?
sentences.literal: Spring become, gradually warm became-came.

tokens.word: 暖かくなってきました
tokens.reading: あたたかくなってきました

sentences.nuanceNote: Noun + になる and い-adj + くなる.

sentences.japanese: 薬を飲んで、気分がよくなりました。
sentences.english: After taking medicine, I felt better.
sentences.nuanceNote: いい uses the よい stem, giving よくなる.

sentences.japanese: 姉は先生になりました。この町も便利になりました。
sentences.english: My older sister became a teacher. This town has also become convenient.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nouns and な-adjectives take に before なる, unlike い-adjectives with く.

quiz.question: 薬を飲んだら、痛みがだいぶ（　　）なりました。
quiz.translation: After taking the medicine, the pain became considerably better.
quiz.grammarFocus: Change of state with いい (よくなる)
quiz.ruleHint: い-adj (drop い) + くなる | な-adj stem + になる | Noun + になる

explanations.reason: Correct! いい changes through root よい to become adverbial よく + なりました.
Incorrect. いいに is ungrammatical; い-adjectives take く.
Incorrect. よくに is double adverbial marking.
Incorrect. いいく is invalid root conjugation.

title: 比較・一番
meaning: Compare two or several items.
connection: Aのほうが Bより [Property] です | AとBとどちらが [Property] ですか | [Category]の中で [Item]が一番 [Property] です
nuance: Japanese has no inflectional comparative suffixes like '-er' or '-est'; comparisons are framed entirely with particles. (1) Comparison between Two Items: 'A のほうが B より [Property] です' (A is more [Property] than B). Word order variation: 'B より A のほうが [Property] です' is common in real life; track particles carefully—のほうが always marks the superior item, and より always marks the benchmark/standard. (2) Question between Two Items: 'A と B と どちら (どっち) が [Property] ですか' (Between A and B, which is more [Property]?). (3) Superlatives among Three or More Items: '[Category] の中で A が 一番 [Property] です' (Among [Category], A is the most [Property]). (4) Question for Three or More Items: '[Category] の中で {だれ / どこ / 何 / どれ} が 一番 [Property] ですか'. CRITICAL BAN: The words どちら and のほう are STRICTLY PROHIBITED in statements and questions comparing three or more items. Use open question words instead (どれ for distinct listed choices, 何 for general categories).
keyTakeaway: Two items: Aのほうが Bより [Property] (Q: AとBとどちらが). Three+ items: [Category]の中で Aが一番 [Property] (Q: Categoryの中で 何/だれ/どこ/どれ が一番). NEVER use どちら for 3+ items.

sentences.japanese: 電車のほうがバスより速いです。
sentences.english: The train is faster than the bus.

sentences.japanese: この三つの中で、どれが一番安いですか。
sentences.english: Which of these three is the cheapest?
sentences.nuanceNote: The group is explicitly limited by この三つの中で; 一番 need not mean the best in the whole world.

quiz.question: 季節の中で、春と秋とどちらの（　　）好きですか。
quiz.translation: Between spring and autumn, which one do you like better?
quiz.grammarFocus: Comparison: A と B とどちらのほうが〜か
quiz.ruleHint: When comparing two alternatives, どちらのほうが asks 'which side is more...'.

explanations.reason: Correct! どちらのほうが is the fixed comparative formula for choosing between two items.
Incorrect. より marks the baseline of comparison ('than'), not the selected side.
Incorrect. から means 'from' or 'because'.
Incorrect. ほど is used in negative comparison ('not as much as').

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 230 (PDF p. 238). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 名詞の代わりの「の」
meaning: Replace an understood noun.
connection: い-adj + の | な-adj + なの | Noun + の
nuance: When a noun follows an adjective or another noun, and its referent is clear from context, the indefinite noun の ('one') replaces it to avoid repetition. Conjugation rules: (1) い-adjective + の: 赤いセーター → 赤いの (the red one). (2) な-adjective + な + の: 好きなケーキ → 好きなの (the ones you like; な must be retained!). (3) Noun + の: メアリーさんのかばん → メアリーさんの (Mary's one / Mary's). CRITICAL TEXTBOOK CONSTRAINT (Footnote 4): The substitute の stands for inanimate things or animals, NOT people. When referring to a person, you must use an explicit human noun like 人 (e.g. 頭がいい人, NEVER *頭がいいの).
keyTakeaway: Replaces understood noun: い-adj + の (赤いの), な-adj + なの (好きなの - keep な!), Noun + の (メアリーさんの). STRICT RESTRICTION: の cannot replace human beings (use 人).

sentences.japanese: 青いのより、赤いのが好きです。
sentences.english: I prefer the red one to the blue one.

sentences.japanese: 赤いかばんは高いです。青いのを買います。
sentences.english: The red bag is expensive. I will buy the blue one.
sentences.nuanceNote: の replaces the understood noun after an い-adjective.

sentences.japanese: 大きな部屋より、静かなのがいいです。
sentences.english: I would prefer a quiet room to a large one.
sentences.nuanceNote: A な-adjective retains な before noun-replacing の.

quiz.question: A:「どれが田中さんのペンですか。」 B:「あの黒い（　　）です。」
quiz.translation: A: 'Which one is Tanaka-san's pen?' B: 'It's that black one.'
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun-substitute pronoun の (The one)
quiz.ruleHint: Adjective + の replaces a previously mentioned concrete noun (黒いペン → 黒いの).

explanations.reason: Correct! の acts as the pronoun 'one' replacing the noun ペン: 黒いのです.
Incorrect. こと refers to abstract concepts or matters, never physical items like pens.
Incorrect. 黒いもの is unnecessarily general/formal when referring to an identified pen.
Incorrect. 方 means 'direction' or 'person' (polite).

title: どこか・どこにも・で
meaning: Somewhere, nowhere and a means or cost.
connection: どこか(へ/に) + affirmative | どこにも / どこへも + negative | [Means/Tool] で | 歩いて行く (exception, no で)
nuance: This grammar point covers indefinite place pronouns and the instrumental particle で. (1) Indefinite Place Pronouns: どこか ('somewhere') and どこにも / どこへも ('nowhere / not anywhere'). In affirmative sentences: どこか(へ/に)行きましたか (Did you go somewhere?). Particles へ and に can be omitted after か. In negative sentences: Particle に or へ is PRESERVED before も: どこにも行きませんでした / どこへも行きませんでした (I went nowhere). (2) Means / Instrument Particle で: Used for vehicles, tools, and languages (電車で行く, バスで行く, はしで食べる, 日本語で話す). CRITICAL TEXTBOOK EXCEPTION: Going on foot uses the te-form adverb 歩いて行く (walk / on foot), NEVER with particle で (*歩いてで行く is wrong).
keyTakeaway: どこか(へ) (somewhere, affirmative). どこにも / どこへも (nowhere, negative; keep に/へ before も). Means: [Vehicle/Tool] で行く/食べる. EXCEPTION: 歩いて行く (no で).

sentences.japanese: 休みはどこにも行きません。二千円でこの本を買いました。
sentences.english: I will not go anywhere on my day off. I bought this book for two thousand yen.

sentences.japanese: 休みにどこかへ行きたいです。
sentences.english: I want to go somewhere on my day off.
sentences.nuanceNote: どこか expresses an unspecified place; へ marks destination.

sentences.japanese: 昨日はどこにも行きませんでした。今日はバスで学校へ行きます。
sentences.english: I did not go anywhere yesterday. Today I will go to school by bus.
sentences.nuanceNote: どこにも needs the negative here; バスで marks the means of transport.

sentences.japanese: この本を五百円で買いました。
sentences.english: I bought this book for five hundred yen.
sentences.nuanceNote: で can mark the price/amount for the transaction, not just an action location or transport method.

quiz.question: 先週末は疲れていたので、（　　）出かけませんでした。
quiz.translation: Because I was tired last weekend, I didn't go anywhere.
quiz.grammarFocus: どこにも + Negative (Not anywhere)
quiz.ruleHint: どこか means 'somewhere'; どこにも / どこへも pairs with negative verbs to mean 'nowhere'.

explanations.reason: Correct! どこにも pairs with negative verbs (出かけませんでした) to mean 'nowhere at all'.
Incorrect. どこかに means 'to somewhere' and pairs with affirmative actions.
Incorrect. どこかへ also pairs with affirmative predicates.
Incorrect. どこでも means 'anywhere / everywhere' and takes affirmative verbs.

title: 〜たい / 〜たくない (Expressing Desire to Do: Want to Do)
meaning: Want to do an action; たくない means not want to do it.
connection: Vます-stem + たい / たくない / たかった / たくなかった | Vます-stem + たいと思っています | Vます-stem + たがっている
nuance: Attach たい to the verb stem (the form before ます) to express personal hope or aspiration: V-stem + たいです. Direct Object Particle: A verb that usually takes particle を can take EITHER を OR が when followed by たい (e.g. 映画を見る → 映画を見たい OR 映画が見たい). Particles other than を remain unchanged (中国に行きたい). Conjugation: たい conjugates identically to an い-adjective: たい、たくない、たかった、たくなかった. Long-Held Wish: If the speaker has entertained the desire for some time ('have wanted to'), use 〜たいと思っています (e.g. 留学したいと思っています). Third-Person Wishes: Bare 〜たい describes only the speaker's desires (or the listener in direct questions). For third persons, report their desire as quotation (メアリーさんはチベットに行きたいと言っていました) or use the observation verb 〜たがっている (derived from u-verb たがる: メアリーさんは着物を着たがっています). CRITICAL PARTICLE CONSTRAINT: 〜たがっている takes ONLY を, NEVER が (*着物が着たがっている is strictly ungrammatical).
keyTakeaway: V-stem + たい (conjugates like い-adj). Direct object can take を or が. Long-term wish: 〜たいと思っています. Third person: 〜たいと言っていました or 〜たがっています (takes ONLY を, never が).

sentences.japanese: 日本へ行って、本場のラーメンが食べたいです。
sentences.english: I want to go to Japan and eat authentic ramen.
sentences.literal: Japan-to go, authentic ramen eat-want is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Desire to eat authentic ramen.

sentences.japanese: 日本へ行きたいです。どこへ行きたいですか。
sentences.english: I want to go to Japan. Where do you want to go?
sentences.nuanceNote: A statement normally reports the speaker's desire; a question can ask the listener's desire.

sentences.japanese: 今日は何もしたくないです。子供のころは先生になりたかったです。
sentences.english: I do not want to do anything today. When I was a child, I wanted to become a teacher.
sentences.nuanceNote: たい conjugates like an い-adjective: たくない and たかった.

quiz.question: 今日はとても疲れたので、何も（　　）たくないです。
quiz.translation: Because I am so tired today, I do not want to do anything.
quiz.grammarFocus: Negative desire 〜たくない with verb stem
quiz.ruleHint: Vます-stem + たい / たくない / たかった

explanations.reason: Correct! する stem is し + たくない (したくない = do not want to do).
Incorrect. する is dictionary form.
Incorrect. して is te-form.
Incorrect. した is past form.

title: 〜ことがある (Past Experiential Aspect: Have Ever Done)
meaning: Have done something before; have had an experience.
connection: V-た形 + ことがある / あります | V-た形 + ことがありません / ない
nuance: The past tense short form of an affirmative verb + ことがある / あります describes that one has had the experience of doing something in earlier times: V-た + ことがある / あります (e.g. 富士山に登ったことがあります). Negative: V-た + ことがありません / ない (have never done; often paired with 一度も: 一度も馬刺しを食べたことがありません). Response Etiquette: In reply to 〜たことがありますか, respond with はい、あります or repeat the verb (はい、行ったことがあります), but NEVER *はい、そうです or *はい、行きました without experiential framing. CRITICAL DISTINCTION (Footnote 1): Contrast 〜たことがありません with まだ〜ていません (Lesson 9). Use まだ〜ていません when you have not yet done something but expect to do it eventually (e.g. まだ宿題をしていません). Use 〜たことがありません when you simply lack the historical experience and do not necessarily anticipate doing it (e.g. 南極に行ったことがありません). Can pair with だけ (一回だけ会ったことがある).
keyTakeaway: V-た + ことがある / あります (have had experience of). Negative: 〜たことがありません. Answer: はい、あります (never *はい、そうです). Lacking experience = 〜たことがない vs pending plan = まだ〜ていません.

sentences.japanese: 富士山に登ったことがありますか。「ええ、一度あります。」
sentences.english: Have you ever climbed Mt. Fuji? 'Yes, once.'
sentences.literal: Mt-Fuji climbed experience have question? Yes, once have.

tokens.word: 登ったことがありますか
tokens.reading: のぼったことがありますか

sentences.nuanceNote: Lifetime experiential inquiry.

sentences.japanese: 京都へ行ったことがあります。
sentences.english: I have been to Kyoto before.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vたことがある presents a past occurrence as an experience, rather than simply reporting a dated trip.

sentences.japanese: 歌舞伎を見たことは一度もありません。昨日は映画を見ました。
sentences.english: I have never seen kabuki. Yesterday I watched a film.
sentences.useLabel: Never, contrasted with a past report
sentences.nuanceNote: Experiential 一度も…ない differs from a simple past report about yesterday.

quiz.question: 歌舞伎を（　　）ことがありますか。「いいえ、一度もありません。」
quiz.translation: Have you ever seen Kabuki? 'No, not once.'
quiz.grammarFocus: V-た + ことがある lifetime experience
quiz.ruleHint: V-た + ことがある / あります (Negative: ありません / ない)

explanations.reason: Correct! Experiential aspect requires past form 見た + ことがある.
Incorrect. 見ることがある means 'there are times when I see' (occasional habit), not past experience.
Incorrect. 見て is te-form.
Incorrect. 見 is masu-stem.

title: 〜たり〜たりする・や
meaning: Give non-exhaustive examples.
connection: V1-た + り、V2-た + りする / しました | Noun A や Noun B (など)
nuance: This grammar point covers non-exhaustive representative listing for activities and nouns. (1) 〜たり〜たりする: Connects actions as non-exhaustive examples in no set chronological order ('do such things as this and that'). Contrast with 〜て clause chaining (which implies an exhaustive list executed in strict sequential order). Formation: Attach り to the past tense short forms of verbs: V-た + り、V-た + りする (e.g. 週末は勉強したり、友達と話したりしました). Tense & Polarity: Carried exclusively by the final helping verb する (e.g. 〜したり〜したりしませんでした / 〜したり〜したりするのが好きです). (2) Noun A や Noun B: Connects nouns non-exhaustively ('A and B, for example'). Contrast with と (which lists all items exhaustively). Frequently followed by など ('and so on'). (3) Expression Note: In negative sentences, particle は often replaces を or が to mark contrast (テレビは見ません; コーヒーは好きじゃありません).
keyTakeaway: V-た + り、V-た + りする = non-exhaustive activities in no set order (tense on final する). Noun や Noun = non-exhaustive nouns (unlike と). Negative sentences often replace を/が with contrastive は.

sentences.japanese: 休みの日は料理をしたり、本を読んだりします。
sentences.english: On days off I do things such as cooking and reading.

sentences.japanese: 週末は映画を見たり、買い物をしたりしました。
sentences.english: At the weekend I did things such as watching a film and shopping.
sentences.nuanceNote: たり lists examples, not a strict sequence or necessarily a complete list; tense is on the final しました.

sentences.japanese: 机の上に本やノートがあります。
sentences.english: There are books, notebooks, and other things on the desk.
sentences.nuanceNote: や lists representative nouns and leaves room for other items; と more directly lists the specified items together.

quiz.question: 休みの日は、部屋を掃除し（　　）、洗濯し（　　）しました。
quiz.translation: On my days off, I did things like cleaning my room and doing laundry.
quiz.grammarFocus: Listing representative activities (〜たり〜たりする)
quiz.ruleHint: Verb た-form + り + Verb た-form + り + する lists representative non-exhaustive actions.

explanations.reason: Correct! 掃除したり、洗濯したりしました lists non-exhaustive weekend activities.
Incorrect. て-form lists chronological sequential actions in full, not representative examples.
Incorrect. 〜し〜し lists reasons or predicates in plain form.
Incorrect. 〜ながら indicates simultaneous actions conducted at the exact same moment.

title: 〜すぎる (Excessiveness: Too Much / Overdoing)
meaning: Indicates exceeding a proper, healthy, or desirable threshold: 'too [adj]' or 'doing [verb] too much'.
connection: Vます-stem + すぎる | い-adj (drop い) + すぎる | な-adj stem + すぎる
nuance: The helping verb すぎる means 'too much' or 'to excess', indicating that an action or property is beyond normal or proper degree. Conjugation: すぎる conjugates as a regular Ru-verb (すぎます、すぎて、すぎました、すぎない). Formation: (1) Verbs: verb stem (pre-ます) + すぎる (早く起きすぎました: got up too early; 食べすぎてはいけません: must not overeat). (2) い-adjectives: drop final い + すぎる (高すぎる: too expensive; 大きすぎる: too big). Exception: いい → よすぎる. (3) な-adjectives: adjective base (drop な) + すぎる (静かすぎる: too quiet; 親切すぎる: too kind). PRAGMATIC CAUTION: すぎる suggests an undesirable or unwelcome excess; 親切すぎます (too kind) is NOT a straightforward compliment. Use とても or すごく for straightforward praise. Noun form: The noun form 〜すぎ is also widely used (e.g. 食べすぎです: overeating).
keyTakeaway: V-stem / い-adj (drop い) / な-adj (drop な) + すぎる. Conjugates as Ru-verb. Suggests unwelcome excess (not a simple compliment). Noun form: 〜すぎ (食べすぎ).

sentences.japanese: 昨夜はお酒を飲みすぎて、今朝はひどい二日酔いです。
sentences.english: Last night I drank too much alcohol, and this morning I have a terrible hangover.
sentences.literal: Last-night alcohol drink-excessively, this-morning terrible hangover is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Excessive drinking resulting in hangover.

sentences.japanese: 昨日は食べすぎました。
sentences.english: I ate too much yesterday.
sentences.nuanceNote: Verb stem + すぎる; the resulting expression conjugates as a ru-verb.

sentences.japanese: この服は高すぎます。説明は簡単すぎました。
sentences.english: These clothes are too expensive. The explanation was too simple.
sentences.nuanceNote: An い-adjective drops い; a な-adjective uses its stem without な.

quiz.question: この問題は難し（　　）て、私には全く分かりません。
quiz.translation: This problem is too difficult, so I don't understand it at all.
quiz.grammarFocus: い-adjective + すぎる excessiveness
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem + すぎる | い-adj (drop い) + すぎる | な-adj stem + すぎる (Conjugates as Ru-verb)

explanations.reason: Correct! 難しい drops い + すぎて forms 難しすぎて ('too difficult').
Incorrect. そう indicates appearance (難しそう).
Incorrect. やすく indicates ease (難しやすく is nonsense).
Incorrect. がち indicates negative tendency.

title: 〜ので (Reason / Background Circumstance)
meaning: Because; since. Presents a reason or background circumstance.
connection: Short form (V / い-adj) + ので | な-adj + なので | Noun + なので
nuance: Connects a reason to a situation: (reason) ので、(situation) ('Because [reason], [situation]'). Stylistic comparison: Semantically similar to から, but ので sounds slightly more formal, courteous, and objective; it presents the clause as an objective circumstance rather than a personal emotional justification, and is preferred in polite requests and formal writing. Formation: Preceding clause is in short form. CRITICAL RULE: When following a な-adjective or a noun in the present tense affirmative, な comes in between: な-adj + なので, Noun + なので (いじわるなので, 日曜日なので! NEVER *日曜日だので).
keyTakeaway: Objective reason linker: clause(short form) + ので. Nouns and な-adj in present affirmative MUST take なので (日曜日なので; never *だので). More formal/objective than から.

sentences.japanese: 明日は朝早く出発するので、今夜は準備をして早く寝ます。
sentences.english: Since I will depart early tomorrow morning, I will prepare tonight and go to bed early.
sentences.literal: Tomorrow morning early depart since, tonight prepare early sleep.
sentences.nuanceNote: Objective factual circumstance motivating early rest.

sentences.japanese: 少し寒いので、窓を閉めてもいいですか。
sentences.english: It is a little cold, so may I close the window?
sentences.nuanceNote: ので can precede a polite request; a universal ban on requests after ので is false.

sentences.japanese: 今日は休みなので、家にいます。昨日は休みだったので、出かけました。
sentences.english: Today is a day off, so I am at home. Yesterday was a day off, so I went out.
sentences.nuanceNote: Non-past affirmative nouns use なので; the past form retains だった before ので.

quiz.question: 明日は（　　）なので、一日中家でのんびり過ごします。
quiz.translation: Since tomorrow is a holiday, I will spend the entire day relaxing at home.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + な + ので objective causality
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + ので | な-adj / Noun + な + ので (Notice the required な!)

explanations.reason: Correct! Noun 休み connects via な to ので (休みなので).
Incorrect. 休みの is an invalid connector to ので.
Incorrect. 休みだ cannot attach to ので (must be なので, NOT だので ❌).
Incorrect. 休みに is adverbial.

title: 〜なければいけません / なきゃいけません (Obligation: Must Do / Have to Do)
meaning: Expresses an unavoidable obligation or necessity: 'Must do / Have to do X'. Spoken contraction: 〜なきゃいけません / なきゃ.
connection: V-ない (drop い) + ければいけません / なきゃいけません | Past: 〜ければいけませんでした
nuance: Expresses obligation: 'must do / have to do'. Double Negative Logic: なければ / なきゃ literally means 'if you do not do X', and いけません means 'you cannot proceed / it won't do'. The double negative construct yields the affirmative mandate. Formation: Take the negative short form V-ない, drop the final い, and attach: (1) Formal / standard written: 〜なければいけません (e.g. 薬を飲まなければいけません). (2) Colloquial spoken: 〜なきゃいけません (or casual short forms: 〜なければいけない, 〜なきゃ). Past obligation: Change いけません to いけませんでした (今朝は六時に起きなければいけませんでした: I had to get up at six this morning).
keyTakeaway: V-ない (drop い) + ければいけません (formal) / なきゃいけません (colloquial). Past: 〜なければいけませんでした. Double negative structure.

sentences.japanese: 明日の朝九時までに、レポートを提出しなければいけません。
sentences.english: I must submit the report by 9:00 AM tomorrow morning.
sentences.literal: Tomorrow morning 9-by report submit must.

tokens.word: 提出しなければいけません
tokens.reading: ていしゅつしなければいけません

sentences.nuanceNote: Strict academic obligation.

sentences.japanese: 明日までに宿題を出さなければいけません。
sentences.english: I must submit the homework by tomorrow.
sentences.nuanceNote: 出す becomes 出さない; replace final い with ければいけない.

sentences.japanese: もう帰らなきゃ。
sentences.english: I have to go home now.
sentences.nuanceNote: なきゃ is a conversational contraction; the final いけない can be omitted when understood.

quiz.question: 熱が高いですから、今日は病院へ（　　）ければいけませんよ。
quiz.translation: Since your fever is high, you must go to the hospital today.
quiz.grammarFocus: Obligation formula 〜なければいけません
quiz.ruleHint: V-ない (drop い) + ければいけません / ければなりません

explanations.reason: Correct! 行く negative stem is 行かな + ければいけません.
Incorrect. 行く is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 行って is te-form.
Incorrect. 行き is masu-stem.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 272 (PDF p. 280). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜でしょう / 〜だろう (Conjecture & Probability: Probably)
meaning: Expresses conjecture or probability without absolute certainty: 'Probably / It will likely be X'. Also used with rising tone to seek agreement ('Right?').
connection: Short form (V / い-adj) + でしょう | な-adj stem + でしょう (no だ!) | Noun + でしょう (no だ!)
nuance: Expresses conjecture and probability: 'probably'. Interrogative use: Phrasing a question with 〜でしょうか adds tentativeness and politeness, implying that the listener probably has better information and avoiding putting them on the spot (e.g. 明日は雨が降るでしょうか). Non-interrogative guess: Makes a guess, frequently paired with the adverb たぶん (probably) earlier in the sentence (明日はたぶん寒くないでしょう). CRITICAL BAN FOR NOUNS AND な-ADJECTIVES: Follows nouns and な-adjectives directly WITHOUT だ! e.g. トマトは野菜でしょう (strictly prohibited: *野菜だでしょう). e.g. 明日は静かでしょう (strictly prohibited: *静かだでしょう). Past forms: 雨だったでしょう, 静かだったでしょう. Casual speech: 〜だろう (rising intonation: 〜でしょ？).
keyTakeaway: Short form + でしょう (probably). Interrogative: 〜でしょうか (polite tentative query). CRITICAL RULE: Nouns & な-adj attach directly WITHOUT だ (雨でしょう, never *雨だでしょう).

sentences.japanese: 天気予報によると、明日は午後から雨が降るでしょう。
sentences.english: According to the weather forecast, it will probably rain from the afternoon tomorrow.
sentences.literal: Weather-forecast according-to, tomorrow afternoon-from rain fall probably.
sentences.nuanceNote: Meteorological conjecture.

sentences.japanese: 明日は寒いでしょう。
sentences.english: It will probably be cold tomorrow.
sentences.nuanceNote: でしょう expresses a prediction, not a numerical probability guarantee.

sentences.japanese: あの人は先生でしょう。
sentences.english: That person is probably a teacher.
sentences.nuanceNote: A non-past affirmative noun attaches directly to でしょう, without だ.

quiz.question: 田中さんはよく勉強していますから、明日の試験に（　　）でしょう。
quiz.translation: Tanaka studies hard, so they will probably pass tomorrow's exam.
quiz.grammarFocus: Conjecture 〜でしょう with plain verb
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + でしょう (Polite) / だろう (Plain) [Noun & な-adj attach directly without だ!]

explanations.reason: The dictionary form connects directly to でしょう.
The te-form does not connect directly to でしょう here.
The bare stem does not form the required predicate.
Do not put だ after a finite verb before でしょう.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 272 (PDF p. 280). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜んです
meaning: Explain background or ask for an explanation.
connection: Short form (V / い-adj) + んです | な-adj + なんです | Noun + なんです
nuance: There are two distinct ways to make a statement in Japanese: simple reporting of facts as observed (あした試験があります), versus explaining things (あした試験があるんです: explains why I cannot go out tonight). The sentence-final expression んです connects what the sentence says with what it accounts for in the conversational situation. Question use: Invites clarifications or explanations, frequently with どうして (why) and どうしたんですか (what happened?). Footnote 2 rule: A どうしたんですか question is best answered by an 〜んです sentence with the subject marked by が rather than は (e.g. 猫が死んだんです). Invariant ending: んです itself does not appear in negative or past tense forms; tense and polarity are carried entirely by the preceding short form (成績がよくないんです; 試験が終わったんです). Formation: Verbs & い-adjectives attach directly in short forms. CRITICAL RULE: Nouns and な-adjectives in present affirmative MUST insert な before んです (静かなんです, 学生なんです! NEVER *静かだんです or *学生だんです). Style variants: のです (formal/written), んだ (casual spoken), の (casual question).
keyTakeaway: Explanatory link for reasons and clarifications. Verbs/い-adj: short form + んです. な-adj & Nouns: MUST take なんです (静かなんです, 学生なんです; never *だんです).

sentences.japanese: 今日は早く帰ります。試験があるんです。
sentences.english: I am going home early today. I have an exam.

sentences.japanese: 今日は早く帰ります。用事があるんです。
sentences.english: I am going home early today. I have something to do.
sentences.nuanceNote: んです presents the second statement as an explanation relevant to the first.

sentences.japanese: どうして休んだんですか。熱があったんです。
sentences.english: Why were you absent? I had a fever.
sentences.nuanceNote: The explanatory question asks for background; the past predicates retain their past forms before んです.

quiz.question: A:「顔色が悪いですね。どうしたんですか。」 B:「頭がとても痛い（　　）。」
quiz.translation: A: 'You look pale. What's the matter?' B: 'It's that I have a very bad headache.'
quiz.grammarFocus: Explanatory 〜んです (Providing rationale)
quiz.ruleHint: 〜んです provides an explanation or reason for an observed situation or state.

explanations.reason: Correct! 痛いんです directly answers どうしたんですか with an explanatory statement.
Incorrect. のですか is a question form, but B is providing an answer.
Incorrect. からだ is plain causal assertion without the communicative engagement of んです.
Incorrect. わけだ means 'so that's why' (drawing a logical conclusion).

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 272 (PDF p. 280). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ほうがいい
meaning: Giving direct personal advice or recommendations: 'It is better to / you should' (Vたほうがいい) or 'better not to' (Vないほうがいい).
connection: V-た + ほうがいいです (affirmative advice) | V-ない + ほうがいいです (negative advice)
nuance: Sentence-final expression used to give advice or recommendations: 'it is better (for you) to do X'. TENSE ASYMMETRY (CRITICAL TEXTBOOK RULE): (1) Affirmative advice: Uses PAST TENSE short form of the verb: V-た + ほうがいいです (e.g. もっと野菜を食べたほうがいいですよ: You'd better eat more vegetables). (2) Negative advice: Uses PRESENT TENSE short form of the verb: V-ない + ほうがいいです (e.g. 授業を休まないほうがいいですよ: It is better not to skip classes). Never use *V-る + ほうがいいです for specific personal advice in standard Genki Japanese. Pragmatics: Giving advice directly can sound intrusive; soften with sentence particles like よ or ね.
keyTakeaway: Giving advice: Affirmative uses PAST short form: V-た + ほうがいいです. Negative uses PRESENT short form: V-ない + ほうがいいです. Asymmetry rule is strict.

sentences.japanese: 今日は早く寝たほうがいいですよ。
sentences.english: You should go to bed early today.

sentences.japanese: 疲れているなら、少し休んだほうがいいです。
sentences.english: If you are tired, you should rest a little.
sentences.nuanceNote: The affirmative advice uses Vた even though the recommended action is still in the future.

sentences.japanese: 夜遅くにコーヒーを飲まないほうがいいです。
sentences.english: You should not drink coffee late at night.
sentences.nuanceNote: Negative advice uses Vない; it is advice, not the formal prohibition てはいけない.

sentences.japanese: どうして遅刻したのですか。「目覚まし時計が鳴らなかったんです。」
sentences.english: Why were you late? "The thing is, my alarm clock didn't ring."
sentences.nuanceNote: Explanatory んです provides the empathetic reason for the mishap.

sentences.japanese: どうして遅刻したのですか。電車が止まったんです。
sentences.english: Why were you late? It's because the train stopped.
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜んです provides an underlying causal explanation for an observed situation.

sentences.japanese: 頭が痛いんです。少し休んでもいいですか。
sentences.english: The thing is, I have a headache. May I rest a little?
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜んです frames personal circumstances before requesting permission.

quiz.question: 熱が高いですから、今日は無理をしない（　　）いいですよ。
quiz.translation: Since your fever is high, it's better not to overdo it today.
quiz.grammarFocus: Negative Advice: 〜ないほうがいい
quiz.ruleHint: Giving advice: V-た + ほうがいい (should do) / V-ない + ほうがいい (should not do).

explanations.reason: Correct! V-ない + ほうがいい advises against an action: 無理をしないほうがいい.
Incorrect. より marks comparison ('than'), not advice.
Incorrect. ほど indicates degree or extent.
Incorrect. ように denotes purpose or indirect request, not direct advice.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 272 (PDF p. 280). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 可能形 (Potential Verbs: Ability & Possibility)
meaning: Expresses that an agent has the ability to do an action or that circumstances permit it.
connection: Ru: V-stem + られる | U: V (u->e) + る | くる→こられる | する→できる
nuance: Potential verbs express that an agent has the ability to do an action ("can do"), or that circumstances permit it ("is possible"). Conjugation rules: (1) Ru-verbs: drop -ru and add -rareru (見る → 見られる, 食べる → 食べられる). Spoken casual allows "ra-less" forms (見れる, 食べれる), though school grammar flags them (Footnote 1). (2) U-verbs: drop -u and add -eru (行く → 行ける, 泳ぐ → 泳げる, 話す → 話せる, 待つ → 待てる, 飲む → 飲める, 買う → 買える). (3) Irregular verbs: 来る (くる) → こられる (ra-less: これる); する → できる. Potential verbs themselves conjugate as regular Ru-verbs (話せる、話せない、話せます、話せません、話せた、話せて). PARTICLE ALTERNATION: Verbs that take direct object を can take EITHER を OR が when converted to the potential (漢字を読む → 漢字が読める OR 漢字を読める). Special case: できる takes が almost exclusively (仕事ができる). All particles other than を (に, で, へ, etc.) remain unchanged (山に登れる).
keyTakeaway: Ru-verbs: -rareru (見られる). U-verbs: -eru (行ける, 読める). くる→こられる, する→できる. Direct object を can switch to が (漢字が読める). Other particles do not change.

sentences.japanese: 漢字が難しくて、新聞がすらすら読めません。
sentences.english: The kanji are difficult, so I cannot read the newspaper smoothly.
sentences.literal: Kanji difficult-being, newspaper smoothly read-cannot.
sentences.nuanceNote: 読む potential negative: 読める → 読めません.

sentences.japanese: 私は日本語の新聞が読めます。弟はまだ読めません。
sentences.english: I can read Japanese newspapers. My younger brother cannot yet.
sentences.nuanceNote: An u-verb changes 読む→読める; the potential verb then has polite affirmative/negative forms.

sentences.japanese: この店では、新鮮な魚が食べられます。
sentences.english: You can eat fresh fish at this restaurant.
sentences.nuanceNote: 食べる→食べられる is the standard ru-verb potential; this example describes an available opportunity, not just a personal skill.

quiz.question: 「食べることができません」という意味です。生魚が食べ（　　）。
quiz.translation: I cannot eat raw fish.
quiz.grammarFocus: 可能形 potential negative
quiz.ruleHint: Ru-verbs: 食べる→食べられる | U-verbs: 書く→書ける, 飲む→飲める | Irregular: する→できる, くる→こられる

explanations.reason: 食べられません is the standard potential negative.
食べさせます is causative: make/let eat.
食べたいです expresses desire.
食べました is past affirmative.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: Genki II: Potential Verbs (可能形) Matrix (Lesson 13)
table.subtitle: Expressing ability and situational possibility ("can do").

rows.label: Group 2: Ru-Verbs
cells: 食べる, 見る, 起きる
食べられる, 見られる, 起きられる (Drop る, attach られる)
Direct object particle を shifts to が: 漢字が読める, 日本語が話せる
Colloquial "ra-nuki" (ら抜き): 食べれる, 見れる (frequent in spoken Japanese, but avoid on formal JLPT!)
rows.note: Identical form to passive; context disambiguates.

rows.label: Group 1: U-Verbs
cells: 行く, 飲む, 話す, 待つ, 泳ぐ
行ける, 飲める, 話せる, 待てる, 泳げる (Shift final -u sound to -e sound and add る)
All potential verbs conjugate as Group 2 (Ichidan) verbs once transformed: 話せる → 話せます / 話せない
Do NOT add られる to U-verbs! 行く becomes 行ける, NOT 行かられる ❌!
rows.note: Clean shift: -u → -eru.

rows.label: Group 3: Irregular
cells: する (to do), 来る (くる, to come)
する → できる, 来る → こられる (来られる)
Particle shift: 運転ができる (Can drive), 日本語ができる (Can speak Japanese)
Note the reading of 来 changes to "ko": こられる (NOT ちられる ❌).
rows.note: する completely transforms into the independent potential verb できる.

title: 〜し、〜し (Listing Multiple Parallel Reasons)
meaning: Lists two or more complementary reasons leading up to a conclusion or emotion ('Not only... but also...').
connection: Short form + し | な-adj / Noun + だし
nuance: Used to mention two or more parallel reasons leading up to a situation or conclusion: (reason 1) し、(reason 2) し、(situation). Predicate form: Usually follows predicates in the short form (面白いし、物価が安いし). In polite speech, can follow long forms (好きですし). Single し: When only one し clause is cited, it implies that it is not the only reason for the situation. MANDATORY だ RULE: For な-adjectives and Nouns in the present tense affirmative, mandatory だ must precede し (親切だし, 学生だし! NEVER *親切し or *学生し). い-adjectives take し directly (面白いし).
keyTakeaway: Listing reasons: [Reason 1]し、[Reason 2]し、[Situation]. Short form predicate. MANDATORY: な-adj and Nouns take だし (親切だし, 学生だし; never bare stem + し).

sentences.japanese: 物価も安いし、治安もいいし、この街に住んでよかったです。
sentences.english: Prices are cheap and public safety is great, so I am really glad I live in this town.
sentences.literal: Prices-also cheap-and, safety-also good-and, this town-in living glad-was.
sentences.nuanceNote: Two positive factors combined using 〜し.

sentences.japanese: この店は安いし、おいしいし、よく来ます。
sentences.english: I come here often because it is cheap and the food is good.
sentences.nuanceNote: し accumulates contributing reasons; it need not claim that these are the only ones.

sentences.japanese: 明日は休みだし、少し夜更かししてもいいでしょう。
sentences.english: Tomorrow is a day off, among other things, so staying up a little should be fine.
sentences.useLabel: One explicit reason with others implied
sentences.nuanceNote: A single stated し reason is possible; a noun predicate uses だし.

quiz.question: この部屋は（　　）し、駅にも近いです。
quiz.translation: This room is quiet and is also near the station.
quiz.grammarFocus: い-adjective connection to 〜し
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + し (Noun/な-adj non-past affirmative takes だ: 綺麗だし, 休みだし)

explanations.reason: A plain affirmative na-adjective takes だ before し.
The bare na-adjective stem does not attach directly to し.
な is the noun-modifying linker, not the ending before し.
で is connective but does not form the required predicate before し.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てみる (Trying Out an Action: Doing Something to See What Happens)
meaning: Performs an experimental action to test the waters or see what the outcome will be: 'try doing / give it a try'.
connection: V-て形 + みる / みます / みて / みた
nuance: The te-form of a verb plus the helping auxiliary みる expresses "doing something tentatively" or "trying something out to see what happens" (testing the waters when outcome is uncertain). Formation: V-て + みる (e.g. 食べてみる, 書いてみる, 行ってみる, 着てみる). Conjugation: みる conjugates as a regular Ru-verb (〜てみます、〜てみた、〜てみてください). ORTHOGRAPHY RULE: Unlike the main lexical verb 見る (to look/see), the auxiliary 〜てみる is ALWAYS written in hiragana.
keyTakeaway: V-て + みる (try doing to see outcome). みる conjugates as Ru-verb. Orthography: Always write auxiliary 〜てみる in hiragana (never *〜て見る).

sentences.japanese: 日本の納豆はまだ食べたことがないので、一口食べてみます。
sentences.english: Since I have never eaten Japanese natto yet, I will try taking a bite to see what it's like.
sentences.literal: Japan's natto yet eaten experience have-not since, one-bite eat-and-see.
sentences.nuanceNote: Experimental culinary trial.

sentences.japanese: この靴を履いてみてもいいですか。
sentences.english: May I try these shoes on?
sentences.nuanceNote: てみる means carrying out the action to see what it is like or what happens.

sentences.japanese: 先生に聞いてみましたが、先生も知りませんでした。
sentences.english: I tried asking the teacher, but the teacher did not know either.
sentences.useLabel: Try an action, learn the result
sentences.nuanceNote: The attempt at asking occurred; the desired information was not obtained.

quiz.question: この服、サイズが合うかどうか一度（　　）みてもいいですか。
quiz.translation: May I try this clothing on once to see if the size fits?
quiz.grammarFocus: V-て + みる (Try doing)
quiz.ruleHint: V-て + みる (Conjugates as a Ru-verb: 〜てみます, 〜てみたい)

explanations.reason: Correct! 着る is a Ru-verb: te-form 着て + みてもいいですか (着てみてもいいですか).
Incorrect. 着る is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 着 is bare stem.
Incorrect. 着た is past form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: なら (Contextual Limitation Conditional: If It's X / As For X)
meaning: Singles out a specific topic from context: 'If we're talking about X, then... / As for X (though other things might not be)'.
connection: Noun + なら | Noun + [に/で/から] + なら
nuance: X (noun) なら Y (predicate) introduces a conditional context where predicate Y applies specifically to X and is not more generally valid. Semantic core: Contrast and Limitation. It singles out an item from the conversational context and introduces a positive statement about that specific item while contrasting it with other alternatives (e.g. チリなら行きましたが、ブラジルは行ったことがありません: If it's Chile, yes; but Brazil, no; ひらがななら読めます: If it's in hiragana, I can read it). PARTICLE RULE (Footnote 6): Particles は, が, を never appear before なら (they are dropped). Particles like に, で, から may optionally be retained (チリになら).
keyTakeaway: Noun + なら (contextual limitation: If it is X / As for X). Singles out an item with contrastive positive applicability. Particles は/が/を are dropped before なら.

sentences.japanese: 英語なら話せますが、フランス語は全く話せません。
sentences.english: If it's English, I can speak it, but I cannot speak French at all.
sentences.literal: English if-talking-about speak-can but, French at-all speak-cannot.
sentences.nuanceNote: Selective linguistic competence.

sentences.japanese: 日本へ行くなら、少し日本語を勉強しておくといいです。
sentences.english: If you are going to Japan, it is a good idea to study some Japanese beforehand.
sentences.nuanceNote: The recommended preparation comes before the trip; なら does not mean after going.

sentences.japanese: ひらがななら読めますが、漢字はまだ苦手です。
sentences.english: I can read hiragana, but I am still not good at kanji.
sentences.nuanceNote: なら focuses the ability claim on hiragana. The contrast is supplied explicitly here.

quiz.question: 「明日京都に行くんですが。」「京都（　　）、金閣寺がおすすめですよ。」
quiz.translation: 'I'm going to Kyoto tomorrow.' 'If it's Kyoto, Kinkaku-ji is highly recommended!'
quiz.grammarFocus: Contextual conditional なら
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + なら (Attaches directly without だ!) | Plain form + なら

explanations.reason: Correct! なら picks up the conversational topic mentioned by the partner.
Incorrect. たら is temporal sequence ('if/when Kyoto happens').
Incorrect. ば requires a predicate (verb/adjective).
Incorrect. と is natural inevitable consequence.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜そうです：様子
meaning: An appearance-based impression.
connection: い-adj (drop い) + そうです | いい → よさそうです | な-adj stem + そうです | V-stem + そうです
nuance: Add そうです to adjective bases to state a conjectural impression based on visual/intuitive appearance ("it looks like / seems [property]"). Conjugation rules: (1) い-adjectives: drop final い + そうです (おいしい → おいしそうです, 寒そう). CRITICAL EXCEPTION: The adjective いい changes to よさそう (NOT *いそう ❌). (2) な-adjectives: drop な + そうです (元気[な] → 元気そうです, 暇そう). (3) Negative appearance: い-adj negative ない changes to なさそう (よくなさそう, 面白くなさそう), or negate the ending (おいしそうじゃないです). (4) Verbs: verb stem + そうです (雨が降りそうです: it looks like it will rain). CRITICAL VISUAL CONSTRAINT: 〜そうです is used when we lack conclusive evidence (e.g. before tasting food). For adjectives where visual evidence is already self-evident to the eyes, such as きれい (pretty/clean) or かわいい (cute), you CANNOT use そうです: *きれいそうです is strictly prohibited. Say きれいですね.
keyTakeaway: い-adj (drop い) + そうです (おいしそう). EXCEPTION: いい→よさそう. な-adj (drop な) + そうです (元気そう). Verbs: stem + そうです (降りそう). BAN on self-evident visual words (*きれいそう is wrong).

sentences.japanese: このケーキはおいしそうです。雨が降りそうです。
sentences.english: This cake looks tasty. It looks like it will rain.

sentences.japanese: このケーキはおいしそうです。
sentences.english: This cake looks delicious.
sentences.nuanceNote: Appearance そう drops the final い of the adjective; compare hearsay おいしいそうです.

sentences.japanese: 空が暗くなってきました。雨が降りそうです。
sentences.english: The sky has become dark. It looks as if it will rain.
sentences.nuanceNote: Verb stem + そう predicts an event from signs, rather than reporting what someone said.

sentences.japanese: この方法はよさそうです。問題もなさそうです。
sentences.english: This method looks good. There do not seem to be any problems either.
sentences.nuanceNote: いい→よさそう and ない→なさそう are special forms; do not use いそう for good.

sentences.japanese: 漢字が難しくて、新聞をすらすら読むことができません（読めません）。
sentences.english: The kanji are difficult, so I cannot read the newspaper smoothly.
sentences.nuanceNote: 読む (U-verb) becomes 読める in potential form (読めません).

sentences.japanese: 以前は泳げませんでしたが、今は一キロ泳げます。
sentences.english: Previously I could not swim, but now I can swim one kilometer.
sentences.useLabel: Potential verb with が particle flip
sentences.nuanceNote: Potential verbs commonly take が instead of を for the object of ability.

sentences.japanese: この図書館では、誰でも無料で本を借りることができます。
sentences.english: In this library, anyone can borrow books for free.
sentences.nuanceNote: 〜ことができる expresses circumstantial permission or institutional feasibility.

quiz.question: このケーキは甘くてとても美味し（　　）ですね。
quiz.translation: This cake looks very delicious, doesn't it?
quiz.grammarFocus: Conjecture 〜そう (Visual Impression)
quiz.ruleHint: い-adjective stem (drop い) + そう; 美味しい becomes 美味しそう.

explanations.reason: Correct! い-adjective stem (美味し) + そう denotes visual appearance ('looks delicious').
Incorrect. らしい attaches to dictionary form (美味しいらしい) and denotes hearsay/typicality.
Incorrect. ように/ようだ requires plain form (美味しいようだ).
Incorrect. みたい attaches to plain form (美味しいみたい).

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: Genki II: Potential Verbs (可能形) Matrix (Lesson 13)
table.subtitle: Expressing ability and situational possibility ("can do").

rows.label: Group 2: Ru-Verbs
cells: 食べる, 見る, 起きる
食べられる, 見られる, 起きられる (Drop る, attach られる)
Direct object particle を shifts to が: 漢字が読める, 日本語が話せる
Colloquial "ra-nuki" (ら抜き): 食べれる, 見れる (frequent in spoken Japanese, but avoid on formal JLPT!)
rows.note: Identical form to passive; context disambiguates.

rows.label: Group 1: U-Verbs
cells: 行く, 飲む, 話す, 待つ, 泳ぐ
行ける, 飲める, 話せる, 待てる, 泳げる (Shift final -u sound to -e sound and add る)
All potential verbs conjugate as Group 2 (Ichidan) verbs once transformed: 話せる → 話せます / 話せない
Do NOT add られる to U-verbs! 行く becomes 行ける, NOT 行かられる ❌!
rows.note: Clean shift: -u → -eru.

rows.label: Group 3: Irregular
cells: する (to do), 来る (くる, to come)
する → できる, 来る → こられる (来られる)
Particle shift: 運転ができる (Can drive), 日本語ができる (Can speak Japanese)
Note the reading of 来 changes to "ko": こられる (NOT ちられる ❌).
rows.note: する completely transforms into the independent potential verb できる.

title: 期間に回数
meaning: Frequency within a period.
connection: (Period) に (Frequency: 〜回) | (Period) に (Duration: 〜時間)
nuance: Framework for expressing the frequency of events or duration of activities over a period of time: (period) に (frequency / duration). Examples: 一週間に三回 (three times a week), 一日に三時間 (three hours a day), 一か月に三日か四日 (three or four days a month). Question pattern: (period) に何回 [V] ますか (e.g. 一週間に何回髪を洗いますか: How many times a week do you wash your hair?).
keyTakeaway: (period) に (frequency / duration) = [frequency] per [period] (e.g. 一週間に三回: 3 times a week; 一日に一時間: 1 hour a day).

sentences.japanese: 週に三回、日本語を練習しています。
sentences.english: I practice Japanese three times a week.

sentences.japanese: 一週間に三回、泳いでいます。
sentences.english: I swim three times a week.
sentences.nuanceNote: The period takes に before the number of occurrences.

sentences.japanese: 二日に一回、花に水をやります。
sentences.english: I water the flowers once every two days.
sentences.nuanceNote: 二日に一回 gives a repeated interval, not two occurrences every day.

quiz.question: 私は一週間に（　　）プールで泳ぎます。
quiz.translation: I swim at the pool twice a week.
quiz.grammarFocus: Frequency per Time Period (〜に〜回)
quiz.ruleHint: Time frame + に + Frequency counter (一週間に二回).

explanations.reason: Correct! Frequency counter attaches directly following the timeframe: 一週間に二回.
Incorrect. Frequency counter does not take particle に.
Incorrect. で specifies total count or cost, not recurrent rate.
Incorrect. を marks direct objects, not rate of occurrence.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 30). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: ほしい (Expressing Desire for an Object: Want Something)
meaning: Expresses first-person desire to possess a concrete object or commodity: [Item] が ほしい ('I want [Item]').
connection: Noun が ほしい / ほしくない / ほしかった | Noun を ほしがっている (third person)
nuance: ほしい means "(I) want (something)", expressing desire to possess a tangible or intangible entity. Conjugation: ほしい inflects identically to an い-adjective: ほしい、ほしくない、ほしかった、ほしくなかった. Particle: The object of desire is standardly marked with が (いい成績がほしいです). In negative sentences, contrastive は is also common (プレゼントはほしくないです). FIRST-PERSON RESTRICTION: Like 〜たい (Lesson 11), bare ほしい describes only the speaker's desires (or the listener in questions: プレゼントがほしいですか). It CANNOT describe third-person desires directly (*メアリーさんは車がほしいです is wrong). To describe third-person desires: (1) Quotation: 〜と言っていました (ヤスミンさんは新しいスマホがほしいと言っていました). (2) Guess / Probability: 〜でしょう / 〜かもしれません (アミさんはぬいぐるみがほしくないでしょう). (3) Derived verb ほしがる (usually 〜ほしがっている): conjugates as an u-verb. CRITICAL PARTICLE RULE: ほしがる takes ONLY particle を, NEVER が (友達をほしがっている; strictly prohibited: *友達がほしがっている). SEMANTIC BOUNDARY: Core meaning is desire to possess an object. To express desire to perform an action, use V-たい (昼ご飯を食べたい, not *昼ご飯がほしい).
keyTakeaway: Noun が ほしい (I want [object]; conjugates like い-adj). First-person only. Third person: 〜と言っていた, 〜かもしれない, or 〜ほしがっている (takes ONLY を, never が). Action wish: use V-たい.

sentences.japanese: 今度の誕生日に、新しいノートパソコンがほしいです。
sentences.english: For my upcoming birthday, I want a new laptop computer.
sentences.literal: This-time's birthday-on, new laptop want is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Desire for material item marked with が.

sentences.japanese: 新しい辞書がほしいです。
sentences.english: I want a new dictionary.
sentences.nuanceNote: ほしい describes desire for a thing; the basic target is marked with が.

sentences.japanese: 車がほしいですが、今は買いたくありません。
sentences.english: I want a car, but I do not want to buy one now.
sentences.nuanceNote: ほしい expresses wanting the thing; たい expresses wanting to perform an action. The two need not coincide.

quiz.question: 今は何も（　　）くないです。ただゆっくり休みたいです。
quiz.translation: Right now I don't want anything. I just want to rest leisurely.
quiz.grammarFocus: Negative of ほしい (ほしくない)
quiz.ruleHint: [Item] が ほしいです (Conjugates 100% as an い-adjective: ほしくない, ほしかった)

explanations.reason: Correct! ほしい drops い + くない = ほしくない (Nothing wanted).
Incorrect. ほしいくない retains the extra い.
Incorrect. ほしく is already adverbial; adding another くない is invalid.
Incorrect. ほしな is ungrammatical.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 46 (PDF p. 54). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜かもしれない / 〜かもしんない (Epistemic Possibility: Might / May)
meaning: States that something is possible without guaranteeing it: 'might / may be X' (roughly 50% or less certainty).
connection: Short form (V / い-adj) + かもしれません | な-adj stem + かもしれません (no だ!) | Noun + かもしれません (no だ!)
nuance: 〜かもしれない / 〜かもしんない expresses epistemic possibility: "maybe / might / may". It indicates a possibility where the speaker is less certain than with 〜でしょう. Casual contractions: 〜かもしんない or simply 〜かも (very common in spoken Japanese). Formation: Attaches to the short forms of predicates in both affirmative and negative, present and past (雨が降るかもしれない, よくないかもしれない, 背が高いかもしれない, いじめっ子だったかもしれない). CRITICAL COPULA BAN: For nouns and な-adjectives in the present tense affirmative, だ IS DROPPED! Attach かもしれません directly without だ: e.g. ウダイさんはインド人かもしれない (strictly prohibited: *インド人だかもしれない). e.g. 山下先生は犬が嫌いかもしれない (strictly prohibited: *嫌いだかもしれない).
keyTakeaway: Short form + かもしれません (might / may). Casual: 〜かもしんない / 〜かも. CRITICAL RULE: Nouns & な-adj in present affirmative drop だ completely (インド人かもしれない, never *だかもしれない).

sentences.japanese: 午後から天気が崩れて、雨が降るかもしれません。
sentences.english: The weather may deteriorate from the afternoon, and it might rain.
sentences.literal: Afternoon-from weather deteriorate, rain fall might.
sentences.nuanceNote: Epistemic possibility of rain.

sentences.japanese: 明日は雪が降るかもしれません。
sentences.english: It may snow tomorrow.
sentences.nuanceNote: かもしれない leaves open a possibility; it does not encode a fixed numerical probability.

sentences.japanese: 今日は休みかもしれません。昨日も休みだったかもしれません。
sentences.english: It may be closed today. It may have been closed yesterday too.
sentences.nuanceNote: Non-past affirmative nouns omit だ before かもしれない; a past predicate retains だった.

quiz.question: 山田さんは道に迷っ（　　）かもしれません。
quiz.translation: Yamada may have got lost.
quiz.grammarFocus: Past conjecture with 〜かもしれない
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + かもしれません | Noun / な-adj attach directly without だ!

explanations.reason: 迷った is a past predicate before かもしれません.
The te-form does not directly connect to かもしれません.
たり needs a different continuation.
のに is a conjunction and does not form this possibility predicate.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 46 (PDF p. 54). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜たらどうですか (Casual Advice / Suggestion: Why Don't You?)
meaning: Offers a suggestion or recommendation to the listener: 'Why don't you try X? / How about doing X?'.
connection: V-た形 + らどうですか | Casual: V-た形 + らどう？ / 〜たら？
nuance: 〜たらどうですか conveys advice or a recommendation: "Why don't you...? / How about doing...?". Formation: Attaches to the past tense affirmative short form of a verb: V-た + らどうですか (薬を飲んだらどうですか, もっと勉強したらどうですか). Casual variants: shortened to 〜たらどう？ or simply 〜たら？ in casual speech. PRAGMATIC USE & INVITATION CONVENTION: 〜たらどうですか focuses on advising the other person what they should do. Consequently, standard Japanese etiquette avoids using it to invite someone to do an activity together with the speaker (for invitations to join the speaker, use 〜ませんか or 〜ましょうか instead of 〜たらどうですか). It can also carry a critical or pushy tone if unsolicited, so it is best used when advice is sought.
keyTakeaway: V-た + らどうですか (Why don't you...?; advice). Can carry critical tone if unsolicited. Avoid for mutual invitations (use 〜ませんか / 〜ましょうか instead).

sentences.japanese: 頭が痛いなら、無理をしないで薬を飲んで寝たらどうですか。
sentences.english: If you have a headache, why don't you stop overworking, take medicine, and sleep?
sentences.literal: Head hurts if, overwork do-not medicine take slept-if how is?
sentences.nuanceNote: Sympathetic peer recommendation.

sentences.japanese: 分からないなら、先生に聞いてみたらどうですか。
sentences.english: If you do not understand, why not try asking your teacher?
sentences.nuanceNote: Vたらどう suggests a possible solution; it does not assert that the action already happened.

sentences.japanese: 疲れているなら、今日は早く寝たらどう。
sentences.english: If you are tired, why not go to bed early today?
sentences.nuanceNote: The same construction can sound caring or critical depending on tone and relationship.

quiz.question: 分からない単語があるなら、辞書で（　　）たらどうですか。
quiz.translation: If there are vocabulary words you don't understand, why don't you look them up in a dictionary?
quiz.grammarFocus: Advice formula 〜たらどうですか
quiz.ruleHint: V-た + らどうですか

explanations.reason: Correct! 調べる (Ru-verb) past form is 調べた + らどうですか (調べたらどうですか).
Incorrect. 調べる is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 調べて is te-form.
調べた plus the supplied たら would produce 調べたたら; the blank must contain 調べ.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 46 (PDF p. 54). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: あげる・くれる・もらう
meaning: Giving and receiving objects.
connection: (giver) は (recipient) に [Item] を あげる / くれる | (recipient) は (giver) に/から [Item] を もらう
nuance: Japanese distinguishes transactions based on the direction of giving relative to psychological distance: (1) あげる: Used when the transaction moves away from the center (speaker) or stays away among others: I give to you; I give to others; You give to others; Third party gives to third party. Formula: (giver) は/が (recipient) に [Thing] を あげる. (2) くれる: Used when the transaction moves toward the center (toward "me" or my in-group/family): Somebody gives me; You give me; Somebody gives to my family member (Footnote 2: 大統領が妹に手紙をくれました). Formula: (giver) は/が (recipient: 私/in-group) に [Thing] を くれる. (3) もらう: Recipient is the grammatical subject who receives from a giver: Formula: (recipient) は/が (giver) に/から [Thing] を もらう. Perspective constraint: もらう implies feeling closer to the recipient than the giver; it is not used when the transaction is outbound from the speaker.
keyTakeaway: あげる = Outward/neutral giving (I->you, I->others, others->others). くれる = Inward giving to me/my family. もらう = Subject receives from giver (recipient は giver に/から もらう).

sentences.japanese: 妹が私に本をくれました。私は妹に本をもらいました。
sentences.english: My younger sister gave me a book. I received a book from her.

sentences.japanese: 私は友達に本をあげました。
sentences.english: I gave a book to a friend.
sentences.nuanceNote: The giver is the subject and the receiver takes に. あげる views the gift as moving away from the speaker's side.

sentences.japanese: 友達が私に本をくれました。
sentences.english: A friend gave me a book.
sentences.nuanceNote: くれる presents the giver's action toward the speaker or their side.

sentences.japanese: 私は友達に本をもらいました。
sentences.english: I received a book from a friend.
sentences.nuanceNote: The receiver is the subject with もらう; this describes the same transfer from another viewpoint.

quiz.question: 誕生日に母が素敵なセーターを（　　）。
quiz.translation: On my birthday, my mother gave me a lovely sweater.
quiz.grammarFocus: くれる (Inward Giving to Speaker)
quiz.ruleHint: Someone else gives to the speaker / speaker's in-group takes くれる; speaker gives takes あげる.

explanations.reason: Correct! 母 (giver) giving to me (implicit recipient) requires くれました.
Incorrect. あげる denotes outward giving from the speaker to another.
Incorrect. もらう requires the recipient as grammatical subject (私は母にセーターをもらいました).
Incorrect. やる is used downward to pets or plants, not from mother to speaker.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 46 (PDF p. 54). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: Giving & Receiving Triad (授受動詞): あげる vs くれる vs もらう
table.subtitle: Tracks social perspective, insider/outsider psychology, and debt of gratitude.

rows.label: X は Y に あげる / 〜てあげる
cells: X (Giver / "I" or insider)
From Speaker/Insider OUTWARD to Receiver
差し上げる (さしあげる - Humble toward higher status)
CAUTION: Doing a favor directly to a superior with 〜てあげます can sound condescending. Avoid!
rows.note: Subject = Giver. Particle に = Receiver.

rows.label: X が 私に くれる / 〜てくれる
cells: X (Giver / Outside party)
From Outside party INWARD to Speaker / My In-Group
くださる (Honorific - Superior gave to me)
The giver is the subject. The recipient is understood from the speaker or empathy viewpoint, typically the speaker or their in-group.
rows.note: 先生が私に本をくださった (Teacher gave me a book).

rows.label: 私 は X に/から もらう / 〜てもらう
cells: 私 (Receiver / Beneficiary as Subject)
The subject receives from the giver; the subject need not be the speaker.
いただく (Humble - I humbly received from superior)
The receiver is the subject (often presented as a は-topic). The giver takes に; から is possible for receiving objects, but not freely interchangeable with に in てもらう.
rows.note: 田中さんに手伝ってもらった (I got Tanaka-san to help me).

title: 数量＋も・しか〜ない
meaning: A surprisingly large amount or a restricted amount.
connection: [Number] + も (large quantity) | [Number] + しか + 否定形 (scarce quantity)
nuance: Modifying quantities to express surprising abundance or lamented scarcity: (1) Number + も: "As many as..." Expresses that the quantity is unexpectedly large or impressive: 母は猫を三匹も飼っている (My mother owns as many as three cats!); 二十人も来ました (As many as 20 people came). (2) Number + しか + Negative verb: "Only / as few as..." Expresses that the quantity is insufficient or surprisingly small: 本を一冊しか持っていません (I have only one book); 二台しかありません (There are only two computers). Contrast with だけ: だけ means "just that many (neutral / sufficient)" and can take affirmative verbs; しか expresses scarcity and STRICTLY REQUIRES a negative verb.
keyTakeaway: [Number] + も + affirmative = "as many as" (surprising abundance). [Number] + しか + negative = "only / as few as" (lamented scarcity; strictly requires negative verb).

sentences.japanese: 一時間も待ちました。お金は五百円しかありません。
sentences.english: I waited a whole hour. I have only five hundred yen.

sentences.japanese: 昨日は十時間も寝ました。
sentences.english: I slept as many as ten hours yesterday.
sentences.nuanceNote: Quantity + も signals that the speaker considers the amount notable or large.

sentences.japanese: 昨日は三時間しか寝ませんでした。
sentences.english: I slept only three hours yesterday.
sentences.nuanceNote: Quantity + しか pairs with a negative predicate. It excludes a larger amount in the statement.

quiz.question: 財布の中に千円（　　）ありませんから、買い物に行けません。
quiz.translation: Because I only have 1,000 yen in my wallet, I can't go shopping.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜しか…ない (Nothing But / Only with Negative)
quiz.ruleHint: しか is strictly paired with a negative predicate (ありません) to express a lamentable shortage.

explanations.reason: Correct! しか + negative verb (ありません) means 'only / nothing other than'.
Incorrect. だけ pairs with affirmative predicates (千円だけあります).
Incorrect. も with negative means 'not even / not at all', clashing with having 1,000 yen.
Incorrect. ほど denotes general approximation, not exclusive limitation.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 46 (PDF p. 54). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 意向形 (The Volitional Form: Casual Let's Do / Self-Resolve)
meaning: The casual plain equivalent of 〜ましょう: 'Let's do X!' In monologue, expresses personal determination: 'I shall do X!'.
connection: Ru: V-stem + よう | U: V (u->o) + う | くる→こよう | する→しよう | 意向形 + か (offer/suggestion)
nuance: The volitional form of a verb is the casual spoken equivalent of 〜ましょう ("Let's do / shall we?"). It is used to suggest a plan to a close friend or to express firm self-resolve. Conjugation rules: (1) Ru-verbs: drop final -ru and add -yoo (見る → 見よう, 食べる → 食べよう, 寝る → 寝よう). (2) U-verbs: drop final -u and add -oo (the final syllable shifts to the o-row of the hiragana chart + う): 行く → 行こう, 泳ぐ → 泳ごう, 話す → 話そう, 待つ → 待とう, 飲む → 飲もう, 帰る → 帰ろう, 買う → 買おう. (3) Irregular verbs: 来る (くる) → こよう; する → しよう. Questions: Volitional + か asks for the listener's opinion or makes an offer: 手伝おうか (Shall I lend you a hand?); 今度いつ会おうか (When shall we meet again?).
keyTakeaway: Ru-verbs: -yoo (食べよう). U-verbs: u -> o-row + う (行こう, 飲もう). くる→こよう, する→しよう. Casual "Let's do". Question + か: "Shall I / we?"

sentences.japanese: 今日は天気がいいから、海までドライブに行こう！
sentences.english: The weather is great today, so let's go for a drive to the beach!
sentences.literal: Today weather good since, beach-to drive-to let's-go!
sentences.nuanceNote: Casual peer invitation.

sentences.japanese: 一緒に帰ろう。
sentences.english: Let's go home together.
sentences.nuanceNote: 帰る is an u-verb: 帰ろう. The volitional can invite another person to join.

sentences.japanese: よし、もう一度やってみよう。
sentences.english: All right, I will try once more.
sentences.nuanceNote: The volitional can express the speaker's resolve without inviting anyone else.

quiz.question: 少し休もう。これは「休みましょう」の（　　）形です。
quiz.translation: Let us rest a little. Which form of rest is 休もう?
quiz.grammarFocus: U-verb volitional form 休もう
quiz.ruleHint: Ru-verbs: drop る + よう (食べよう) | U-verbs: change final -u to -ou (行こう, 飲もう) | する→しよう, くる→こよう

explanations.reason: 休もう is the plain volitional form.
The passive is 休まれる, not 休もう.
The plain negative is 休まない.
The plain past is 休んだ.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 70 (PDF p. 78). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: Genki II: Volitional Form (意向形 / 意志形) Matrix (Lesson 15)
table.subtitle: Casual "Let's do" (~ましょう) and ongoing personal intentions (~と思っています).

rows.label: Group 2: Ru-Verbs
cells: 食べる, 見る, 起きる
食べよう, 見よう, 起きよう (Drop る, attach よう)
1. Casual invitation: 一緒に行こう (Let's go together!)
rows.note: Casual equivalent of 〜ましょう.

rows.label: Group 1: U-Verbs
cells: 行く, 飲む, 話す, 買う, 待つ
行こう, 飲もう, 話そう, 買おう, 待とう (Shift final -u to -o sound and elongate with う)
2. On-the-spot decision: 〜ようと思う (I think I will...)
rows.note: Elongated vowel sound: ikou, nomou, hanasou.

rows.label: Group 3: Irregular
cells: する, 来る (くる)
しよう, 来よう (こよう)
3. Ongoing firm resolve: 〜ようと思っている (I have been intending to...)
rows.note: Pronounced ko-you.

title: 意向形 + と思っている (Firm Ongoing Determination: Intending To)
meaning: Expresses an ongoing, settled determination that the speaker has been contemplating over time: 'I have been planning/intending to do X'.
connection: V-意向形 + と思っている (ongoing plan) | V-意向形 + と思う (on-the-spot decision)
nuance: Volitional form + と思っている / と思う expresses personal resolutions and intentions ("I am intending / planning to do X"). ASPECTUAL DICHOTOMY: (1) 意向形 + と思っている: Firm ongoing determination that the speaker has entertained for some time and has already decided (毎日三時間日本語を勉強しようと思っています: I have decided to study 3 hours every day). (2) 意向形 + と思う: A decision made on the spot at the moment of speaking (旅行に行こうと思います: I will go on a trip - decision made right now). CRITICAL CONTRAST: Volitional form vs Present tense before と思う: 日本の会社で働こうと思います = Intention ("I intend / resolve to work"). 日本の会社で働くと思います = Prediction ("I think they/I will be working").
keyTakeaway: 意向形 + と思っている = Ongoing firm resolution already decided. 意向形 + と思う = On-the-spot decision. Volitional = Intention; Present dictionary = Prediction.

sentences.japanese: 来年から日本企業で働こうと思っています。
sentences.english: I am planning on working at a Japanese firm starting next year.
sentences.literal: Next-year-from Japanese firm-at work-shall quote thinking-am.

tokens.word: 働こうと思っています
tokens.reading: はたらこうとおもっています

sentences.nuanceNote: Ongoing career resolution.

sentences.japanese: 来年、日本へ留学しようと思っています。
sentences.english: I intend to study abroad in Japan next year.
sentences.nuanceNote: The volitional 留学しよう makes this an intention, while と思っている presents it as an ongoing plan.

sentences.japanese: 今日は歩いて帰ろうと思います。
sentences.english: I think I will walk home today.
sentences.nuanceNote: と思います expresses an intention here; it does not prove that the decision was made at this exact second.

quiz.question: 「登る」の意向形を使います。夏休みに富士山に（　　）と思っています。
quiz.translation: Use the volitional form: I intend to climb Mount Fuji during summer vacation.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-意向形 + と思っている
quiz.ruleHint: V volitional + と思う / と思っている

explanations.reason: 登ろう is the volitional and expresses intention with と思っている.
登ると思う can report a belief, but 登る is not the requested volitional form.
登り is the polite stem, not volitional.
登った is the plain past, not volitional.

title: 連体修飾節 (Relative Clauses / Qualifying Nouns with Sentences)
meaning: Embedding an entire sentence before a noun to modify it without any relative pronoun ('The book that I bought yesterday').
connection: [V-short form] + Noun | [Subject が V-short] + Noun
nuance: Relative clauses (qualifying nouns with sentences) in Japanese precede the modified head noun directly without relative pronouns (who, which, that do not exist). Formation rules: (1) Qualifier verbs: The predicate inside the relative clause MUST be in short form (present or past, affirmative or negative: 昨日買った本, 彼女がくれた本, テーブルの上にある本, 日本で買えない本). (2) INTERNAL SUBJECT RULE: When the subject of the action appears inside the relative clause, it is marked by particle が, NEVER は! (彼女がくれた本; strictly prohibited: *彼女はくれた本). (3) Synthesis: The entire [Clause + Noun] unit functions as a single noun phrase and can take any case particle in the main clause (これは彼女がくれた本です; 父が村上春樹が書いた本をくれました).
keyTakeaway: [Sentence in short form] + Noun = Relative clause. No relative pronouns! INTERNAL SUBJECT RULE: Subject inside the qualifier clause takes が, NEVER は (彼女がくれた本).

sentences.japanese: これは私が昨日デパートで買ったセーターです。
sentences.english: This is the sweater that I bought at the department store yesterday.
sentences.literal: This topic I-subject yesterday department-store-at bought sweater is.

tokens.word: 私が昨日デパートで買った
tokens.meaning: that I bought at department store yesterday
tokens.reading: わたしがきょうデパートでかった
tokens.romaji: watashi ga kinou depaato de katta

sentences.nuanceNote: Direct noun qualification without pronouns.

sentences.japanese: これは友達が作ったケーキです。
sentences.english: This is the cake my friend made.
sentences.nuanceNote: The modifying clause goes before ケーキ; its subject takes が in this example.

sentences.japanese: 昨日会った人は医者です。
sentences.english: The person I met yesterday is a doctor.
sentences.nuanceNote: The person is understood as the one met inside 昨日会った; do not insert an English-style relative pronoun.

quiz.question: あそこに立って（　　）人は、私の高校の英語の先生です。
quiz.translation: The person standing over there is my high school English teacher.
quiz.grammarFocus: Relative clause noun modification with plain form
quiz.ruleHint: Plain modifying clause + noun; embedded subjects commonly marked with が

explanations.reason: Correct! Plain form いる modifies the head noun 人 (立っている人).
Incorrect. Polite form います cannot modify a noun directly.
Incorrect. いたの人は has unnecessary nominalizer の.
Incorrect. いまして is te-form.

title: 〜ておく
meaning: Prepare in advance or leave something in a state.
connection: V-て形 + おく / おきます / おいて / おいた | Casual: V-て形 + とく
nuance: The te-form of a verb plus the auxiliary verb おく describes an action performed in advance, in preparation for a future event or convenience ("to do something in preparation / beforehand"). Formation: V-て + おく (e.g. ホテルを予約しておく: make hotel reservations in advance; 部屋を掃除しておく: clean room beforehand). Conjugation: おく conjugates as a regular U-verb (〜ておきます、〜ておいてください、〜ておいた). SPOKEN CONTRACTION: In casual spoken Japanese, 〜ておく frequently contracts to 〜とく (予約しとく: I will reserve in advance; 買っとく: I will buy beforehand; 読んどく: I will read in advance).
keyTakeaway: V-て + おく (action performed in preparation for future). Conjugates as U-verb. Spoken casual contraction: 〜ておく → 〜とく (予約しとく, 買っとく).

sentences.japanese: 明日のために資料を読んでおきます。
sentences.english: I will read the materials in advance for tomorrow.

sentences.japanese: 旅行の前に、ホテルを予約しておきます。
sentences.english: I will reserve a hotel before the trip.
sentences.nuanceNote: ておく presents the action as preparation for a later purpose.

sentences.japanese: あとで使うので、電気はつけておいてください。
sentences.english: We will use it later, so please leave the light on.
sentences.nuanceNote: ておく can maintain a useful state rather than perform a new action immediately.

sentences.japanese: パーティーの前に、部屋を綺麗に掃除しておきます。
sentences.english: Before the party, I will clean up the room nicely in advance.
sentences.nuanceNote: Preparatory action executed specifically for the upcoming party.

sentences.japanese: 明日友達が遊びに来るので、部屋を掃除しておきました。
sentences.english: Because my friends are coming over tomorrow, I cleaned my room in advance.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-ておく denotes an action performed in preparation for a future event.

sentences.japanese: 窓を開けておいてください。部屋の空気を入れ替えたいので。
sentences.english: Please leave the window open, as I want to air out the room.
sentences.useLabel: Leaving a state as it is
sentences.nuanceNote: V-ておく can express leaving a resultant state intact for a purpose.

quiz.question: 旅行へ行く前に、新幹線の切符を（　　）おきました。
quiz.translation: Before going on the trip, I bought the Shinkansen tickets in advance.
quiz.grammarFocus: Preparation in Advance (〜ておく)
quiz.ruleHint: Verb て-form + おく expresses doing an action in advance as preparation.

explanations.reason: Correct! て-form attaches to おく: 買って + おきました.
Incorrect. Dictionary form cannot attach to おく.
Incorrect. Stem form cannot attach to おく.
Incorrect. Volitional form cannot attach to おく.

title: 〜といい (Hoping for Favorable Outcomes: I Hope That...)
meaning: Expresses hope or wish that a favorable condition will happen: 〜といいね (Hoping for listener's sake) vs 〜といいんですが (Hoping for speaker's own sake).
connection: Short present + といいんですが (self) | Short present + といいですね (listener)
nuance: 〜といい expresses hope for a favorable outcome: "I hope that [favorable event happens]". Formation: Attaches to the present tense short form of a predicate (affirmative or negative). SPEAKER VS LISTENER PRAGMATICS: (1) Hoping for oneself: Use 〜といいんですが or 〜といいんだけど (with explanatory/softening んですが) to politely express hope for oneself without sounding presumptuous (試験がやさしいといいんですが: I hope the exam will be easy). (2) Wishing for someone else: Use 〜といいですね or 〜といいね (friendly wish for the listener: いい仕事が見つかるといいですね: I hope you find a good job!).
keyTakeaway: V(short present) + といい. Wishing for oneself: 〜といいんですが (softened). Wishing for listener: 〜といいですね (friendly encouragement).

sentences.japanese: 明日の試合、晴れるといいですね。「ええ、本当に。」
sentences.english: I hope it will be sunny for tomorrow's match, don't you? 'Yes, truly.'
sentences.literal: Tomorrow's match, clear-up if good is right? Yes, really.
sentences.nuanceNote: Expressing mutual hope for good weather.

sentences.japanese: 試験に合格できるといいですね。
sentences.english: I hope you can pass the exam.
sentences.nuanceNote: Potential + といい expresses a hoped-for possibility; ですね shares the wish with the listener.

sentences.japanese: 来年また会えるといいんですが。
sentences.english: I hope we can meet again next year.
sentences.nuanceNote: んですが softens the wish; it is not a rigid first-person-only ending.

quiz.question: 合格できると（　　）ですね。
quiz.translation: I hope you pass.
quiz.grammarFocus: Hoping formula 〜といい
quiz.ruleHint: Plain non-past verb + といいですね / といいんですが

explanations.reason: といいですね expresses a hope.
よく cannot serve as the adjective predicate here.
よいに is not the required form.
いいな cannot be followed directly by ですね in this construction.
