title: 〜時（とき）の時制 (Tense Nuances in 'When' Clauses: V-る時 vs V-た時)
meaning: Tense distinctions before とき: V-る時 (Action NOT yet completed before main verb) vs V-た時 (Action ALREADY completed before main verb).
connection: V-る時 (B happens before A) | V-た時 (A completed before B) | な-adj + な時 | Noun + の時
nuance: Relative tense in 時 (when) temporal clauses depends strictly on the chronological completion of Event A relative to Event B: (1) Clause A (present short) + 時、Clause B: Event B occurs BEFORE or DURING Event A (出かける時、鍵をかけました: Locked door BEFORE going out; 寝る時、電気を消します: Turn off light BEFORE going to sleep). (2) Clause A (past short) + 時、Clause B: Event A has ALREADY OCCURRED / is completed before Event B takes place (中国に行った時、お茶を買いました: Bought tea AFTER arriving in China; 疲れた時、お風呂に入ります: Take bath AFTER getting tired). (3) Ongoing background: If B occurs in the middle of ongoing action A, use V-ている時 (テレビを見ている時、電話がかかってきました). (4) Adjectives & Nouns: い-adj + 時 (寒い時); な-adj + な時 (元気な時 - keep な!); Noun + の時 (病気の時 - takes の!).
keyTakeaway: Event order controls tense: V-る時 = B occurs BEFORE/during A (出かける時鍵をかける). V-た時 = A ALREADY HAPPENED before B (中国に行った時お茶を買う). な-adj takes な時, Nouns take の時.

sentences.japanese: 出かける時、鍵をかけるのを忘れました。
sentences.english: When I was heading out, I forgot to lock the door.
sentences.literal: Head-out when, lock apply forgot.
sentences.nuanceNote: Action was in progress/prior to completing the departure.

sentences.japanese: 日本へ行くとき、空港でお土産を買いました。
sentences.english: When I was going to Japan, I bought souvenirs at the airport.
sentences.nuanceNote: Dictionary-form 行くとき commonly locates the purchase before reaching the destination.

sentences.japanese: 日本へ行ったとき、京都を訪ねました。
sentences.english: When I went to Japan, I visited Kyoto.
sentences.nuanceNote: たとき presents the trip as realized; interpret the relation to the main action in context rather than translating every た as after everything finished.

quiz.question: 旅行に行く（　　）、パスポートを確認しました。
quiz.translation: Before going on a trip, I checked my passport.
quiz.grammarFocus: Tense before とき (V-る時 prior action)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 + 時 (Prior/During) | V-た + 時 (After completion)

explanations.reason: 前に marks before the event.
前で would mark a physical action location, not this time relation.
前を does not connect this temporal clause.
前が cannot connect these clauses as written.

title: 〜てあげる・てくれる・てもらう
meaning: Describe beneficial actions from a viewpoint.
connection: V-て + あげる / くれる / もらう | [Person] のために V-てあげる
nuance: Helping verbs あげる, くれる, and もらう following the te-form of a verb describe the giving and receiving of services and favors: (1) V-てあげる: Doing something as a favor for someone else. The beneficiary keeps whatever particle the main verb calls for (妹にお金を貸してあげた, 妹を駅に連れて行ってあげた). FOOTNOTE 1 RULE: If the main verb has no slot for a person (e.g. 買い物に行く, 掃除する), use [Person] のために (ゆいのために買い物に行ってあげました). (2) V-てくれる: Someone performs a favor for the speaker (or the speaker's in-group/family). Beneficiary is usually the speaker (友だちが宿題を手伝ってくれた; 親戚がりんごを送ってくれた). (3) V-てもらう: The beneficiary subject receives, arranges for, or persuades someone to do a favor: (beneficiary) は (benefactor) に [V-て] もらう (友だちに宿題を手伝ってもらいました). Can also simply acknowledge goodwill (知らない人に漢字を読んでもらいました).
keyTakeaway: V-てあげる = do favor for others (use のために if verb lacks person slot). V-てくれる = someone does favor for me/my family. V-てもらう = subject receives favor from benefactor (に).

sentences.japanese: 友達に作文を見てもらいました。
sentences.english: I had a friend look over my composition.

sentences.japanese: 私は友達に日本語を教えてあげました。
sentences.english: I taught my friend Japanese as a favor.
sentences.nuanceNote: てあげる frames an action as benefiting someone else; directly announcing favors to a superior can sound presumptuous.

sentences.japanese: 友達が駅まで迎えに来てくれました。
sentences.english: My friend came to the station to pick me up.
sentences.useLabel: Receive a favor from the giver's viewpoint
sentences.nuanceNote: The friend is the subject; くれる presents the action as benefiting the speaker.

sentences.japanese: 私は友達に駅まで送ってもらいました。
sentences.english: I had a friend take me to the station.
sentences.useLabel: Receive a favor from the receiver's viewpoint
sentences.nuanceNote: The receiver is the subject, and に identifies the person performing the helpful action.

quiz.question: 道が分からなくて困っていたら、親切な人が駅まで（　　）くれました。
quiz.translation: When I was lost and having trouble, a kind person guided me to the station.
quiz.grammarFocus: Benefactive Favor (〜てくれる)
quiz.ruleHint: Verb て-form + くれる expresses that another party did a helpful favor for the speaker.

explanations.reason: Correct! Verb て-form (案内して) + くれました denotes receiving a kind favor.
Incorrect. Passive て-form does not pair with くれる.
Incorrect. Causative stem does not attach to くれる.
Incorrect. Past form cannot precede auxiliary くれる.

table.title: Giving & Receiving Triad (授受動詞): あげる vs くれる vs もらう
table.subtitle: Tracks social perspective, insider/outsider psychology, and debt of gratitude.

rows.label: X は Y に あげる / 〜てあげる
cells: X (Giver / "I" or insider)
From Speaker/Insider OUTWARD to Receiver
差し上げる (さしあげる - Humble toward higher status)
CAUTION: Doing a favor directly to a superior with 〜てあげます can sound condescending. Avoid!
rows.note: Subject = Giver. Particle に = Receiver.

rows.label: X が 私に くれる / 〜てくれる
cells: X (Giver / Outside party)
From Outside party INWARD to Speaker / My In-Group
くださる (Honorific - Superior gave to me)
The giver is the subject. The recipient is understood from the speaker or empathy viewpoint, typically the speaker or their in-group.
rows.note: 先生が私に本をくださった (Teacher gave me a book).

rows.label: 私 は X に/から もらう / 〜てもらう
cells: 私 (Receiver / Beneficiary as Subject)
The subject receives from the giver; the subject need not be the speaker.
いただく (Humble - I humbly received from superior)
The receiver is the subject (often presented as a は-topic). The giver takes に; から is possible for receiving objects, but not freely interchangeable with に in てもらう.
rows.note: 田中さんに手伝ってもらった (I got Tanaka-san to help me).

title: 〜ていただけませんか
meaning: Politely request a favor.
connection: V-て + いただけませんか (superiors) | V-て + くれませんか (polite) | V-て + くれない？ (casual)
nuance: Three distinct politeness tiers for asking favors in Japanese: (1) V-ていただけませんか: Most polite and deferential. Derived from potential いただける (humble receiving). Standard and appropriate when making a request of professors, supervisors, superiors, or strangers (手伝っていただけませんか: Would you kindly lend me a hand?). (2) V-てくれませんか: Polite standard. Roughly equivalent to 〜てください. Standard in host-family or casual-polite interactions (待ってくれませんか). (3) V-てくれない？ / V-て: Casual. Appropriate with close peers and family (取ってくれない？ / 取って).
keyTakeaway: Politeness hierarchy: V-ていただけませんか (most polite, for superiors/strangers) > V-てくれませんか (host family, peers in polite mode) > V-てくれない？ / V-て (casual peers).

sentences.japanese: もう一度説明していただけませんか。
sentences.english: Could you please explain it one more time?

sentences.japanese: すみませんが、この漢字の読み方を教えていただけませんか。
sentences.english: Excuse me, could you tell me how to read this kanji?
sentences.nuanceNote: The preface helps introduce the request. The verb still needs its te-form.

quiz.question: すみません、この漢字の読み方を（　　）いただけませんか。
quiz.translation: Excuse me, could you please teach me how to read this kanji?
quiz.grammarFocus: Polite Request (〜ていただけませんか)
quiz.ruleHint: Verb て-form + いただけませんか is a very polite request formula.

explanations.reason: Correct! Request formula requires verb te-form: 教えていただけませんか.
Incorrect. Dictionary form cannot attach to いただけませんか.
Incorrect. Masu-stem cannot attach to いただけませんか.
Incorrect. Passive form changes the agent of the request.

title: 〜てすみません・なくてすみません
meaning: Apologize for an action or omission.
connection: V-て + すみませんでした / ごめん | V-なくて + すみませんでした / ごめん
nuance: Apologizing for actions performed or neglected: (1) Apologizing for doing something: V-て + すみませんでした (汚い言葉を使って、すみませんでした: I am sorry for using bad language; 約束を忘れて、ごめん: Sorry I forgot our promise). (2) Apologizing for failing to do something: V-なくて + すみませんでした (take negative short form V-ない, drop final い, and add くて: 宿題を持ってこなくて、すみませんでした: Sorry for not bringing homework; 早く言わなくて、ごめん: Sorry for not telling you earlier). FOOTNOTE 8 TENSE NUANCE: すみませんでした (past) implies making a clean break from the mistake (e.g. after class: 遅刻してすみませんでした); すみません (present) is used when the problem is still ongoing (e.g. as you arrive at the classroom door: 遅刻してすみません).
keyTakeaway: Apologizing for doing: V-て + すみませんでした. Apologizing for NOT doing: V-なくて + すみませんでした. Past すみませんでした = clean break; Present すみません = ongoing problem.

sentences.japanese: 連絡が遅くなってすみません。
sentences.english: I am sorry for contacting you late.

sentences.japanese: 遅れてすみません。
sentences.english: I am sorry for being late.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vて gives the action/state for which the speaker apologizes.

sentences.japanese: 連絡しなくてすみませんでした。
sentences.english: I am sorry I did not contact you.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vなくて gives the negative cause for the apology; it differs from Vないで used for doing something without another action.

quiz.question: 約束の時間に遅れ（　　）すみませんでした。
quiz.translation: I am very sorry for being late for our appointed time.
quiz.grammarFocus: Apology for an action (〜てすみません)
quiz.ruleHint: Verb て-form + すみません expresses an apology for having done an action.

explanations.reason: Correct! 遅れて + すみませんでした apologizes for the action of being late.
Incorrect. Dictionary form (遅れる) cannot attach directly to すみません.
Incorrect. Past form cannot attach directly to すみません.
Incorrect. Conditional ば cannot attach to an apology.

title: 〜そうです (Hearsay / Quoting Reports: I Heard That / Reportedly)
meaning: Relays information obtained from external news, reports, or rumors without personal verification: 'I heard that... / Reportedly'.
connection: Short form (V / い-adj) + そうです | な-adj + だそうです | Noun + だそうです | [Source] によると
nuance: 〜そうです presents a hearsay report quoting information heard from others ("I heard that... / reportedly..."). CONTRAST WITH LESSON 13 〜そうです (Conjectural Appearance): (1) Lesson 13 appearance: attaches to bare adjective stems (おいしそう, 元気そう, いい→よさそう) and verb stems (降りそう). (2) Lesson 17 hearsay: attaches to COMPLETE SHORT FORM PREDICATES in affirmative/negative, present/past (話すそうです, 寒かったそうです). MANDATORY だ RULE: For な-adjectives and Nouns in present affirmative, mandatory だ MUST precede そうです (親切だそうです: I hear they are kind; 学生だそうです: I hear they are students! NEVER *親切そうです which means "looks kind"). INVARIANCE (Footnote 1): Hearsay そうです is robustly invariant; only 〜そうです and casual 〜そうだ are used (never *そうじゃありません or *そうでした). SOURCE MARKER: Preface with [Source] によると to specify the information source (天気予報によると: according to the weather forecast).
keyTakeaway: Short form + そうです = Hearsay ("I heard that..."). Invariant ending. MANDATORY: な-adj & Nouns take だそうです (親切だそうです; never bare stem). Source: [Source] によると.

sentences.japanese: ニュースによると、明日は関東地方で雪が降るそうです。
sentences.english: According to the news, I heard that it will snow in the Kanto region tomorrow.
sentences.literal: News according-to, tomorrow Kanto-region snow fall reportedly.
sentences.nuanceNote: Relaying journalistic weather forecast.

sentences.japanese: この店はおいしいそうです。この料理もおいしそうです。
sentences.english: I hear this restaurant is good. This dish looks tasty too.
sentences.nuanceNote: Hearsay keeps い; appearance drops it. The information source differs.

sentences.japanese: 新しい先生は親切だそうです。
sentences.english: I hear the new teacher is kind.
sentences.nuanceNote: Hearsay keeps the plain affirmative だ before そうです.

quiz.question: 田中さんの話では、新しい先生はとても（　　）そうです。
quiz.translation: According to Tanaka-san, I heard that the new teacher is very kind.
quiz.grammarFocus: Hearsay 〜そうです with な-adjective
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + そうです (Noun / な-adj non-past takes だ: 暇だそうです, 雨だそうです)

explanations.reason: Correct! Hearsay requires plain affirmative copula だ for な-adjectives: 親切だそうです.
Incorrect. 親切 without だ creates appearance/conjecture ('looks kind').
Incorrect. 親切な is noun-modifying form.
Incorrect. 親切に is adverbial.

title: 〜たら (Specific & Temporal Conditional: If / When / Once Done)
meaning: Universal conditional: 1) Hypothetical condition ('If X happens, then Y'). 2) Temporal certainty in future ('When / Once X finishes, Y will happen').
connection: V-た + ら | い-adj (drop い) + かったら | な-adj / Noun + だったら | Negative: 〜なかったら
nuance: A たら B refers to conditional dependence: Event B is realized if and when the condition in A is met. Formation: Initial た comes from the past short form of predicates: Verbs: V-た + ら (行ったら, 食べたら; negative: 行かなかったら). い-adjectives: い → かったら (寒かったら; negative: 寒くなかったら). な-adjectives & Nouns: stem + だったら (静かだったら, 学生だったら; negative: 静かじゃなかったら). SEMANTIC MODES: (1) Open condition & consequence: If A occurs, B follows (山下先生に会ったら聞きます). (2) Temporal certainty ("once / when"): When A is virtually certain, arranges sequence in time: "Once A is done, let's do B" (宿題が終わったら、遊びに行きましょう). (3) Counterfactual hypothetical: Unreal condition contrary to fact (私が猫だったら、一日中寝ているのに: If I were a cat, I'd sleep all day). CHRONOLOGICAL RESTRICTION: In A たら B, B CANNOT occur before A! B takes place at the time A comes true or later. NATURAL DEPENDENCY (Footnote 6): A たら B describes natural cause-consequence; it CANNOT express "even if A, B" (for "even if", use 〜ても).
keyTakeaway: Past short form + ら (V-たら, かったら, だったら). Means: "if" (open), "once / when" (temporal sequence), or "if ... were" (counterfactual). B cannot happen before A.

sentences.japanese: 家に帰ったら、すぐに手を洗ってうがいをしましょう。
sentences.english: Once you return home, let's wash our hands and gargle right away.
sentences.literal: Home return-once, immediately hands wash gargle let's-do.
sentences.nuanceNote: Temporal sequential conditional triggering action.

sentences.japanese: 駅に着いたら、電話してください。
sentences.english: Please call when you arrive at the station.
sentences.nuanceNote: たら can introduce a request to be carried out after the condition is met.

sentences.japanese: 家に帰ったら、誰もいませんでした。
sentences.english: When I got home, nobody was there.
sentences.nuanceNote: たら can introduce an actual past discovery, not only a hypothetical condition.

quiz.question: 東京駅に（　　）ら、私に電話をかけてください。
quiz.translation: Once you arrive at Tokyo Station, please call me.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-たら conditional connection
quiz.ruleHint: V-た + ら | い-adj かった + ら | な-adj / Noun だった + ら

explanations.reason: Correct! 着く past is 着いた + ら = 着いたら ('once you arrive').
Incorrect. 着く is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 着き is masu-stem.
Incorrect. 着いて is te-form.

table.title: The 4 Great Conditionals Decoded: と vs ば vs たら vs なら
table.subtitle: The #1 JLPT trap point across N4, N3, and N2. Never confuse them again.

rows.label: 〜と (Natural / Mechanic)
cells: Natural law, physics, mechanical trigger: "Once X happens, Y automatically follows."
Normally excludes requests and intentions in the result of a hypothetical condition.
YES ✅ (Discovered a new surprise: 窓を開けると、雪が降っていた)
For a request triggered by a future event, use a suitable たら construction. Distinguish conditional と from quotation と.
rows.note: Example: ボタンを押すと、切符が出る (Press button -> ticket dispenses).

rows.label: 〜ば (Provisional Hypothetical)
cells: Logical requirement: "Provided that X is met, Y is true."
RESTRICTED ⚠️ (Only if verb is non-action / state like ある, or subjects differ)
Not the usual form for a one-off past discovery; habitual past results are possible.
TRAP: "薬を飲めば、熱が下がった" is WRONG. Use 飲んだら.
rows.note: Classic saying: 安ければ買う (If it is cheap, I will buy it).

rows.label: 〜たら (Chronological Trigger)
cells: "Once X is completed, THEN Y happens." The most versatile conditional.
YES ✅ (Freely allows requests, intentions, invitations: 〜てください, 〜ましょう)
YES ✅ (Indicates sequential discovery in the past: 家に帰ったら、手紙があった)
SAFE HARBOR: When in doubt on volitional clauses or conversational requests, たら is king.
rows.note: Connection: Past short form (た) + ら.

rows.label: 〜なら (Contextual Topic / Advice)
cells: "If that is the case you are talking about..." Topic conditional based on listener input.
YES ✅ (Excellent for advice, recommendations: 〜がいいですよ)
Not a chronological after-marker; it can refer to a past premise.
TRAP: Time inversion! In "日本へ行くなら、カメラを買ったほうがいい", you buy the camera BEFORE going!
rows.note: Noun / Plain form + なら (no だ).

title: 〜なくてもいいです (Lack of Obligation: You Do Not Have To)
meaning: States that an action is unnecessary: 'You do not have to do X / It is fine even if you don't do X'.
connection: V-ない (drop い) + くてもいいです / くてもいい / なくていい
nuance: 〜なくてもいいです describes lack of obligation: "you do not have to / you do not need to do X". Formation: Take negative short form V-ない, drop final い, and add くていいです (V-なくてもいいです). Examples: 靴を脱がなくてもいいです (You do not need to take off your shoes); プレゼントは高くなくてもいいです (The present does not need to be expensive). Casual variants: Omit です for casual speech (〜なくてもいい), or omit も for spoken casual (〜なくていい: 来なくていいよ: You don't need to come).
keyTakeaway: V-ない (drop い) + くて + もいいです = "do not have to / need not do". Casual: 〜なくてもいい / 〜なくていい. Describes absence of obligation.

sentences.japanese: 明日は祝日ですから、朝早く起きなくてもいいですよ。
sentences.english: Since tomorrow is a national holiday, you do not have to wake up early.
sentences.literal: Tomorrow national-holiday is since, morning early wake-not-even-if good is.

tokens.word: 起きなくてもいいですよ
tokens.meaning: you don't have to wake up
tokens.reading: おきなくてもいいですよ

sentences.nuanceNote: Releasing listener from waking up early.

sentences.japanese: 明日は学校へ来なくてもいいです。
sentences.english: You do not have to come to school tomorrow.
sentences.nuanceNote: Permission not to act is different from a prohibition against acting.

sentences.japanese: 書かなくてもいいです。でも、ここに書いてはいけません。
sentences.english: You do not have to write it. But you must not write here.
sentences.nuanceNote: なくてもいい removes necessity; てはいけない forbids an action in the specified place.

quiz.question: 明日は来（　　）てもいいです。
quiz.translation: You do not have to come tomorrow.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜なくてもいい lack of obligation
quiz.ruleHint: V-ない (drop い) + くてもいいです

explanations.reason: 来ない becomes 来なくてもいい.
ないても is not the negative te-form.
なかても is not a conjugation.
なかったても is not the required form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 114 (PDF p. 122). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜って・みたいです
meaning: Casual quotation and inference/resemblance.
connection: Short form + って | Noun + みたいです | V-short form + みたいです
nuance: This grammar point covers informal quotation 〜って and resemblance/inference 〜みたいです: (1) 〜って: The informal conversational counterpart of quotation particle と and hearsay そうです ("they say / she said..."). Follows short forms directly (メアリーさんは今日忙しいって; 明日試験があるって). Also replaces と before speech verbs (〜って言っていました). (2) 〜みたいです: - Resemblance to Noun: Noun + みたいです ("looks/acts like [Noun]"; 私の父はカーネル・サンダースみたいです: My dad looks like Colonel Sanders). - Inference from Observation: Verb(short form) + みたいです ("appears to be the case / looks like"; 雨が降ったみたいです: It looks like it rained; 空いているみたいです: Looks like they are hungry). Inflects like a な-adjective (みたいだ、みたいです、みたいなNoun、みたいにVerb).
keyTakeaway: 〜って = Casual quote/hearsay (busyって, 行くって言ってた). 〜みたいです = Resemblance to noun (Nounみたい) or inference from observation (V-shortみたいです: looks like it rained).

sentences.japanese: 店は今日休みだって。だれもいないみたいです。
sentences.english: I heard the shop is closed today. It seems no one is there.

sentences.japanese: 田中さんは明日来ないって。
sentences.english: Tanaka said they are not coming tomorrow.
sentences.nuanceNote: って conveys reported content in casual speech.

sentences.japanese: 電気が消えています。誰もいないみたいです。
sentences.english: The lights are off. It looks as if nobody is there.
sentences.nuanceNote: みたい expresses an inference in this context; it is not automatically a report from another person.

sentences.japanese: この雲は動物みたいです。
sentences.english: This cloud looks like an animal.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nみたい describes resemblance; distinguish it from information-based inference.

quiz.question: 外は風が強くて、今にも雨が降り出す（　　）ですね。
quiz.translation: The wind outside is strong, and it looks like it will start raining at any moment.
quiz.grammarFocus: Colloquial Resemblance / Inference 〜みたいだ
quiz.ruleHint: Verb plain form + みたいだ denotes immediate observational inference ('looks like / seems like').

explanations.reason: Correct! 降り出す + みたい attaches directly to plain form to denote observational inference.
Incorrect. らしい denotes hearsay or typicality from external evidence.
Incorrect. そう requires stem (降り出しそう), not dictionary form 降り出す.
Incorrect. はず denotes logical expectation ('is supposed to'), clashing with sensory visual inference.

title: 〜前に・〜てから
meaning: Before and after an action.
connection: V-辞書形 + 前に (before doing) | V-て形 + から (after doing / ever since)
nuance: Expressing chronological temporal sequence between two events: (1) V-る + 前に: "Before doing A, do B". CRITICAL TENSE INVARIANCE: The verb preceding 前に is ALWAYS in the present dictionary form (V-る), regardless of whether the overall main sentence is present or past! (日本へ来る前に、日本語を勉強しました: Before I came to Japan, I studied Japanese; NEVER *来た前に). (2) V-て + から: "After doing A, do B / and then B". (勉強してから、遊びに行きました: I studied and then went out; けんさんが来てから、食べましょう: Let's eat after Ken arrives). Footnote 10: V-てから can also mean "ever since A happened": 猫が死んでから、とても寂しいです (I've been lonely ever since my cat died).
keyTakeaway: V(short present) + 前に = Before doing A, B (verb before 前に is strictly present tense!). V-て + から = After doing A, B (or "ever since A").

sentences.japanese: 出かける前に電話しました。帰ってから勉強します。
sentences.english: I called before going out. I will study after returning.

sentences.japanese: 寝る前に、歯を磨きます。
sentences.english: I brush my teeth before going to bed.
sentences.nuanceNote: Dictionary-form V前に gives a temporal relation even if the main sentence later uses past tense.

sentences.japanese: 宿題をしてから、遊びに行きます。
sentences.english: I will go out to play after doing my homework.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vてから foregrounds completing the first action before the next.

quiz.question: 食事を（　　）前に、必ず手を洗いましょう。
quiz.translation: Let's be sure to wash our hands before eating.
quiz.grammarFocus: Temporal Sequence: Verb 辞書形 + 前に
quiz.ruleHint: 〜前に is ALWAYS preceded by the non-past dictionary form, even for past events.

explanations.reason: Correct! 〜前に strictly requires non-past dictionary form: 食事をする前に.
Incorrect. Past form た cannot precede 前に (common learner error).
Incorrect. Continuous 〜ている cannot precede 前に.
Incorrect. Te-form cannot precede 前に.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 114 (PDF p. 122). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 自動詞 vs 他動詞 (Intransitive vs Transitive Verb Pairs)
meaning: Pairs of verbs distinguishing self-occurring natural phenomena (自動詞: marked with が) from deliberate actions on an object (他動詞: marked with を).
connection: Transitive: [Agent は] [Object を] V-他動詞 | Intransitive: [Subject が] V-自動詞 | Resultant state: [Subject が] V-自動詞 + ている
nuance: Japanese has paired verbs of transitivity: (1) Transitive verbs describe an agent acting upon an object (requires subject は/が and direct object を: たけしさんが電気をつけた: Takeshi turned on the light). (2) Intransitive verbs describe changes that things or people undergo without an agent explicitly mentioned (subject は/が only: 電気がついた: The light went on). 10 Essential Pairs in Genki II: 開ける (transitive: open) vs 開く (intransitive: opens); 閉める (close) vs 閉まる (closes); 入れる (put inside) vs 入る (goes inside); 出す (take out) vs 出る (goes out); つける (turn on) vs つく (goes on); 消す (turn off/extinguish) vs 消える (goes off); 壊す (break) vs 壊れる (breaks down); 汚す (make dirty) vs 汚れる (becomes dirty); 落とす (drop) vs 落ちる (drops); 沸かす (boil water) vs 沸く (water boils). ASPECTUAL DICHOTOMY WITH 〜ている: - Transitive verb + ている = ACTION IN PROGRESS (窓を開けています: in the middle of opening window). - Intransitive verb + ている = RESULTANT STATE (窓が開いています: the window is open / in an open state; 電気が消えています: the light is off).
keyTakeaway: Transitive takes を (agent acts on object). Intransitive takes が (object undergoes change). Intransitive + ている = RESULTANT STATE (窓が開いている = window is open).

sentences.japanese: 風でドアが閉まりました。寒かったので、私がドアを閉めました。
sentences.english: The door closed in the wind. Because it was cold, I deliberately closed the door.
sentences.literal: Wind-by door closed (intrans). Cold was since, I door closed (trans).
sentences.nuanceNote: Side-by-side contrast of intransitive vs transitive pairs.

sentences.japanese: 窓が開きました。私が窓を開けました。
sentences.english: The window opened. I opened the window.
sentences.nuanceNote: 開く is intransitive; 開ける takes the window as its object. Intransitive does not itself prove there was no human cause.

sentences.japanese: 電気がついています。テレビは消えています。
sentences.english: The light is on. The television is off.
sentences.nuanceNote: Intransitive ている describes resulting states rather than a continuing act of turning something on/off.

quiz.question: 部屋が暗いですね。電気を（　　）ましょう。
quiz.translation: The room is dark, isn't it? Let's turn on the lights.
quiz.grammarFocus: Transitive verb つける with direct object を
quiz.ruleHint: Entity が 自動詞 (開く, 閉まる, つく, 消える) | Agent が Object を 他動詞 (開ける, 閉める, つける, 消す)

explanations.reason: Correct! Direct object marker を requires transitive verb つける (stem つけ + ましょう).
Incorrect. つく is intransitive (電気がつく).
Incorrect. 消す means turn off.
Incorrect. 消える is intransitive turn off.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 136 (PDF p. 144). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: Genki II: Transitive vs Intransitive (他動詞 vs 自動詞) Pairs (Lesson 18)
table.subtitle: Human deliberate action with を vs Spontaneous state change with が + 〜ている.
columns: 他動詞 (Transitive: Subject + を + V)
自動詞 (Intransitive: Subject + が + V)
Resulting State: 自動詞 + 〜ている

rows.label: Open (To open)
cells: 窓を開ける (Open the window)
窓が開く (The window opens)
窓が開いている (The window is open)
rows.note: Transitive takes を; Intransitive takes が.

rows.label: Close (To close)
cells: ドアを閉める (Close the door)
ドアが閉まる (The door closes)
ドアが閉まっている (The door is closed)
rows.note: Intransitive -aru ending indicates state change.

rows.label: Turn on / Light up
cells: 電気をつける (Turn on light)
電気がつく (Light turns on)
電気がついている (Light is on)
rows.note: State: It is currently illuminated.

rows.label: Turn off / Extinguish
cells: 電気を消す (Turn off light)
電気が消える (Light goes out)
電気が消えている (Light is off)
rows.note: 消す (transitive, -su) vs 消える (intransitive, -eru).

rows.label: Drop / Fall
cells: 財布を落とす (Drop wallet)
財布が落ちる (Wallet drops/falls)
財布が落ちている (A wallet is lying dropped)
rows.note: 落とす is human action; 落ちる is spontaneous event.

rows.label: Put in / Enter
cells: 本をかばんに入れる (Put book in bag)
部屋に入る (Enter room)
かばんに本が入っている (A book is inside the bag)
rows.note: 「入る（はいる）」は一段動詞の形ですが、五段（う動詞）活用です。

rows.label: Take out / Come out
cells: ペンを出す (Take out pen)
月が出る (Moon comes out)
手紙が出ている (Letter has been sent out)
rows.note: 出す (transitive) vs 出る (intransitive).

rows.label: Break / Break down
cells: 時計を壊す (Break a clock)
時計が壊れる (Clock breaks)
時計が壊れている (Clock is broken)
rows.note: 壊れている describes existing condition of brokenness.

rows.label: Soil / Get dirty
cells: 服を汚す (Soil one's clothes)
服が汚れる (Clothes get dirty)
服が汚れている (Clothes are stained/dirty)
rows.note: Intransitive state marker.

title: 〜と (Natural Consequence & Inevitable Conditional: When / If)
meaning: States an inevitable natural consequence, physical law, or habitual fact: 'Whenever X happens, Y automatically occurs'.
connection: Short present (V / い-adj) + と | な-adj + だと | Noun + だと
nuance: Clause A (short present) + と、Clause B expresses that whenever situation A holds true, consequence B inevitably happens ("Whenever A happens, B follows / If A, naturally B"). Formation: Clause A is ALWAYS in the present tense short form (affirmative or negative: 話すと, 混むと, 降らないと). Clause B describes the natural consequence or state, which can be present or past (冬になると、風邪を引きました). Adjective outcomes in Clause B are typically framed as a transition of state using 〜くなる or 〜になる (秋になると、木が赤くなります; 夜になると、町が静かになります). CRITICAL VOLITIONAL RESTRICTION: Clause B CANNOT contain speaker requests, suggestions, commands, or volitional intentions (*話すと、カフェに行きましょう is strictly ungrammatical; use 〜たら instead).
keyTakeaway: V(short present) + と = Natural consequence ("whenever A happens, B inevitably follows"). Clause A is strictly present tense. Clause B CANNOT contain volition, requests, or commands.

sentences.japanese: このボタンを押すと、お釣りが出ます。
sentences.english: When you press this button, the change automatically comes out.
sentences.literal: This button press-when, change comes-out.
sentences.nuanceNote: Automatic mechanical consequence.

sentences.japanese: このボタンを押すと、ドアが開きます。
sentences.english: If you press this button, the door opens.
sentences.nuanceNote: Conditional と presents the mechanism's result rather than a request or decision.

sentences.japanese: 窓を開けると、雪が降っていました。
sentences.english: When I opened the window, it was snowing.
sentences.nuanceNote: Narrative と can introduce an actual discovery in the past; it is not limited to universal natural laws.

quiz.question: あの交差点を右に（　　）と、左手に大きな郵便局が見えます。
quiz.translation: When you turn right at that intersection, you will see a large post office on your left.
quiz.grammarFocus: Route guidance conditional 〜と
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-ない + と

explanations.reason: Correct! Plain non-past 曲がる connects directly to と for automatic route guidance.
Incorrect. Past 曲がった cannot connect to と for future directions.
Incorrect. 曲がって is te-form.
Incorrect. 曲がり is masu-stem.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 136 (PDF p. 144). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ばよかった (Retrospective Regret: I Should Have Done)
meaning: Expresses retrospective regret or remorse over an unfulfilled action: 'I should have done X (but unfortunately I didn't)'. Negative: 'I shouldn't have done X'.
connection: V (u->eba) + よかった (affirmative) | V-なければよかった (negative)
nuance: 〜ばよかった expresses retrospective regret: "I wish I had done... / I should have done..." (expressing regret over an alternative course of action not taken). Formation: (1) Affirmative: Drop final -u of the dictionary form and add -eba + よかった (食べる → 食べればよかった: I should have eaten; 行く → 行けばよかった; 言う → 言えばよかった). (2) Negative: Drop final い from negative short form ない and add ければ + よかった (別れる → 別れなければよかった: I should not have broken up with her; 買わない → 買わなければよかった). Regular formation: All verbs form 〜ばよかった regularly without exceptions.
keyTakeaway: Retrospective regret: Affirmative: V(u->eba) + よかった ("should have done"). Negative: V-なければよかった ("should not have done"). Regular for all verbs.

sentences.japanese: 昨夜もっと早く寝ればよかった。今日は一日中頭がぼーっとしています。
sentences.english: I should have gone to bed earlier last night. Today my head is in a daze all day long.
sentences.literal: Last-night more early slept-if was-good. Today all-day head dazed-is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Remorse over late night.

sentences.japanese: もっと早く予約すればよかったです。
sentences.english: I should have booked earlier.
sentences.nuanceNote: The speaker evaluates the unchosen action as the better choice.

sentences.japanese: あんなことを言わなければよかったです。
sentences.english: I should not have said such a thing.
sentences.nuanceNote: The negative conditional expresses regret that the action did occur.

quiz.question: こんなに雨が降るなら、傘を持って（　　）ばよかった。
quiz.translation: If it was going to rain this much, I should have brought an umbrella.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-ばよかった retrospective regret
quiz.ruleHint: V-ば + よかった (Affirmative regret: should have) | V-なければ + よかった (Negative regret: shouldn't have)

explanations.reason: Correct! 持ってくる conditional is 持ってくれば + よかった (should have brought).
Incorrect. くる is dictionary form.
Incorrect. こ is negative stem.
Incorrect. きた is past form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 136 (PDF p. 144). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てしまう
meaning: Completion or an unwanted result.
connection: V-て + しまう / しまいました / しまった | Casual: V-て → 〜ちゃう / 〜じゃう
nuance: The te-form of a verb + しまう has two interrelated aspectual meanings: (1) Thorough completion / culmination: Carrying out an action completely or finishing it to the end (本を読んでしまいました: I finished reading the whole book). (2) Regret / unintended mishap: Lack of premeditation or control over an outcome, expressing regret or dismay (電車の中にかばんを忘れてしまいました: I inadvertently left my bag on the train; 宿題を忘れて先生が怒ってしまった). FOOTNOTE 1 CONSTRAINT: V-てしまう only pairs with affirmative verbal te-forms (cannot express negated regret like *しなくてしまった). SPOKEN CONTRACTIONS: - 〜てしまう → 〜ちゃう (忘れてしまった → 忘れちゃった). - 〜でしまう → 〜じゃう (飲んでしまった → 飲んじゃった).
keyTakeaway: V-てしまう: (1) Complete culmination ("finish completely"), (2) Regrettable mishap ("unintentionally ended up doing"). Spoken casual: 〜ちゃう / 〜じゃう (忘れちゃった, 飲んじゃった).

sentences.japanese: 大切なメールを消してしまいました。
sentences.english: I accidentally deleted an important email.

sentences.japanese: この本を今日中に読んでしまいます。
sentences.english: I will finish reading this book today.
sentences.nuanceNote: てしまう can emphasize completing an action; it need not express regret.

sentences.japanese: 大切な写真を消してしまいました。
sentences.english: I accidentally deleted an important photo.
sentences.nuanceNote: Context makes the completed action regrettable. The grammar alone does not guarantee an accident.

sentences.japanese: 宿題はもうやっちゃった。
sentences.english: I have already finished the homework.
sentences.nuanceNote: てしまう can contract to ちゃう; voiced でしまう can become じゃう, as in 飲んじゃった.

quiz.question: 大切な書類を電車の中に忘れ（　　）しまいました。
quiz.translation: I regrettably left the important document behind on the train.
quiz.grammarFocus: Regrettable Completion (〜てしまう)
quiz.ruleHint: Verb て-form + しまう expresses unintentional action accompanied by regret or chagrin.

explanations.reason: Correct! 忘れて + しまいました expresses regretful accidental completion.
Incorrect. Ta-form cannot attach to しまう.
Incorrect. Dictionary form cannot attach to しまう.
Incorrect. Negative form cannot attach to しまう.

table.subtitle: Human deliberate action with を vs Spontaneous state change with が + 〜ている.
columns: 他動詞 (Transitive: Subject + を + V)
自動詞 (Intransitive: Subject + が + V)
Resulting State: 自動詞 + 〜ている

rows.label: Open (To open)
cells: 窓を開ける (Open the window)
窓が開く (The window opens)
窓が開いている (The window is open)

rows.label: Close (To close)
cells: ドアを閉める (Close the door)
ドアが閉まる (The door closes)
ドアが閉まっている (The door is closed)
rows.note: Intransitive -aru ending indicates state change.

rows.label: Turn on / Light up
cells: 電気をつける (Turn on light)
電気がつく (Light turns on)
電気がついている (Light is on)
rows.note: State: It is currently illuminated.

rows.label: Turn off / Extinguish
cells: 電気を消す (Turn off light)
電気が消える (Light goes out)
電気が消えている (Light is off)
rows.note: 消す (transitive, -su) vs 消える (intransitive, -eru).

rows.label: Drop / Fall
cells: 財布を落とす (Drop wallet)
財布が落ちる (Wallet drops/falls)
財布が落ちている (A wallet is lying dropped)
rows.note: 落とす is human action; 落ちる is spontaneous event.

rows.label: Put in / Enter
cells: 本をかばんに入れる (Put book in bag)
部屋に入る (Enter room)
かばんに本が入っている (A book is inside the bag)
rows.note: 「入る（はいる）」は一段動詞の形ですが、五段（う動詞）活用です。

rows.label: Take out / Come out
cells: ペンを出す (Take out pen)
月が出る (Moon comes out)
手紙が出ている (Letter has been sent out)
rows.note: 出す (transitive) vs 出る (intransitive).

rows.label: Break / Break down
cells: 時計を壊す (Break a clock)
時計が壊れる (Clock breaks)
時計が壊れている (Clock is broken)
rows.note: 壊れている describes existing condition of brokenness.

rows.label: Soil / Get dirty

服が汚れる (Clothes get dirty)
服が汚れている (Clothes are stained/dirty)
rows.note: Intransitive state marker.

title: 〜ながら
meaning: Do two actions at the same time.
connection: V1-stem + ながら、V2
nuance: V1 (masu-stem) + ながら、V2 connects two verbs to express that two actions are performed simultaneously by the same actor ("while doing V1, doing V2"). Focus structure: V2 is the PRIMARY action; V1 is secondary/background (音楽を聞きながら、日本語を勉強します: Studies Japanese while listening to music). SAME ACTOR CONSTRAINT: Both actions flanking ながら MUST be performed by the SAME PERSON! It cannot describe an action performed while another person does something (*メアリーが買い物をしながら、たけしが掃除した is ungrammatical; use 〜間に or 〜時 instead).
keyTakeaway: V1(masu-stem) + ながら + V2 = while doing V1, do V2. V2 is the main action. SAME ACTOR RULE: Both actions must be performed by the same person (never two different people).

sentences.japanese: 音楽を聞きながら料理します。
sentences.english: I cook while listening to music.

sentences.japanese: 音楽を聞きながら、料理をしています。
sentences.english: I am cooking while listening to music.
sentences.nuanceNote: The same person performs both actions. The final predicate is the main activity.

sentences.japanese: 料理をしながら、友達と電話で話しました。
sentences.english: I talked to a friend on the phone while cooking.
sentences.nuanceNote: Changing the final predicate changes which activity is presented as central; ながら itself does not specify a fixed priority for cooking or talking.

quiz.question: 音楽を（　　）ながら、部屋の掃除をしました。
quiz.translation: I cleaned the room while listening to music.
quiz.grammarFocus: Simultaneous Actions (Verb stem + ながら)
quiz.ruleHint: Verb ます-stem + ながら indicates performing a secondary action while focusing on the main action.

explanations.reason: Correct! Verb masu-stem (聞き) + ながら denotes simultaneous action.
Incorrect. Te-form cannot attach to ながら.
Incorrect. Dictionary form cannot attach to ながら.
Incorrect. Ta-form cannot attach to ながら.

title: 尊敬語 (Honorific Speech: Special Verbs & Regular Formulas)
meaning: Honorific verbs show respect toward the person whose action is described.
connection: Special honorific verbs OR お + V-stem + になる / ご + Noun + になる (subject は/が)
nuance: Honorific speech (尊敬語 sonkeigo) bestows honor upon, or exalts, the person performing an activity (used when speaking about superiors, teachers, customers, or guests; NEVER used to describe one's own actions). SPECIAL HONORIFIC VERBS (Genki II Table p. 164): ・行く・来る・いる → いらっしゃる (long form: いらっしゃいます; て-form: いらっしゃって) ・食べる・飲む → 召し上がる (めしあがります) ・くれる → くださる (くださいます; request imperative: ください) ・する → なさる (なさいます) ・寝る → お休みになる (おやすみになります) ・見る → ご覧になる (ごらんになります) ・言う → おっしゃる (おっしゃいます) ・〜ている → 〜ていらっしゃる (〜ていらっしゃいます) IRREGULAR CONJUGATIONS NOTE: いらっしゃる, おっしゃる, なさる, くださる conjugate irregularly in their polite long forms: they take -i instead of -ri before -masu (いらっしゃいます, おっしゃいます, なさいます, くださいます). FOOTNOTE 1 (COMPOUND VERBS): Special verbs also substitute into compound verbs ending with 来る: 持ってくる → 持っていらっしゃる, 連れてくる → 連れていらっしゃる. REGULAR HONORIFIC FORMULA (p. 165): For verbs without dedicated special forms: お + verb stem + になる (e.g. 先生は今朝の新聞をお読みになりましたか: Did the professor read this morning's paper?; お帰りになる, お話しになる). RESTRICTIONS: (1) One-syllable stem verbs (見る, 寝る, 出る) cannot use the regular お〜になる formula (special verbs ご覧になる, お休みになる must be used). (2) Suru-compound verbs use ご〜なさる or ご〜になる (ご案内になる, ご案内なさる).
keyTakeaway: 尊敬語 exalts the actions of respected subjects (teachers/clients), NEVER oneself. Special verbs: いらっしゃる, 召し上がる, おっしゃる, なさる, ご覧になる, お休みになる, くださる. Regular formula: お + V-stem + になる. Never use on 1-syllable stems.

sentences.japanese: 先生は昨日の学会で、非常に興味深い研究成果をおっしゃいました。
sentences.english: The professor stated highly intriguing research findings at yesterday's academic conference.
sentences.literal: Professor yesterday's conference-at, intriguing findings honorably-said.
sentences.nuanceNote: Elevating professor's speech act via おっしゃる.

sentences.japanese: 先生は何を召し上がりますか。
sentences.english: What will you have to eat/drink, Professor?
sentences.nuanceNote: 召し上がる honors the actor's eating/drinking; do not use it to honor yourself.

sentences.japanese: 先生はもういらっしゃいましたか。
sentences.english: Has the teacher arrived yet?
sentences.nuanceNote: いらっしゃる has the special polite stem いらっしゃい. The intended sense can be come/go/be depending on context.

quiz.question: 社長はもうお昼ご飯を（　　）ましたか。
quiz.translation: Has the company president already eaten lunch?
quiz.grammarFocus: Special honorific verb 召し上がる
quiz.ruleHint: Honorific verb; お + suitable verb stem + になる; some verbs have special forms

explanations.reason: Correct! 召し上がる is the special honorific (尊敬語) verb for 食べる/飲む.
Incorrect. いただく is humble (謙譲語) for oneself eating.
Incorrect. 参る is humble for going/coming.
Incorrect. 拝見する is humble for looking.

title: お + V-stem + ください (Polite Honorific Request: Please Graciously Do)
meaning: A graceful, courteous request formula for superiors or customers: 'Please graciously do X' (much more polite than 〜てください).
connection: お + V-stem + ください | ご + Noun + ください
nuance: お + verb stem + ください expresses a respectful request or polite advice to an honored person ("please do... graciously"). It is much more respectful and formal than the standard 〜てください, and is the standard formula used in public announcements, hospitality, reception desks, and store attendants. FORMATION: (1) Native Japanese (wago) verbs: お + verb masu-stem + ください (切符をお取りください: Please take your ticket; どうぞお入りください: Please come in; お使いください: Please use it; 少々お待ちください: Please wait a moment). (2) Sino-Japanese (kango / suru-compounds): ご + Noun + ください (ご注意ください: Please be careful / watch out; ご覧ください: Please take a look; ご案内ください; ご遠慮ください: Please refrain). RESTRICTION: Does not apply to 1-syllable stem verbs without compound stems (e.g. *お見ください is forbidden; use ご覧ください).
keyTakeaway: Respectful request / advice: Wago: お + V-stem + ください (お取りください). Suru-compounds: ご + Noun + ください (ご注意ください, ご覧ください). Formal public/business register.

sentences.japanese: 足元が滑りやすくなっておりますので、十分にお気をつけください。
sentences.english: Because the footing has become slippery, please take great care.
sentences.literal: Footing slippery become since, sufficiently take-care please.
sentences.nuanceNote: Polite safety announcement.

sentences.japanese: 少々お待ちください。
sentences.english: Please wait a moment.
sentences.nuanceNote: お + verb stem + ください makes an honorific request; not every verb takes the pattern freely.

sentences.japanese: こちらの写真をご覧ください。
sentences.english: Please look at this photograph.
sentences.nuanceNote: ご覧ください is the conventional honorific form for looking; do not invent ご見ください.

quiz.question: どうぞこちらのお席にお（　　）ください。
quiz.translation: Please graciously have a seat here in this chair.
quiz.grammarFocus: Honorific request formula お + stem + ください
quiz.ruleHint: お + V-stem + ください (Group 3 する verbs: ご + Noun + ください: ご注意ください)

explanations.reason: Correct! 腰を掛ける stem is 掛け: お掛けください (Please have a seat).
Incorrect. 掛ける is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 掛けて is te-form.
Incorrect. 掛けた is past form.

title: 〜てくれてありがとう・〜てよかった
meaning: Thank someone or express relief.
connection: V-て + くれてありがとう / くださってありがとうございました | V-てよかった / V-なくてよかった
nuance: This section encompasses two closely related expressions of gratitude and emotional relief: (1) Gratitude for Specific Favors: 〜てくれてありがとう / 〜てくださってありがとうございました. Used to thank someone for performing a specific action: ・Casual (peers, close friends, family): V-てくれてありがとう (手伝ってくれてありがとう: Thanks for helping me). ・Polite Honorific (superiors, teachers, non-intimate associates): V-てくださって、ありがとうございました (推薦状を書いてくださって、ありがとうございました: Thank you for graciously writing a recommendation letter for me). ・Negative favor ("thank you for not doing"): 〜ないでくれてありがとう / 〜ないでくださってありがとうございました. (2) Emotional Relief / Being Glad: 〜てよかった. Expresses retrospective relief or happiness that an event occurred or that an action was taken: ・Affirmative: V-てよかった (日本語を勉強してよかったです: I am glad that I studied Japanese). ・Negative: V-なくてよかった (きのう雨が降らなくてよかったです: I am glad that it did not rain yesterday; 行かなくてよかった: I am glad I did not go).
keyTakeaway: Gratitude: Casual: V-てくれてありがとう. Polite/Superior: V-てくださってありがとうございました. Relief: V-てよかった (glad it happened) vs V-なくてよかった (glad it didn't happen).

sentences.japanese: 手伝ってくれてありがとう。間に合ってよかったです。
sentences.english: Thank you for helping. I am glad we made it in time.

sentences.japanese: 手伝ってくれて、ありがとう。
sentences.english: Thank you for helping me.
sentences.nuanceNote: くれる presents the action as a benefit toward the speaker's side. A more formal thanks uses くださってありがとうございます.

sentences.japanese: 無事に着いてよかったです。
sentences.english: I am glad you arrived safely.
sentences.nuanceNote: てよかった evaluates the event positively; it does not mean that the event was morally good in every sense.

quiz.question: 忙しい時に手伝って（　　）どうもありがとうございました。
quiz.translation: Thank you very much for helping me out when I was busy.
quiz.grammarFocus: Gratitude for an Inward Favor (〜てくれてありがとう)
quiz.ruleHint: 〜てくれてありがとう expresses gratitude for an action someone performed for you.

explanations.reason: Correct! 〜てくれてありがとう thanks the other person for their kind favor toward the speaker.
Incorrect. 〜てあげてありがとう would imply thanking someone for letting the speaker do a favor.
Incorrect. もらって requires different subject construction.
Incorrect. やる is downward/condescending.

title: 〜はずです
meaning: An expectation supported by a reason.
connection: Short form predicate (+ な for な-adj, + の for Noun) + はずです
nuance: 〜はずです expresses an expectation or logical deduction based on surrounding evidence, circumstances, or common sense: "supposed to be the case / should logically happen / must be". The speaker believes something is true or likely, though lacking 100% conclusive proof (今日日曜だから、銀行は閉まっているはずです: Banks must be closed, because today is Sunday). FORMATION (Attached to Short Forms): ・Verbs: Short form (present/past, aff/neg) + はずです (届くはずです / 来ないはずです / 買ったはずです). ・い-adjectives: Short form + はずです (面白いはずです / 寒くないはずです). ・な-adjectives: な-adjective + な + はずです (元気なはずです: supposed to be healthy; 親切なはずです). ・Nouns: Noun + の + はずです (日本人のはずです: supposed to be Japanese; 休みのはずです: supposed to be off). PRAGMATIC CONSTRAINTS: (1) Cannot be used for moral duty or legal obligation (e.g. "you are supposed to obey rules" must use べき or なければならない, not はず). (2) Strong negative conviction: 〜はずがない / 〜はずはありません (cannot possibly be the case).
keyTakeaway: 〜はずです: Logical expectation based on evidence ("supposed to be / should be"). Formations: Verb-short / い-adj + はずです; な-adj + なはずです; Noun + のはずです. Cannot express moral duty.

sentences.japanese: 今日は祝日なので、銀行は休みのはずです。
sentences.english: It is a holiday today, so the bank should be closed.

sentences.japanese: 田中さんは毎日練習しているので、上手なはずです。
sentences.english: Tanaka practices every day, so I expect they are good.
sentences.nuanceNote: はず expresses an expectation supported by a premise, not direct observation or certainty beyond error.

sentences.japanese: ここに置いたはずなのに、見つかりません。
sentences.english: I am sure I put it here, but I cannot find it.
sentences.nuanceNote: はず can present a remembered/expected situation that clashes with what is observed.

quiz.question: 彼は毎日一生懸命練習していますから、明日の試合に（　　）はずです。
quiz.translation: Because he practices diligently every day, he is expected to win tomorrow's match.
quiz.grammarFocus: Objective Expectation 〜はずだ (Plain form)
quiz.ruleHint: Verb plain form + はずだ expresses strong logical confidence based on clear evidence.

explanations.reason: Correct! Dictionary form (勝つ) + はずです denotes confident expectation.
Incorrect. Masu-stem cannot attach to はず.
Incorrect. Te-form cannot attach to はず.
Incorrect. Volitional form cannot attach to はず.

title: 丁重語・謙譲語
meaning: Speak modestly and respectfully.
connection: 丁重語: 参ります / 申します / いたします | 謙譲語: お + V-stem + する / ご + Noun + する | 伺う / 差し上げる
nuance: Genki II distinguishes two types of self-humbling expressions: (1) Extra-Modest Expressions (丁重語 teichougo, pp. 184-185): Talk modestly of what you (or your in-group, family, company) do, showing deference generally to the listener. Used in self-introductions, job interviews, customer service, and announcements. Verbs: ・いる → おる (おります) ・行く・来る → 参る (まいります) ・言う → 申す (もうします) ・する → いたす (いたします) ・食べる・飲む → いただく (いただきます) ・ある → ござる (ございます) ・〜ている → 〜ておる (〜ております) ・〜です → 〜でござる (〜でございます) (2) Humble Expressions (謙譲語 kenjougo, pp. 186-187): Talk humbly of an action performed directly for or in deference to a specific honored recipient who appears in the event described. ・Regular formula (wago): お + verb stem + する (お持ちします: I will carry for you; お送りします: I will walk/drive you; お貸しします). ・Regular formula (kango suru-compounds): ご + Noun + する (ご紹介します: let us introduce to you; ご案内します: I will guide you; ご説明します: I will explain; ご連絡します). ・Special humble verbs: もらう → いただく; あげる → 差し上げる (さしあげます); 訪ねる/聞く → 伺う (うかがいます); 会う → お目にかかる (おめにかかります).
keyTakeaway: 丁重語: Modest actions exalting the listener generally (参る, 申す, いたす, おる, ござる). 謙譲語: Humble action directed toward a specific honored recipient (お+stem+する / ご+Noun+する; special: 伺う, 差し上げる, お目にかかる).

sentences.japanese: 私は田中と申します。資料をお送りします。

sentences.japanese: 資料はこちらにございます。

title: 〜ないで
meaning: Do something without doing something else.
connection: V-ない + で + Main Verb
nuance: V-ないで expresses doing something without doing X (accompanying circumstance or bypassed expected step: "without doing..."). Formation: Short present negative verb + で: V-ないで + Main Verb (昨日の夜、寝ないで、勉強しました: Last night I studied without getting any sleep; 辞書を使わないで、新聞を読みます: I read the newspaper without using a dictionary). CRITICAL TENSE CONSTRAINT (p. 188): The present tense negative form 〜ないで is used for BOTH present and past sentences! You never conjugate the 〜ないで clause into the past (*寝なかったで is completely ungrammatical). Tense is marked exclusively on the sentence-final main verb.
keyTakeaway: V-ないで: "without doing X". The present form 〜ないで is used for BOTH present and past sentences (never *なかったで). Tense is determined by the final verb.

sentences.japanese: 朝ご飯を食べないで出かけました。
sentences.english: I went out without eating breakfast.

sentences.japanese: 朝ご飯を食べないで、学校へ行きました。
sentences.english: I went to school without eating breakfast.
sentences.nuanceNote: ないで links an omitted accompanying action to the main action.

sentences.japanese: 傘を持たないで出かけました。傘がなくて困りました。
sentences.english: I went out without an umbrella. I was in trouble because I did not have one.
sentences.nuanceNote: ないで describes what was not done while leaving; なくて supplies a negative circumstance as a cause here.

quiz.question: 昨晩は歯を（　　）ないで寝てしまいました。
quiz.translation: Last night I regrettably fell asleep without brushing my teeth.
quiz.grammarFocus: Doing without doing X (Verb ない-stem + ないで)
quiz.ruleHint: Verb negative plain base + ないで indicates performing an action without doing another.

explanations.reason: Correct! Group 1 verb 磨く conjugates to negative base 磨か + ないで.
Incorrect. Masu-stem cannot attach to ないで.
Incorrect. Dictionary form cannot attach to ないで.
Incorrect. Past form cannot attach to ないで.

title: 文の中の疑問・という名前
meaning: Embed questions and name things.
connection: Embedded Wh-Q: clause + か | Embedded Yes/No: clause + かどうか | Naming: [Name] という [Noun]
nuance: This section encompasses questions embedded within larger sentences and naming constructions: (1) Embedded Questions (pp. 188-189): ・With question word (who, what, where): Short form clause + か (だれが一番上手か知りません: I don't know who is the best; 何時に始まるか教えてください: Tell me what time it starts). ・Yes/No question (whether or not): Short form clause + かどうか (あの人が学生かどうか知りません: I don't know whether that person is a student; 来るかどうか分かりません). ・Mandatory だ dropping rule: The present affirmative copula だ on な-adjectives and nouns is dropped before か and かどうか (学生かどうか, 暇かどうか; never *学生だかどうか). ・Internal subject rule: The subject of the embedded clause is marked with が, not は. (2) Name-Calling (Noun called X, p. 190): ・[Name] という [Noun] specifies the name of a person, item, song, or book (「花」という歌: a song called "Hana"; 「吾輩は猫である」という小説: a novel titled "I Am a Cat"; ポチという犬).
keyTakeaway: Embedded Qs: Wh-word + short form + か | Yes/No: short form + かどうか. The copula だ on nouns/な-adj is dropped before か/かどうか. Internal subject takes が. Naming: [Name] という [Noun].

sentences.japanese: 電車が何時に来るか分かりません。
sentences.english: I do not know what time the train comes.

sentences.japanese: 会議が何時に始まるか、知っていますか。
sentences.english: Do you know what time the meeting starts?
sentences.nuanceNote: か closes the embedded question; the final か makes the whole sentence a question about knowing.

sentences.japanese: 明日行けるかどうか、まだ分かりません。
sentences.english: I do not yet know whether I can go tomorrow.
sentences.nuanceNote: かどうか embeds a yes/no uncertainty rather than an information question with who/when.

sentences.japanese: さくらという店で昼ご飯を食べました。
sentences.english: I had lunch at a restaurant called Sakura.
sentences.nuanceNote: という connects a name to the following category noun 店.

quiz.question: 会議が何時に始まる（　　）、知っていますか。
quiz.translation: Do you know what time the meeting will start?
quiz.grammarFocus: Embedded Question with Question Word (〜か)
quiz.ruleHint: Embedded clauses with question words (何時, どこ, だれ) take 〜か; clauses without take 〜かどうか.

explanations.reason: Correct! Because 何時に is an interrogative question word, the clause closes with か.
Incorrect. かどうか is used for yes/no questions without question words ('whether or not').
Incorrect. の nominalizes the sentence but does not form an embedded interrogative.
Incorrect. と marks direct quotation rather than an embedded inquiry.

title: 〜やすい・〜にくい
meaning: Easy or difficult to do.
connection: V(masu-stem) + やすい / にくい
nuance: Attaching 〜やすい or 〜にくい to the masu-stem of a verb creates compound い-adjectives describing ease or difficulty: (1) V-stem + やすい: "easy to do / prone to doing" (この電子辞書はとても使いやすいです: This electronic dictionary is very easy to use; 読みやすい: easy to read; 分かりやすい: easy to understand; 壊れやすい: fragile / prone to breaking; 太りやすい: prone to gaining weight). (2) V-stem + にくい: "hard/difficult to do / unlikely to do" (この苦い薬は飲みにくいです: This bitter medicine is hard to swallow; 読みにくい: hard to read; 分かりにくい: hard to understand; 骨折しにくい: hard to fracture). INFLECTION: They conjugate identically to い-adjectives: ・Present: 〜やすい / 〜にくい ・Negative: 〜やすくない / 〜にくくない ・Past: 〜やすかった / 〜にくかった ・Past Negative: 〜やすくなかった / 〜にくくなかった ・Adverbial: 〜やすく / 〜にくく FOCUS CONSTRAINT: Can focus on psychological ease/difficulty, physical manageability, or statistical propensity of an object.
keyTakeaway: V-stem + やすい = easy to V / prone to V. V-stem + にくい = hard to V. Conjugates as regular い-adjectives (〜やすくない, 〜やすかった, 〜にくかった).

sentences.japanese: このペンは書きやすいです。
sentences.english: This pen is easy to write with.

sentences.japanese: このペンは書きやすいですが、細い字は書きにくいです。
sentences.english: This pen is easy to write with, but fine lettering is hard to write.
sentences.useLabel: Ease or difficulty of an action
sentences.nuanceNote: V-stem + やすい/にくい forms an い-adjective describing ease/difficulty.

sentences.japanese: このコップは割れやすいです。
sentences.english: This glass breaks easily.
sentences.nuanceNote: やすい can describe a tendency of an event to occur, not someone's conscious effort.

quiz.question: この字は薄くてとても（　　）にくいです。
quiz.translation: This lettering is faint and very difficult to read.
quiz.grammarFocus: Difficulty Suffix 〜にくい (Verb stem + にくい)
quiz.ruleHint: Verb ます-stem + やすい (easy to do) / にくい (hard to do).

explanations.reason: Correct! Verb masu-stem (読み) + にくい expresses physical or practical difficulty.
Incorrect. Dictionary form cannot attach to にくい.
Incorrect. Te-form cannot attach to にくい.
Incorrect. Ta-form cannot attach to にくい.

title: 〜てある (Transitive Verb Resultant State: Deliberately Prepared)
meaning: Describes a continuous state that resulted from someone having deliberately performed an action beforehand for a purpose: 'has been done and remains so'.
connection: [Noun が] V(transitive)-て + ある / あります
nuance: 〜てある describes a resultant state that has been brought about intentionally by someone earlier as advance preparation, and that remains currently observable ("has been done and remains ready"). FORMATION: Transitive verb in te-form + ある (レストランの予約がしてあります: A restaurant reservation has been made; 窓が開けてあります: The window has been kept open; カレンダーに予定が書いてあります: The schedule has been written on the calendar). CASE MARKING: The direct object of the original transitive verb is usually marked with が (or topicalized with は), rather than を: [Item が] V(transitive)-てある. ASPECTUAL THREE-WAY DISTINCTION: (1) Transitive + ている: Action in progress (窓を開けています: currently in the middle of opening window). (2) Intransitive + ている: Spontaneous resultant state (窓が開いています: the window is open, no agent implied). (3) Transitive + てある: Intentional resultant state (窓が開けてあります: the window has been opened and left that way on purpose).
keyTakeaway: Transitive V-て + ある = intentional resultant state ("has been done for a purpose and remains ready"). Object takes が (予約がしてある). Contrasts with intransitive + ている (開いている vs 開けてある).

sentences.japanese: 会議室の黒板に、今日の議題が書いてあります。
sentences.english: On the blackboard in the conference room, today's agenda has been written.
sentences.literal: Conference-room blackboard-on, today's agenda written-remains.

tokens.meaning: has been written and remains so

sentences.nuanceNote: Deliberately posted agenda.

sentences.japanese: 机の上に資料が並べてあります。
sentences.english: The materials have been arranged on the desk.
sentences.nuanceNote: てある indicates a resulting state from someone's deliberate arrangement.

sentences.japanese: 旅行のホテルは、もう予約してあります。
sentences.english: The hotel for the trip has already been booked.
sentences.nuanceNote: The action is presented as preparation completed for a later purpose; the agent need not be named.

quiz.question: パーティーのために、壁に綺麗な花が（　　）あります。
quiz.translation: For the party, beautiful flowers have been deliberately hung on the wall.
quiz.grammarFocus: Transitive resultant state 〜てある
quiz.ruleHint: Transitive Vて + ある; affected item often が in a state description, or を in a preparation-focused construction

explanations.reason: Correct! 飾る (to decorate) connects via te-form 飾って + あります.
Incorrect. 飾る is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 飾り is masu-stem.
Incorrect. 飾られ is passive stem.

title: 〜間に vs 〜間 (During a Moment vs Throughout the Entire Duration)
meaning: 間 presents a span during which something continues; 間に locates an event or change within that span.
connection: [V-ている / Noun の] 間に (momentary B) | [V-ている / Noun の] 間 (continuous B)
nuance: Both 〜間に and 〜間 express temporal relations during an ongoing background state A, but they differ fundamentally in aspect: (1) 〜間に (Momentary Event / In the Middle of): Event B is of short duration, beginning and ending inside the temporal span of A ("while / during"). ・[A (V-ている / Noun の)] 間に、[B (momentary action)] ・両親が日本にいる間に、京都へ連れていきたいです (I want to take my parents to Kyoto while they are in Japan). ・留守の間に友だちが来ました (A friend came while I was out). ・お風呂に入っている間に電話がありました (The phone rang while I was in the bath). (2) 〜間 (Continuous Event / Throughout the Entire Duration): Event B extends throughout the entire duration of activity A without interruption ("the whole time that / during all of"). ・[A (V-ている / Noun の)] 間、[B (continuous action/state)] ・留守の間、ずっと雨が降っていました (It rained continuously the whole time I was away). ・子供が寝ている間、本を読んでいました (I read a book the whole time the child was sleeping).
keyTakeaway: 〜間に = momentary event B occurs in the middle of ongoing state A (留守の間に友だちが来た). 〜間 = continuous event B extends throughout the entire duration of A (寝ている間、ずっと本を読んだ).

sentences.japanese: 子供が昼寝をしている間に、急いで晩ご飯の支度を済ませた。
sentences.english: While the child was taking a nap, I quickly completed the dinner preparations.
sentences.literal: Child nap doing was while-in, quickly dinner prep completed.
sentences.nuanceNote: Action finished at a moment within the child's nap window.

sentences.japanese: 母が買い物をしている間、私は車で待っていました。
sentences.english: I waited in the car while my mother was shopping.
sentences.nuanceNote: 間 presents waiting as continuing through the relevant shopping period.

sentences.japanese: 母が買い物をしている間に、友達から電話が来ました。
sentences.english: A friend called while my mother was shopping.
sentences.nuanceNote: 間に places a call within that period; it does not describe a call lasting throughout the shopping.

quiz.question: 日本に住んでいる（　　）に、一度富士山に登りたいです。
quiz.translation: I would like to climb Mount Fuji once while living in Japan.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜間に (Momentary action within time frame)
quiz.ruleHint: V dictionary/ている, い-adjective, な-adjectiveな, Nの + 間 / 間に

explanations.reason: 間に marks an event within the period.
間のに is not this pattern.
間でに incorrectly stacks the particles.

title: 受身
meaning: Describe receiving an action.
connection: Ru: -rareru | U: -areru | くる→こられる | する→される | [Victim は] [Agent に] [Item を] V-passive
nuance: Passive sentences (受身文 ukemi-bun) describe an event from the perspective of the recipient/victim. In Japanese, passive is very frequently used to express adversity or inconvenience caused by someone else's action ("suffering passive" / 迷惑受身). CONJUGATION PARADIGM (pp. 210-211): ・Ru-verbs: drop -ru + rareru (食べる → 食べられる; 見る → 見られる; identical in form to potential verbs). ・U-verbs: drop final -u, add -areru (飲む → 飲まれる; 待つ → 待たれる; 使う → 使われる; distinct from potential -eru). ・Irregular: くる → こられる, する → される. Passive verbs conjugate regularly as ru-verbs (食べられた, 食べられない, etc.). THREE PASSIVE STRUCTURES: (1) Direct Passive: [Victim は] [Agent に] V-passive (私は先生に怒られました: I was scolded by the teacher). (2) Possessive / Affective Passive: [Victim は] [Agent に] [Belonging を] V-passive (私は友だちに車を使われました: A friend used my car on me; 泥棒に財布を盗まれました; 足を踏まれました). (3) Intransitive Adversity Passive: [Victim は] [Agent/Phenomenon に] V(intransitive)-passive (雨に降られました: I got rained on; 赤ちゃんに泣かれました: The baby cried on me). NEUTRAL/FAVORABLE PASSIVES (p. 212): Relatively few verbs express neutral/positive passive (誘われる: be invited; 紹介される: be introduced; 尊敬される: be respected).
keyTakeaway: Passive: Ru: -rareru, U: -areru, くる→こられる, する→される. Conjugates as ru-verb. Used heavily for adversity ("suffering passive"): [Victim は] [Villain に] ([Item を]) V-passive. Rain: 雨に降られた.

sentences.japanese: この本は多くの人に読まれています。
sentences.english: This book is read by many people.

sentences.japanese: 私は先生に褒められました。
sentences.english: I was praised by my teacher.
sentences.nuanceNote: The recipient of praise becomes the subject; に marks the person doing the praising.

sentences.japanese: 弟にケーキを食べられて、がっかりしました。
sentences.english: My younger brother ate my cake, and I was disappointed.
sentences.nuanceNote: The speaker is affected by someone else's action; the cake remains the object inside the passive construction.

sentences.japanese: この橋は百年前に建てられました。
sentences.english: This bridge was built a hundred years ago.
sentences.nuanceNote: A passive can focus on an object/event and leave the builder unnamed; it need not express suffering.

quiz.question: 満員電車の中で、見知らぬ人に足を（　　）痛かったです。
quiz.translation: On the crowded train, someone stepped on my foot, and it was painful.
quiz.grammarFocus: Adversity / Suffering Passive (被害受身)
quiz.ruleHint: Suffering passive: Victim は Culprit に Belonging を Verb-受身形.

explanations.reason: Correct! Adversity passive: 見知らぬ人に足を踏まれる = having one's foot stepped on.
Incorrect. Active voice implies the speaker stepped on someone else's foot.
Incorrect. Causative implies making someone step on the foot.
Incorrect. Masu-stem does not convey passive adversity.

table.title: The Voice Transformation Matrix: Active → Passive → Causative → Causative-Passive
table.subtitle: From direct acts to being victimized (迷惑受身) to being coerced (使役受身).

rows.label: 受身 (Passive)
cells: Action received. Includes Suffering Passive (迷惑受身) where speaker is inconvenienced.
あ-stem + れる (書く → 書かれる, 踏む → 踏まれる)
Stem + られる (食べる → 食べられる, 褒める → 褒められる)
する → される / くる → こられる
rows.note: Suffering Passive: 雨に降られた (I was rained on / inconvenienced by rain).

rows.label: 使役 (Causative)
cells: Make / Let someone do something. Expresses authority, permission, or triggering emotion.
あ-stem + せる (行く → 行かせる, 読む → 読ませる)
Stem + させる (食べる → 食べさせる)
する → させる / くる → こさせる
rows.note: Polite request: 帰らせてください (Please let me go home).

rows.label: 使役受身 (Causative-Passive)
cells: Forced to do against one's personal desire ("I was made to..."). Highly frequent in JLPT!
あ-stem + される (Contracted: 待たされる, 飲まされる, 書かされる) or せられる
Stem + させられる (食べさせられる)
する → させられる / くる → こさせられる
rows.note: Exception: Verbs ending in す (話す) cannot contract to される! Must be 話させられる.

title: 形容詞＋する・〜てほしい
meaning: Cause a state; want someone to act.
connection: い-adj(drop い) + くする | な-adj + にする | [Person に] V-てほしい / V-ないでほしい
nuance: This section encompasses two grammatical patterns: (1) Adjective + する ("to make something [adjective] / adjust deliberately", p. 215): ・い-adjectives: drop final い, add く + する (冷たくする: make cold; 安くする: make cheaper; テレビの音を小さくする: turn down TV). ・な-adjectives: add に + する (静かにする: make quiet; 部屋をきれいにする: clean the room). ・Contrast: 〜くなる / 〜になる describes natural spontaneous change ("becomes"), whereas 〜くする / 〜にする describes deliberate agentive alteration ("makes it so"). (2) 〜てほしい ("want someone else to do something", p. 215): ・[Person に] V-てほしい (私はルームメイトに部屋を掃除してほしいです: I want my roommate to clean the room; 先生に推薦状を書いてほしいです). ・Negative wish ("want someone NOT to do"): [Person に] V-ないでほしい (言わないでほしい: I want you not to tell; 来ないでほしい: I want you not to come). Alternatively: 〜てほしくない.
keyTakeaway: Adj+する: い-adj + くする / な-adj + にする = deliberately make/adjust. 〜てほしい: [Person に] V-てほしい = want someone to do. Negative wish: [Person に] V-ないでほしい.

sentences.japanese: 音を小さくしてください。少し待ってほしいです。
sentences.english: Please turn the sound down. I would like you to wait a little.

sentences.japanese: 部屋をきれいにしました。音も小さくしました。
sentences.english: I made the room clean. I also turned the sound down.
sentences.nuanceNote: な-adjectiveにする and い-adjectiveくする describe making something a certain way.

sentences.japanese: 友達に、この本を読んでほしいです。
sentences.english: I want my friend to read this book.
sentences.nuanceNote: The desired actor takes に; ほしい describes the speaker's wish, not the friend's own desire.

quiz.question: 部屋が暗いから、もっと（　　）してください。
quiz.translation: The room is dark, so please make it brighter.
quiz.grammarFocus: Adjective + する (Deliberate Change: Make X)
quiz.ruleHint: い-adjective (drop い) + くする denotes intentionally changing a state: 明るくする.

explanations.reason: Correct! い-adjective takes く before する: 明るくする (to make bright).
Incorrect. Bare adjective cannot attach to する.
Incorrect. 明るさ is a noun ('brightness') and does not form this comparative adjustment.
Incorrect. い-adjectives do not conjugate with で.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 206 (PDF p. 214). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ば (The Hypothetical Conditional: If)
meaning: States a logical or hypothetical condition: 'If X condition is met, then Y occurs'.
connection: V(u->eba) | V-なければ | い-adj(i->kereba) | な-adj/Noun + なら
nuance: The conditional 〜ば establishes Clause A as a necessary prerequisite condition that naturally leads to consequence B ("If A, then B"). CONJUGATION PARADIGM (p. 235): ・Affirmative verbs: Drop final -u, add -eba (食べる → 食べれば; 行く → 行けば; 待つ → 待てば; くる → くれば; する → すれば). ・Negative verbs: Drop -i from ない, add -ければ (行かない → 行かなければ; 食べない → 食べなければ; しない → しなければ). ・い-adjectives: Drop -i, add -ければ (高い → 高ければ; いい → よければ; 忙しくなければ). ・な-adjectives & Nouns: Add なら / であれば (暇なら; 学生なら). SEMANTIC & PRAGMATIC CONSTRAINTS (p. 236): ・Positive consequence implication: "A ば B" typically implies that fulfilling condition A ensures a good, desirable result ("If you do A, everything will be fine: この薬を飲めば大丈夫です; 先生に聞けばいいです"). ・Advice pattern: Very commonly used in advice: V-ばいい (All you have to do is V). ・Volition constraint: Like と, if clause A describes a volitional action, clause B generally cannot contain commands or requests (use 〜たら instead).
keyTakeaway: Hypothetical conditional: Affirmative: V(u->eba). Negative: V-なければ. Adj: い->ければ, な->なら. Implies positive consequence ("If A, B will turn out well"). Advice: V-ばいい.

sentences.japanese: 分からない言葉があれば、いつでも私に聞いてください。
sentences.english: If there are words you don't understand, please ask me anytime.
sentences.literal: Understand-not words have-if, anytime me-to ask please.
sentences.nuanceNote: ある is a stative verb, so requests in clause B are permitted.

sentences.japanese: 安ければ、買います。
sentences.english: If it is cheap, I will buy it.
sentences.nuanceNote: An い-adjective changes い to ければ. A stative condition can accompany the speaker's intention.

sentences.japanese: 急がなければ、間に合いません。
sentences.english: If we do not hurry, we will not make it in time.
sentences.nuanceNote: The negative conditional comes from ない→なければ.

quiz.question: 毎日練習を（　　）ば、誰でもピアノが上手に弾けるようになりますよ。
quiz.translation: If you practice every day, anyone will become able to play the piano skillfully.
quiz.grammarFocus: Verb conditional form 〜ば of する (すれば)
quiz.ruleHint: Verbs: change final -u to -e + ば (書く→書けば, 食べる→食べれば) | い-adj: drop い + ければ | な-adj / Noun: なら (ば)

explanations.reason: Correct! する irregular conditional is すれば.
Incorrect. する is dictionary form.
Incorrect. した is past form.
Incorrect. して is te-form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 228 (PDF p. 236). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜のに (Frustrated Concession: Even Though / In Spite Of)
meaning: States that contrary to natural, logical expectation, the reality turned out disappointing or perplexing: 'even though / in spite of the fact that'.
connection: Short form (+ な for な-adj/Noun) + のに、Clause B
nuance: Clause A + のに、Clause B connects two facts that hold true contrary to expectations: "Even though A, unexpectedly/frustratingly B" or "B, despite A". Unlike neutral けれども, 〜のに carries strong speaker emotion: disappointment, frustration, dissatisfaction, or surprise at an unfavorable outcome (徹夜で勉強したのに、試験が全然できませんでした: Even though I studied all night, I couldn't do well on the exam at all). FORMATION (Attached to Short Forms, pp. 236-237): ・Verbs: Short form + のに (勉強したのに / 雨が降っているのに). ・い-adjectives: Short form + のに (安いのに / 忙しいのに). ・な-adjectives: な-adj + な + のに (静かなのに / 暇なのに; mandatory な!). ・Nouns: Noun + な + のに (日曜日なのに / 学生なのに; mandatory な, identical to んだ/んです!). PRAGMATIC CONSTRAINTS: Clause B must describe an established fact; it CANNOT contain commands, invitations, or requests (*雨が降っているのに、傘を持っていきなさい is ungrammatical; must use けれども or が instead).
keyTakeaway: 〜のに: Frustrated concession ("even though A, disappointingly B"). Formations: Verbs/い-adj short form + のに; な-adj + なのに; Noun + なのに (mandatory な!). Ban on commands/requests in B.

sentences.japanese: 一生懸命勉強したのに、試験で目標の点数が取れませんでした。
sentences.english: Even though I studied with all my might, I couldn't get my target score on the exam.
sentences.literal: Utmost-effort studied even-though, exam-in target score take-could-not.
sentences.nuanceNote: Frustrated disappointment at unrewarded hard effort.

sentences.japanese: 早く出たのに、電車に間に合いませんでした。
sentences.english: Although I left early, I did not catch the train.
sentences.nuanceNote: The result contradicts the expectation that leaving early would be enough.

sentences.japanese: この店は安いのに、とてもおいしいです。
sentences.english: This restaurant is inexpensive, yet the food is very good.
sentences.nuanceNote: のに can mark a favorable surprise; frustration is not required.

quiz.question: 薬を飲んだ（　　）、頭痛が一向によくなりません。
quiz.translation: Even though I took medicine, my headache is not improving at all.
quiz.grammarFocus: Concessive emotional linker 〜のに
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + のに (Noun / な-adj non-past affirmative takes な: 好きなのに, 暇なのに)

explanations.reason: Correct! のに conveys grievance that medicine failed to work as expected.
Incorrect. ので indicates objective cause ('because I took medicine').
Incorrect. から indicates subjective cause.
Incorrect. なら is conditional.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 228 (PDF p. 236). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 使役・使役＋授受
meaning: Make, let or allow someone to do something.
connection: Ru: -saseru | U: -aseru | [Director は] [Cast に] [Item を] V-causative | V-させてください
nuance: Causative sentences (使役文 shieki-bun) describe who makes someone do something (coercion) or who lets someone do something (permission). CONJUGATION PARADIGM (p. 232): ・Ru-verbs: drop final -ru, add -saseru (食べる → 食べさせる; 見る → 見させる). ・U-verbs: drop final -u, add -aseru (行く → 行かせる; 待つ → 待たせる; 読む → 読ませる; 話す → 話させる). ・Irregular verbs: くる → こさせる, する → させる. Causative verbs conjugate regularly as ru-verbs (食べさせた, 食べさせない, etc.). SENTENCE STRUCTURE & CASE MARKING: (1) Transitive verbs: [Director は] [Cast に] [Item を] V-causative. (To avoid double-wo, the cast is strictly marked with に: お母さんは子供に野菜を食べさせた: The mother made/let her child eat vegetables). (2) Intransitive verbs: [Director は] [Cast を / に] V-causative. (Cast takes を for coercive forced action: お父さんは子供を走らせた; Cast takes に for permissive action: お父さんは子供に行かせた). CAUSATIVE + BENEFACTIVE (pp. 233-234): Adding くれる / あげる unambiguously signals "let/allow": ・[Director は] [Cast に] V-させてくれる (The director allows me to do). ・Humble permission request: V-させてください / させていただけないでしょうか (Please allow me to do: 私に自己紹介をさせてください: Please let me introduce myself; 今日は早く帰らせてください: Please let me go home early today).
keyTakeaway: Causative: Ru: -saseru, U: -aseru, くる→こさせる, する→させる. Dual meaning: make do (coercion) vs let do (permission). Transitive verbs: cast takes に (avoid double-wo). Permission request: V-させてください.

sentences.japanese: 先生が私に発表させてくれました。
sentences.english: The teacher let me give a presentation.

sentences.japanese: 先生は学生に作文を書かせました。
sentences.english: The teacher made the students write an essay.
sentences.nuanceNote: The teacher is the causer; the students perform the writing.

sentences.japanese: 母は私を旅行に行かせてくれました。
sentences.english: My mother let me go on a trip.
sentences.nuanceNote: Causative + くれる presents permission as a benefit to the speaker, rather than coercion.

sentences.japanese: 少し考えさせてください。
sentences.english: Please let me think for a while.
sentences.nuanceNote: The speaker asks to be allowed to perform the action, not for the listener to think.

quiz.question: 母は毎日弟に野菜を（　　）。
quiz.translation: Mother makes my younger brother eat vegetables every day.
quiz.grammarFocus: Causative Form 使役形 (Make someone do)
quiz.ruleHint: Transitive causative: Director は Actor に Object を Verb-Causative (食べさせる).

explanations.reason: Correct! Group 2 verb 食べる becomes causative 食べさせる: makes him eat.
Incorrect. 食べられます is passive or potential ('can eat').
Incorrect. 食べさせられます is causative-passive ('is forced to eat').
Incorrect. 食べてもらう implies receiving a favor, which does not fit parental disciplinary direction.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 228 (PDF p. 236). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: The Voice Transformation Matrix: Active → Passive → Causative → Causative-Passive
table.subtitle: From direct acts to being victimized (迷惑受身) to being coerced (使役受身).

rows.label: 受身 (Passive)
cells: Action received. Includes Suffering Passive (迷惑受身) where speaker is inconvenienced.
あ-stem + れる (書く → 書かれる, 踏む → 踏まれる)
Stem + られる (食べる → 食べられる, 褒める → 褒められる)
する → される / くる → こられる
rows.note: Suffering Passive: 雨に降られた (I was rained on / inconvenienced by rain).

rows.label: 使役 (Causative)
cells: Make / Let someone do something. Expresses authority, permission, or triggering emotion.
あ-stem + せる (行く → 行かせる, 読む → 読ませる)
Stem + させる (食べる → 食べさせる)
する → させる / くる → こさせる
rows.note: Polite request: 帰らせてください (Please let me go home).

rows.label: 使役受身 (Causative-Passive)
cells: Forced to do against one's personal desire ("I was made to..."). Highly frequent in JLPT!
あ-stem + される (Contracted: 待たされる, 飲まされる, 書かされる) or せられる
Stem + させられる (食べさせられる)
する → させられる / くる → こさせられる
rows.note: Exception: Verbs ending in す (話す) cannot contract to される! Must be 話させられる.

title: 〜なさい
meaning: An instruction from someone with authority.
connection: V(masu-stem) + なさい
nuance: V(masu-stem) + なさい expresses a firm, authoritative command or directive ("do...!"). Formation: Attach なさい to the verb masu-stem (食べる → 食べなさい; 飲む → 飲みなさい; 勉強する → 勉強しなさい; 早く起きる → 早く起きなさい). SOCIOPRAGMATIC CONSTRAINTS (p. 234): ・Implication: Speaking down from a position of authority. ・Common usage domains: (1) Parents giving non-negotiable instructions to their children (野菜をちゃんと食べなさい: Eat your vegetables properly), (2) Teachers addressing school students, (3) Standard rubric instructions in written exam tests (次の文を読みなさい: Read the following sentence). ・Strict prohibition: NEVER use toward equals, peers, or social superiors.
keyTakeaway: V(masu-stem) + なさい: Firm, non-negotiable command ("do!"). Used by parents to children, teachers to students, or in written test instructions. Strictly prohibited toward superiors.

sentences.japanese: 名前をここに書きなさい。
sentences.english: Write your name here.

sentences.japanese: 早く寝なさい。
sentences.english: Go to bed soon.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-stem + なさい is a directive, often from an adult to a child; it is not a general respectful request to a superior.

sentences.japanese: 正しい答えを選びなさい。
sentences.english: Choose the correct answer.
sentences.nuanceNote: なさい commonly appears in exercise instructions; use the polite stem before it.

quiz.question: もう遅い時間だから、早く（　　）なさい。
quiz.translation: It is already late, so hurry up and go to sleep.
quiz.grammarFocus: Firm Parental Command 〜なさい
quiz.ruleHint: Verb ます-stem + なさい gives firm, authoritative direction (parents to children, teachers to students).

explanations.reason: Correct! Group 2 verb 寝る takes masu-stem 寝 + なさい: 寝なさい.
Incorrect. Dictionary form cannot attach to なさい.
Incorrect. Te-form cannot attach to なさい.
Incorrect. Ta-form cannot attach to なさい.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 228 (PDF p. 236). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜のような・〜のように
meaning: Resemblance modifying a noun or action.
connection: Noun + のような + Noun | Noun + のように + Verb / Adjective
nuance: Noun + のような and Noun + のように express resemblance, metaphor, or simile: "like / similar to / comparable to Noun" (pp. 237-238). FORMATION: (1) Adnominal (modifying a following Noun): ・Noun A + のような + Noun B ("Noun B like Noun A") ・メアリーさんは天使のような人です (Mary is a person like an angel). ・トヨタのような大企業 (a large corporation like Toyota). (2) Adverbial (modifying a following Verb or Adjective): ・Noun A + のように + Verb / Adjective ("verb or adj in the same way as Noun A") ・魚のように上手に泳ぐ (swims skillfully like a fish). ・孫悟空のように強い (strong like Goku). ・雪のように白い (white like snow).
keyTakeaway: Simile/Resemblance: Noun + のような + Noun (天使のような人 = angel-like person). Noun + のように + Verb/Adj (魚のように泳ぐ = swim like a fish; 雪のように白い = white like snow).

sentences.japanese: 雪のように白い花が咲いています。
sentences.english: Flowers as white as snow are blooming.

sentences.japanese: これは花のような形をしています。
sentences.english: This has a flowerlike shape.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nのような modifies the following noun 形.

sentences.japanese: 鳥のように空を飛びたいです。
sentences.english: I want to fly through the sky like a bird.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nのように modifies the action rather than a noun.

quiz.question: あの雲はまるで白い羊の（　　）ですね。
quiz.translation: That cloud looks just like a white sheep, doesn't it?
quiz.grammarFocus: Simile / Metaphor: Noun + のようだ (Like)
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + のようだ expresses figurative resemblance ('just like N').

explanations.reason: Correct! Noun + のようだ denotes figurative resemblance: 白い羊のようだ.
Incorrect. ようで is linking te-form, but sentence ends here with ね.
Incorrect. そう cannot attach after Noun + の.
Incorrect. Noun + らしい denotes typicality ('acts like a true sheep'), not metaphorical simile.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 228 (PDF p. 236). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ても / 〜でも (Concessive Conditional: Even If / Even Though)
meaning: States that even under extreme or hypothetical condition X, result Y does not change: 'Even if X happens, Y'.
connection: V-て + も | い-adj(i->kute) + も | な-adj/Noun + でも
