nuance: Clause A + ても、Clause B expresses concessive condition: "B, even if A" (B is true in spite of condition A, or B does not change regardless of A). FORMATION (pp. 256-257): ・Verbs (Affirmative): V-て + も (雨が降っても、バーベキューをします: We will have a barbecue even if it rains; 食べても). ・Verbs (Negative): V-なくて + も (行かなくてもいいです; 食べなくても). ・い-adjectives: Drop -i, add -くても (暑くても、エアコンをつけません: I won't turn on the AC even if it's hot; 高くても買います). Negative: -くなくても. ・な-adjectives & Nouns: + でも (嫌いでも食べなさい: Eat it even if you hate it; 雨でも行きます: I'll go even if it rains; 子供でも分かります). Negative: じゃなくても. CONTRAST WITH 〜たら: たら indicates an if-then dependency (雨が降ったらバーベキューをしません: If it rains, we won't BBQ), whereas ても asserts that consequence B will happen regardless (雨が降ってもバーベキューをします).
keyTakeaway: 〜ても / 〜でも: "even if A, B". Formation: V-ても / V-なくても; い-adj + くても; な-adj/Noun + でも. Expresses that consequence B holds regardless of condition A.

sentences.japanese: どんなに困難でも、私は最後まで諦めません。
sentences.english: No matter how difficult it may be, I will not give up until the very end.
sentences.literal: No-matter-how difficult even-if, I last-until give-up-not.
sentences.nuanceNote: Unshakable resolve despite hardship.

sentences.japanese: 雨が降っても、出かけます。
sentences.english: Even if it rains, I will go out.
sentences.nuanceNote: The condition does not reverse the speaker's decision.

sentences.japanese: 何度読んでも、この説明が分かりません。
sentences.english: No matter how many times I read it, I do not understand this explanation.
sentences.nuanceNote: A question-word quantity with ても generalizes across repeated attempts.

quiz.question: いくら（　　）も、答えがどうしても思い出せない。
quiz.translation: No matter how much I think, I just cannot recall the answer.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-て + も concessive conditional
quiz.ruleHint: V-て + も | い-adj くて + も | な-adj / Noun + でも

explanations.reason: Correct! 考える te-form 考えて + も forms 考えても ('even if I think').
Incorrect. 考える is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 考えた is past form.
Incorrect. 考え is masu-stem.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 250 (PDF p. 258). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ことにする vs 〜ことになる (Personal Decision vs Outside Emergence)
meaning: 〜ことにする (The speaker personally decides to do X). 〜ことになる (It has been determined by external rules, organizations, or circumstances that X will happen).
connection: V(short present) + ことにする (personal) | V(short present) + ことになる (external)
nuance: This pattern contrasts personal conscious decisions against externally emerging arrangements: (1) V(short present) + ことにする ("decide to do", p. 257): ・Describes a personal conscious choice made by the speaker (毎日ジョギングすることにしました: I have decided to jog every day; お酒をやめることにしました: I decided to quit drinking). ・Negative decision: V-ないことにする (行かないことにしました: I decided not to go). (2) V(short present) + ことになる ("it has been decided that / turns out that", p. 258): ・Describes an institutional decision, schedule, corporate assignment, or external circumstance outside one's individual agency (来月から大阪支社へ転勤することになりました: It has been decided that I will transfer to the Osaka branch; 会議が中止になることになりました: It turns out the meeting is canceled).
keyTakeaway: 〜ことにする: personal internal decision ("I decided to do"). 〜ことになる: external arrangement / institutional outcome ("it has been decided that / turns out that"). Follows short present forms.

sentences.japanese: 健康のために、毎日野菜をたくさん食べることにしました。
sentences.english: For my health, I decided to eat lots of vegetables every day.
sentences.literal: Health-for, every-day vegetables lots eat-decision made.

tokens.word: 食べることにしました
tokens.reading: たべることにしました

sentences.nuanceNote: Voluntary personal lifestyle decision.

sentences.japanese: 来年、大学院に進むことにしました。
sentences.english: I have decided to go to graduate school next year.
sentences.nuanceNote: ことにする foregrounds a decision by the actor.

sentences.japanese: 来月から新しい部署で働くことになりました。
sentences.english: It has been arranged that I will work in a new department from next month.
sentences.nuanceNote: ことになる presents the settled outcome without specifying exactly who decided it.

quiz.question: 来月から大阪の支店へ転勤する（　　）になりました。
quiz.translation: It has been arranged that I will transfer to the Osaka branch from next month.
quiz.grammarFocus: External emergence 〜ことになる
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-ない + ことにする / ことになる

explanations.reason: Correct! Official company job transfer is an outside organizational decision: 〜ことになった.
Incorrect. ものになった is nonsensical.
Incorrect. わけになった does not exist.
Incorrect. はずになった is ungrammatical.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 250 (PDF p. 258). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 使役受身
meaning: Be made to do something.
connection: Ru: -saserareru | U (non-su): -asareru | す-verbs: -aserareru | [Puppet は] [Puppet Master に] V-causative-passive
nuance: Causative-passive sentences (使役受身文 shieki-ukemi-bun) express that you were forced to do, or coerced/harassed into doing, something against your will ("made to do"). Sentence structure: [Puppet は] [Puppet Master に] [Action を] V-causative-passive (私は彼女に車を洗わされました: I was tricked by my girlfriend into washing her car; 先生に立たされました: I was made to stand by the teacher). CONJUGATION PARADIGM (pp. 254-255): ・Ru-verbs: Drop -ru, add -saserareru (食べる → 食べさせられる: made to eat; 見る → 見させられる). ・U-verbs ending in す: Drop -u, add -aserareru (話す → 話させられる; never contracts!). ・All other u-verbs (Contracted Short Form): Drop -u, add -asareru (行く → 行かされる; 待つ → 待たされる; 飲む → 飲まされる; 買う → 買わされる; 取る → 取らされる; 書く → 書かされる). ・Irregular verbs: くる → こさせられる, する → させられる. All causative-passive verbs conjugate regularly as ru-verbs (飲まされた, 飲まされない, etc.).
keyTakeaway: Causative-passive: forced to do against one's will. Ru: -saserareru. U-verbs (except す): contracted -asareru (行かされる, 待たされる, 飲まされる). Verbs in す: -aserareru (話させられる). する→させられる.

sentences.japanese: 子供の頃、毎日野菜を食べさせられました。
sentences.english: As a child I was made to eat vegetables every day.

sentences.japanese: 学生のころ、毎朝走らされました。
sentences.english: When I was a student, I was made to run every morning.
sentences.nuanceNote: 走らされる is a contracted causative-passive for a suitable u-verb; the subject is the person made to act.

sentences.japanese: 子供のころ、嫌いな野菜を食べさせられました。
sentences.english: As a child, I was made to eat vegetables I disliked.
sentences.nuanceNote: Ru-verbs use stem + させられる; do not replace it with the ordinary passive 食べられる.

sentences.japanese: みんなの前で長く話させられました。
sentences.english: I was made to speak for a long time in front of everyone.
sentences.useLabel: A contraction that is not allowed
sentences.nuanceNote: For a verb ending in す, keep 話させられる; 話される would be an ordinary passive, not this causative-passive.

quiz.question: 子供のころ、嫌いなピーマンを無理やり（　　）。
quiz.translation: When I was a child, I was forced to eat bell peppers against my will.
quiz.grammarFocus: Causative-Passive 使役受身 (Forced to do)
quiz.ruleHint: Causative-passive expresses being compelled by someone else to perform an undesirable action.

explanations.reason: Correct! Group 2 causative-passive 食べさせられる conveys being forced to eat.
Incorrect. 食べさせました is active causative (I made someone else eat).
Incorrect. 食べられました is simple passive or potential.
Incorrect. 食べてあげました means I ate it as a favor to them.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 250 (PDF p. 258). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: The Voice Transformation Matrix: Active → Passive → Causative → Causative-Passive
table.subtitle: From direct acts to being victimized (迷惑受身) to being coerced (使役受身).

rows.label: 受身 (Passive)
cells: Action received. Includes Suffering Passive (迷惑受身) where speaker is inconvenienced.
あ-stem + れる (書く → 書かれる, 踏む → 踏まれる)
Stem + られる (食べる → 食べられる, 褒める → 褒められる)
する → される / くる → こられる
rows.note: Suffering Passive: 雨に降られた (I was rained on / inconvenienced by rain).

rows.label: 使役 (Causative)
cells: Make / Let someone do something. Expresses authority, permission, or triggering emotion.
あ-stem + せる (行く → 行かせる, 読む → 読ませる)
Stem + させる (食べる → 食べさせる)
する → させる / くる → こさせる
rows.note: Polite request: 帰らせてください (Please let me go home).

rows.label: 使役受身 (Causative-Passive)
cells: Forced to do against one's personal desire ("I was made to..."). Highly frequent in JLPT!
あ-stem + される (Contracted: 待たされる, 飲まされる, 書かされる) or せられる
Stem + させられる (食べさせられる)
する → させられる / くる → こさせられる
rows.note: Exception: Verbs ending in す (話す) cannot contract to される! Must be 話させられる.

title: 〜ことにしている
meaning: Maintain a personal rule.
connection: V(short present aff/neg) + ことにしている
nuance: V(short present) + ことにしている expresses doing something as a regular habitual practice based on personal resolve: "I make it a rule to... / I always make sure to...". The speaker has made up their mind to do (or not do) something and conscientiously sticks to that resolution as a sustained personal routine (p. 258). ・Affirmative habit: 毎晩十一時までに寝ることにしています (I make it a rule to go to bed by 11 every night; 毎日野菜を食べることにしています). ・Negative habit: V-ないことにしている (お酒を飲まないことにしています: I have made this firm decision not to drink and have strictly followed it; 夜はコーヒーを飲まないことにしています).
keyTakeaway: V(short present) + ことにしている: personal ongoing policy / habitual rule ("make it a rule to do / make sure not to do"). Based on self-imposed discipline.

sentences.japanese: 寝る前にスマホを見ないことにしています。
sentences.english: I make it a rule not to look at my phone before bed.

sentences.japanese: 毎朝、新聞を読むことにしています。
sentences.english: I make it a rule to read the newspaper every morning.
sentences.nuanceNote: ことにしている describes a maintained chosen practice, not just a plan for one future occasion.

sentences.japanese: 寝る前はスマートフォンを見ないことにしています。
sentences.english: I make it a rule not to look at my phone before bed.
sentences.nuanceNote: The negative clause specifies what the actor has decided to avoid.

quiz.question: 健康のために、毎晩十時前には寝る（　　）にしています。
quiz.translation: For my health, I make it a personal rule to go to bed before ten every night.
quiz.grammarFocus: Maintained Personal Habit (〜ことにしている)
quiz.ruleHint: Verb 辞書形 / ない形 + ことにしている expresses a conscious, self-determined habit or discipline.

explanations.reason: Correct! 〜ことにしている denotes an ongoing self-imposed personal rule.
Incorrect. 〜ものにしている is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. 〜わけにしている is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. 〜ところにしている is ungrammatical.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 250 (PDF p. 258). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜まで・〜方
meaning: Until a boundary; how to do something.
connection: V(short present affirmative) + まで | [Noun の] V(masu-stem) + 方
nuance: This section encompasses temporal boundary marking with 〜まで and method nominalization with 〜方: (1) 〜まで ("until", pp. 258-259): ・Clause A (short present affirmative) + まで、Clause B: Describes an action/state B that continues up to the moment change A coincides with its end. ・STRICT TENSE CONSTRAINT: The verb in clause A is always in the short present affirmative form, even if the entire sentence describes a past event (雨がやむまで、カフェで待ちました: I waited at the café until the rain stopped; never *やんだまで). ・Contrast with までに: まで = continuous duration until A; までに = deadline by which action occurs. (2) 〜方（かた） ("the way of doing / how to do", p. 259): ・V(masu-stem) + 方 forms a compound noun denoting method (泳ぎ方: how to swim; 使い方: how to use; 考え方: way of thinking; 読み方: way of reading). ・Suru-compounds: [Noun の] し方 (勉強の仕方: how to study; 運転の仕方: how to drive). ・SYNTACTIC PARTICLES RULE: Any noun originally marked with object particles (を, に, で) is obligatorily marked with の before 〜方 (漢字を書く → 漢字の書き方; ソフトを使う → ソフトの使い方; never *漢字を書き方).
keyTakeaway: 〜まで = until (verb before まで is strictly short present affirmative: やむまで待った). 〜方 = way of doing (V-stem + 方; object takes の: 漢字の書き方, 使い方).

sentences.japanese: 雨がやむまで待ちます。この字の読み方を教えてください。
sentences.english: I will wait until the rain stops. Please tell me how to read this character.

sentences.japanese: 五時まで待ちます。五時までに来てください。
sentences.english: I will wait until five. Please come by five.
sentences.nuanceNote: まで gives the endpoint of continuing waiting; までに gives a deadline for arriving.

sentences.japanese: この漢字の読み方を教えてください。
sentences.english: Please tell me how to read this kanji.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-stem + 方 forms a noun meaning the way to do something. The original object becomes a の modifier in この漢字の読み方.

quiz.question: レポートは明日の午後五時（　　）提出してください。
quiz.translation: Please submit your report by 5:00 PM tomorrow.
quiz.grammarFocus: Deadline: 〜までに (By the time)
quiz.ruleHint: 〜まで indicates continuous action lasting until a point; 〜までに marks a deadline by which a single action must finish.

explanations.reason: Correct! 〜までに marks a one-time deadline for completion: 五時までに提出する.
Incorrect. 〜まで requires continuous action (五時まで待つ), not one-off instantaneous actions like 提出する.
Incorrect. から means 'starting from'.
Incorrect. で marks duration/means, not a strict clock deadline.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 250 (PDF p. 258). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜うちに (While State Lasts / Before Opportunity Slips)
meaning: While a favorable situation or continuous condition persists, take action before the window of opportunity closes.
connection: Noun + の / な-adj + な / い-adj / Verb (辞書形/ている/ない) + うちに、[Volitional Action]
nuance: 〜うちに expresses seizing a transient window of opportunity before the current state or condition changes: "do something while condition ~ lasts / before opportunity slips away". FORMATION (Printed p. 16): ・Noun + の + うちに (若いうちに: while young; 独身のうちに: while single). ・Verb (Dictionary form / ている / ない) + うちに (温かいうちに: while still warm; 明るいうちに: while still light; 忘れないうちに: before I forget; 雨が降らないうちに: before it rains). ・い-adjectives: 〜いうちに. ・な-adjectives: 〜なうちに (元気なうちに: while still in good health). PRAGMATIC CONSTRAINTS (p. 16): Clause A represents a state or situation. Clause B is strictly an intentional, volitional action performed by the speaker to take advantage of the circumstance (日本にいるうちに一度富士山に登ってみたい: While in Japan, I want to try climbing Mt. Fuji).
keyTakeaway: 〜うちに: Seizing a temporary window of opportunity ("do X while state holds / before state changes"). Clause B is strictly volitional (want to do / do!). Formation: Noun+の / な-adj+な / い-adj / V(dict/te-iru/nai) + うちに.

sentences.japanese: 温かいうちに、どうぞ召し上がってください。
sentences.english: Please go ahead and enjoy the food while it is still warm.
sentences.literal: Warm while, please eat.
sentences.nuanceNote: い-adjective connects directly to うちに.

sentences.japanese: 学生のうちに、いろいろな国を訪ねたいです。
sentences.english: I want to visit various countries while I am a student.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nのうちに sets a window that will end. The later action is something the speaker wants to do within it.

sentences.japanese: 忘れないうちに、予約の時間をメモしておこう。
sentences.english: I will write down the reservation time before I forget.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vないうちに means while not yet forgetting: act before the condition changes.

sentences.japanese: 温かいうちに食べてください。
sentences.english: Please eat it while it is warm.
sentences.nuanceNote: An い-adjective attaches directly. The intended action should occur before the food cools.

quiz.question: 雨が（　　）うちに、急いで洗濯物を取り込みましょう。
quiz.translation: Let's hurry and bring in the laundry before it starts raining.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-ない + うちに (Before...)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-ている / V-ない + うちに | い-adj + うちに | な-adj + な + うちに | Noun + の + うちに

explanations.reason: Correct! 降らないうちに means 'before it rains / while it is not raining'.
Incorrect. 降ったうちに is invalid (past tense cannot combine with うちに).
Incorrect. 降るうちに implies while it is actively raining.
Incorrect. 降らなくて cannot directly attach to うちに.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 16 (PDF p. 39). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜うちに (Unnoticed Natural Evolution: While Doing X, Y Emerged)
meaning: While continuing action X over time, an uncalculated natural change or realization Y developed unnoticed.
connection: Verb (辞書形 / ている形 / ない形) + うちに、[Non-Volitional Change]
nuance: 〜うちに (Natural Evolution) expresses that while a continuous process or action ~ is happening, a change ... also emerges naturally without the deliberate intention of the speaker: "while doing..., gradually / before I realized it, change occurred". FORMATION (Printed p. 16): ・Verb (Dictionary form / ている / ない) + うちに ・音楽を聞いているうちに眠ってしまった (While listening to music, I fell asleep without realizing). ・何回も練習するうちに、上手に弾けるようになった (While practicing repeatedly, I naturally became able to play well). ・最初は嫌いだったが、付き合っているうちに好きになった (At first I disliked him, but while spending time together, I came to like him). STRICT VOLITION BAN (p. 16): Clause B CANNOT express speaker volition, requests, or commands (*見ているうちに、買いましょう is completely ungrammatical). It must describe an unconscious, emergent natural transformation or state change.
keyTakeaway: 〜うちに (Evolution): While a continuous process ~ unfolds, an unforced change ... emerges without speaker volition ("before realizing it / gradually"). Clause B CANNOT be volitional (never requests/commands).

sentences.japanese: 本を読んでいるうちに、いつの間にか眠ってしまった。
sentences.english: While I was reading a book, before I knew it, I fell fast asleep.
sentences.literal: Book reading was while, unnoticed slept-ended-up.
sentences.nuanceNote: Spontaneous transition into sleep.

sentences.japanese: 毎日話すうちに、緊張しなくなりました。
sentences.english: As I spoke every day, I gradually stopped feeling nervous.
sentences.nuanceNote: Repeated activity continues while a change develops; this is not an instruction to seize an opportunity.

sentences.japanese: 気づかないうちに、外は暗くなっていました。
sentences.english: It had become dark outside without my noticing.
sentences.nuanceNote: The negative form is also possible. The change happened while the speaker was unaware.

quiz.question: 何度も練習して（　　）うちに、自然に話せるようになりました。
quiz.translation: While practicing repeatedly, I naturally became able to speak.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-ている + うちに gradual evolution
quiz.ruleHint: V dictionary / Vている / Vない + うちに

explanations.reason: Plain ている attaches to うちに and describes the continuing process.
The polite ending います does not directly modify うち in this pattern.
いたの adds an unnecessary の.
いまして does not modify うち.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 16 (PDF p. 39). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜間 vs 〜間に (Continuous Duration vs Momentary Action)
meaning: 間 presents a span during which something continues; 間に locates an event or change within that span.
connection: [Noun の / Verb (辞書形/ている/ない)] + 間 (continuous B) | 間に (momentary B)
nuance: Shin Kanzen Master N3 rigorously systematizes the aspectual dichotomy between 〜間 and 〜間に: FORMATION (Printed pp. 16-17): ・Noun + の / Verb (辞書形 / ている / ない) + 間 vs 間に. (1) 〜間 (Continuous Co-occurrence, p. 16): ・"While ~ (continuous state), ... is going on continuously throughout the same duration." ・Both ~ and ... describe sustained, ongoing states or actions that span the entire duration together (留守の間、友だちが犬の世話をしてくれた: While I was away, my friend took care of my dog the entire time; お母さんが昼寝をしている間、子どもたちは静かにテレビを見ていた). (2) 〜間に (Momentary Interruption, p. 17): ・"While ~ (continuous state), ... happens as a momentary action or event." ・~ describes a continuous state, but ... describes an instantaneous action or punctual event that begins and concludes within the timeframe (留守の間に泥棒が入った: A burglar broke in while I was away; シャワーを浴びている間に電話が鳴った: The phone rang while taking a shower).
keyTakeaway: 〜間 = both clauses describe continuous actions spanning the whole timeframe together. 〜間に = momentary action or punctual event occurs inside the ongoing duration of clause A.

sentences.japanese: 両親が旅行している間、ずっと一人で留守番をしていた。
sentences.english: Throughout the entire time my parents were traveling, I looked after the house alone.
sentences.literal: Parents traveling while, throughout alone home-tending did.

tokens.meaning: throughout the entire time they traveled
tokens.reading: りょこうしているあいだ

sentences.nuanceNote: Continuous house-sitting for the entire vacation interval.

sentences.japanese: 子供が寝ている間、私は本を読んでいました。
sentences.english: I was reading while my child slept.
sentences.nuanceNote: 間 frames two continuing activities over the relevant interval.

sentences.japanese: 子供が寝ている間に、夕食を作りました。
sentences.english: I prepared dinner while my child was asleep.
sentences.nuanceNote: 間に locates the preparation/completion within the sleep period. It need not take only an instant.

sentences.japanese: 留守の間に、荷物が届きました。
sentences.english: A parcel arrived while I was away.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nの間に: an arrival occurs within a period of absence.

quiz.question: 日本に住んでいる（　　）に、一度富士山に登りたいです。
quiz.translation: I would like to climb Mount Fuji once while living in Japan.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜間に (Momentary event during interval)
quiz.ruleHint: V dictionary/ている, い-adjective, な-adjectiveな, Nの + 間 / 間に

explanations.reason: 間に marks an event within the period.
間のに is not this pattern.
間でに incorrectly stacks the particles.
間をに incorrectly stacks the particles.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 16 (PDF p. 39). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜てからでないと / 〜てからでなければ (Not Until / Only After Prerequisite Is Done)
meaning: Not until; cannot do Y before first doing X.
connection: V-てからでないと / V-てからでなければ、[Negative / Impossibility Predicate]
nuance: 〜てからでないと / 〜てからでなければ expresses an indispensable prerequisite: "until/unless ~ happens or is completed, ... cannot happen or cannot be done either". FORMATION (Printed p. 17): ・Verb て-form + からでないと / からでなければ. ・手続きをしてからでないと、この部屋には入れません (You cannot enter this room until procedures are completed). ・親と相談してからでなければ、留学するかどうか決められません (I cannot decide whether to study abroad until I talk with my parents). ・実際に使ってみてからでないと、本当に役に立つか判断できません (Until actually trying it, one cannot judge whether it is helpful). STRICT NEGATIVE/INABILITY CONSTRAINT (p. 17): The following clause ... is strictly restricted to negative statements, expressing impossibility, inability (〜わけにはいかない, 〜できない), or an unfavorable state.
keyTakeaway: V-てからでないと / でなければ: "not until / unless prerequisite ~ is done". Clause B is STRICTLY NEGATIVE (cannot do, impossible, prohibited: 入れません, 決められません).

sentences.japanese: 上司と相談してからでないと、この場でお返事はできません。
sentences.english: Unless I consult with my supervisor first, I cannot give you an answer on the spot.
sentences.literal: Supervisor-with consult-after-only, this place-at reply cannot.

tokens.word: 相談してからでないと
tokens.reading: そうだんしてからでないと
tokens.romaji: soudan shite kara de nai to

sentences.nuanceNote: Business prerequisite for answer.

sentences.japanese: 実物を見てからでないと、買うかどうか決められません。
sentences.english: I cannot decide whether to buy it until I see the actual item.
sentences.nuanceNote: The second clause expresses inability to decide before the prerequisite.

sentences.japanese: 許可をもらってからでなければ、入場は無理です。
sentences.english: Entry is impossible until permission has been obtained.
sentences.useLabel: Negative meaning without a negative verb
sentences.nuanceNote: 無理 is negative in meaning although it does not end in ない. Do not demand a particular negative ending.

quiz.question: 詳しい契約内容を（　　）からでないと、サインすることはできません。
quiz.translation: Unless I read the detailed contract terms first, I cannot sign it.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-て + からでないと prerequisite
quiz.ruleHint: V-て + からでないと / からでなければ + Negative / Impossible Predicate

explanations.reason: Correct! 読む connects via te-form 読んで + からでないと.
Incorrect. 読む is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 読んだ is past form.
Incorrect. 読まない is negative form.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 16 (PDF p. 39). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ところだ (Temporal Phase: Imminent, In the Midst, or Just Finished)
meaning: Pinpoints the exact temporal boundary: 1) Just about to start (辞書形). 2) In the thick of doing (ている). 3) Just completed moments ago (た形).
connection: Verb (辞書形 / ている形 / た形) + ところだ (Sentence-final) | ところへ / ところを / ところで
nuance: 〜ところだ pinpoints the precise temporal phase of an action (imminent, concurrent, or freshly completed). FORMATION & THREE TEMPORAL PHASES (Printed p. 17): (1) Verb (辞書形) + ところだ: Just before ~ happens / on the very verge of doing: ・ロケットは今まさに飛び立つところです (The rocket is on the very verge of blasting off). ・今から出かけるところです (I am just about to head out right now). (2) Verb (ている形) + ところだ: Right in the midst of ~ happening: ・今、原因を調べているところです (We are currently in the midst of investigating the cause). ・電話しているところです (I am in the middle of a phone call). (3) Verb (た形) + ところだ: Just this very second finished ~ happening: ・たった今、昼ご飯を食べ終わったところです (I have just this moment finished lunch). MID-SENTENCE PARTICLE ALTERNATION: Depending on the following verb, particles attach: ・〜ところへ (at the moment when someone arrives: ケーキを食べているところへ母が帰ってきた). ・〜ところを (caught in the midst of an action: 泥棒が逃げようとするところを逮捕された). ・〜ところで (at the juncture where something interrupts: 相談しているところで電話が入った).
keyTakeaway: 〜ところだ: (1) V-辞書形+ところだ = just about to start; (2) V-ている+ところだ = right in the midst; (3) V-た+ところだ = just finished this moment. Particles: ところへ, ところを, ところで.

sentences.japanese: 今から家を出るところですから、三十分後には着くと思います。
sentences.english: I am just about to leave the house right now, so I think I'll arrive in about 30 minutes.
sentences.literal: Now house leave-about-to, 30-mins-after arrive think.
sentences.nuanceNote: V-辞書形 + ところ indicates imminent departure.

sentences.japanese: 今から夕食を作るところです。
sentences.english: I am just about to make dinner.
sentences.nuanceNote: Dictionary form + ところ locates the moment just before the action starts.

sentences.japanese: こっそりお菓子を食べているところを、妹に見られました。
sentences.english: My younger sister saw me secretly eating sweets.
sentences.useLabel: In progress, caught in the act
sentences.nuanceNote: Vているところを marks the ongoing scene as the object of 見る. It is not simply a sentence-final ところだ.

sentences.japanese: 宿題が終わったところで、友達から電話が来ました。
sentences.english: Just as I finished my homework, a friend called.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vたところで gives the stage at which another event occurred. This is different from concessive Vたところで meaning even if.

sentences.japanese: 料理ができたところへ、お客さんが来ました。
sentences.english: The guests arrived just as the food was ready.
sentences.nuanceNote: ところへ fits an arrival into the situation; the following verb determines the particle.

quiz.question: ちょうど今、昼ご飯を食べ（　　）ところだから、お腹がいっぱいです。
quiz.translation: I just finished eating lunch right now, so I am completely full.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-た + ところだ (Just finished)
quiz.ruleHint: V dictionary / Vている / Vた + ところだ; within a sentence: ところを / ところで / ところへ, according to the following predicate

explanations.reason: Correct! V-た + ところだ indicates an action that concluded moments ago.
Incorrect. 終わるところ implies about to finish.
Incorrect. 終わっているところ is awkward with ところ.
Incorrect. 終われ is imperative.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 16 (PDF p. 39). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

table.title: Time & Instant Sequence Spectrum (時・継起のグラデーション)
table.subtitle: How Japanese grammar sharpens from general timing to split-second interruption.

rows.label: 〜最中に (さいちゅうに)
cells: N3
Right in the middle of active ongoing action
Emphasizes being in the middle of an activity
Often followed by an interruption, but neither surprise nor a negative outcome is required.
rows.note: Conjugation: V-ている + 最中に / N の最中に

rows.label: 〜うちに
cells: N3
Within limited window before condition changes
Natural change or spontaneous urge ⚠️
Do it while hot / Before you forget (冷めないうちに / 忘れないうちに).
rows.note: Conjugation: V dictionary/ない/ている, い-adjective, な-adjectiveな or Nの + うちに

rows.label: 〜たとたん（に）
cells: N3
The exact split-second after X finishes
Immediate surprise, NO speaker volition ❌
Clause B is a sudden surprise event (立ち上がったとたん、めまいがした).
rows.note: Conjugation: V-た + とたん（に）

rows.label: 〜かと思うと / 〜かと思ったら
cells: N2
Right when you thought X had occurred
Sharp unexpected contrast / sudden change ❌
Cannot describe speaker's deliberate action (空が暗くなったかと思うと、雨が降ってきた).
rows.note: Conjugation: V-た + かと思うと

rows.label: 〜か〜ないかのうちに
cells: N2
Literally on the border of completion
Simultaneous / instantaneous sequence
Almost no time gap: ベルが鳴り終わるか終わらないかのうちに.
rows.note: Conjugation: V-辞書形 / V-た + か + V-ない + かのうちに

rows.label: 〜次第 (しだい)
cells: N2
Immediate trigger for planned next step
HIGH speaker volition & business resolve ✅
Used for future events: 決まり次第、ご連絡いたします.
rows.note: Conjugation: V-stem + 次第 (NO past tense in main clause!)

title: 〜とおりに / 〜どおりに (Just As / In Exact Accordance With)
meaning: Executing an action in faithful, exact alignment with instructions, drawings, thoughts, or maps ('Just as planned / Exactly as told').
connection: Noun + のとおりに / Noun + どおりに | Verb (辞書形/た形/ている形) + とおりに
nuance: 〜とおりに / 〜どおりに expresses carrying out an action or manifesting a state in complete conformity with a model, instructions, thought, or plan: "just as / in exact accordance with". FORMATION & RENDAKU (Printed p. 18): ・Noun + の + とおりに (説明書のとおりに: according to the manual; 計画のとおりに: as planned). ・Noun + どおりに (Direct attachment triggers voiced rendaku: 予想どおり: as predicted; 計画どおり: as planned; 指示どおり: as instructed; 思いどおり: as desired). ・Verb (辞書形 / た形 / ている形) + とおりに (私が言うとおりにしてください: Do exactly as I say; 思ったとおりだった: It was just as I thought; 見たとおりに話す: tell it just as seen). RESTRICTION: Verbs attach directly to とおり without particle の (言うとおり, never *言うのとおり).
keyTakeaway: 〜とおりに / どおりに: "just as / in accordance with". Formations: Noun + のとおりに OR direct Noun + どおりに (予想どおり, 計画どおり). Verb (dict/ta/te-iru) + とおりに.

sentences.japanese: 先生が指示したとおりに実験を行ったら、予想どおりの結果が出た。
sentences.english: When we conducted the experiment exactly as the teacher instructed, results came out just as expected.
sentences.literal: Teacher instructed as-exact experiment conducted-when, expectation-as results came-out.
sentences.nuanceNote: Verbal とおりに and nominal どおり.

sentences.japanese: 先生がやったとおりに、紙を折ってください。
sentences.english: Please fold the paper the way the teacher did.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vたとおりに refers to an already demonstrated model.

sentences.japanese: 予定どおりに、会議は三時に始まりました。
sentences.english: The meeting began at three as scheduled.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nどおり is voiced. With の, use Nのとおり: 予定のとおり.

quiz.question: 事態は我々の当初の計画（　　）に進展しており、何の問題もありません。
quiz.translation: The situation is progressing exactly according to our original plan, and there are no problems whatsoever.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + どおり (Voiced without の)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-た + とおりに | Noun + の + とおりに | Noun + どおりに (Voiced sound without の!)

explanations.reason: Correct! Noun 計画 combines directly as 計画どおり (voiced without の).
Incorrect. とおり directly after noun requires の (計画のとおり).
Incorrect. ばかり means only / just.
Incorrect. ほど means extent or proportion.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 18 (PDF p. 41). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜によって / 〜によっては (Depending on / According to Differences)
meaning: Indicates diversity, variety, or contingency: 'Depending on X, things differ / In some cases of X...'.
connection: Noun + によって (predicate: 違う/さまざま) | Noun + によっては (single outcome)
nuance: 〜によって / 〜によっては expresses that behavior, state, or outcomes vary depending on conditions, categories, or differences: "depending on / according to differences in". FORMATION (Printed p. 18): ・Noun + によって / Noun + による + Noun ・国によって習慣が違います (Customs differ depending on the country). ・人によって感じ方がさまざまだ (Ways of feeling vary depending on the individual). PREDICATE COLLOCATIONS: Frequently concludes with diversity predicates: 違う (differ), 異なる (vary), さまざまだ (diverse), 変わる (change). PINPOINTING OUTCOMES WITH 〜によっては (p. 18): 〜によっては pinpoints one specific extreme or notable outcome from among multiple possibilities ("in some cases depending on..."): ・当日の天気によっては、花火大会が中止になることもあります (Depending on the weather, the fireworks may be canceled in some cases).
keyTakeaway: Noun + によって = "depending on differences in..." (predicate: 違う, さまざまだ). Noun + によっては = "in some cases depending on..." (pinpointing a specific outcome, e.g. 中止になることもある).

sentences.japanese: 文化や宗教によって、タブーとされる食べ物は大きく異なる。
sentences.english: Depending on culture and religion, foods considered taboo differ significantly.
sentences.literal: Culture or religion depending-on, taboo considered food greatly differs.

tokens.reading: しゅうきょうによって

sentences.nuanceNote: Societal variations across cultural groups.

sentences.japanese: 好きな食べ物は人によって違います。
sentences.english: Favorite foods differ from person to person.
sentences.nuanceNote: によって marks the variable across which the result changes.

sentences.japanese: 店によっては、現金しか使えません。
sentences.english: At some shops, only cash can be used.
sentences.nuanceNote: によっては singles out some cases rather than making a claim about every shop.

quiz.question: 体質（　　）は、アレルギーが出ることがあります。
quiz.translation: Depending on one's constitution, an allergy can occur.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + によっては (Contingent outcome)
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + によって (異なる, 違う, さまざまだ) | Noun + によっては (Certain specific outcomes)

explanations.reason: The supplied は completes によっては.
This duplicates the は already after the blank.
にとって describes an evaluating perspective.
について marks a topic, not variation by constitution.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 18 (PDF p. 41). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜たびに (Every Single Time / Invariable Recurrence)
meaning: Each time X occurs, Y happens.
connection: Noun + の / Verb (辞書形) + たびに
nuance: 〜たびに expresses recurring, invariable co-occurrence: "every single time ~ happens, ... happens too / whenever ~, always ...". FORMATION (Printed p. 19): ・Noun + の + たびに (旅行のたびに: every time I travel; 会うたびに: every time we meet). ・Verb (辞書形) + たびに (この曲を聞くたびに、学生時代を思い出す: Every time I listen to this song, I recall my student days). STRICT RESTRICTIONS (Printed p. 19): (1) Natural/everyday matter-of-course events cannot be used (*朝起きるたびに顔を洗う: ungrammatical; must describe deliberate, noteworthy recurrence). (2) Neither ~ nor ... can express a static condition/state (both must describe discrete recurring events or actions).
keyTakeaway: V(辞書形) / Noun + の + たびに = "every single time ~ happens, always ...". Strict bans: (1) Cannot be used for everyday matter-of-course habits (*朝起きるたびに), (2) Neither clause can be a static state.

sentences.japanese: このアルバムを見るたびに、楽しかった学生時代を懐かしく思い出す。
sentences.english: Every time I look at this photo album, I fondly recall my happy student days.
sentences.literal: This album look every-time, fun student-era fondly recall.
sentences.nuanceNote: Emotional trigger whenever looking at photos.

sentences.japanese: この曲を聞くたびに、学生時代を思い出します。
sentences.english: Every time I hear this song, I remember my student days.
sentences.nuanceNote: Dictionary verb + たびに links each occurrence to the recurring response.

sentences.japanese: 出張のたびに、報告書を書きます。
sentences.english: I write a report each time I go on a business trip.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nのたびに. A recurring result need not be emotional or surprising.

quiz.question: 「出張するごとに」という意味です。父は出張の（　　）、お土産を買ってきます。
quiz.translation: On every business trip, my father buys souvenirs.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + の + たびに
quiz.ruleHint: V dictionary / Nの + たびに

explanations.reason: Nのたびに means on each occasion.
たびの must modify a noun.
たびで is not the recurrence linker here.
たびを does not link this temporal clause.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 18 (PDF p. 41). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: (〜ば)〜ほど (Proportional Correlation: The More... The More...)
meaning: The more X, the more/less Y; one degree changes with another.
connection: V-ば + V-辞書形ほど | A-ければ + A-いほど | A-なら + A-なほど | Noun + ほど
nuance: (〜ば)〜ほど expresses proportional correlation: "the more ~ increases in degree, the more ... also increases or changes in parallel". FORMATION PARADIGM (Printed p. 19): ・Verbs: V-ば + V-辞書形 + ほど (物が増えれば増えるほど、整理が大変になる: The more things increase, the harder tidying up becomes). ・い-adjectives: A-ければ + A-い + ほど (安ければ安いほどいい: The cheaper, the better; 高ければ高いほど嬉しい). ・な-adjectives: A-なら(ば) + A-な + ほど (簡単なら簡単なほど使いやすい: The simpler, the easier to use; 静かなら静かなほどいい). ・Bare Noun: Noun + ほど (本物ほど価値がある: The more genuine it is, the more value it has). ELLIPSIS: The initial conditional clause (〜ば / 〜なら) is often omitted in natural Japanese (e.g. 考えれば考えるほど → 考えるほど: the more I think; 安いほどいい).
keyTakeaway: (〜ば)〜ほど: "the more..., the more...". Formations: V-ば V-辞書形ほど; A-ければ A-いほど; A-なら A-なほど; Noun+ほど. The first conditional half can be omitted (考えるほど).

sentences.japanese: 外国語は使えば使うほど、上手に話せるようになります。
sentences.english: The more you use a foreign language, the more fluently you become able to speak it.
sentences.literal: Foreign-language use-if use-extent, skillfully speak able become.
sentences.nuanceNote: Proportional correlation between usage and fluency.

sentences.japanese: 練習すればするほど、動きが自然になります。
sentences.english: The more I practice, the more natural my movements become.
sentences.nuanceNote: Repeat the same verb in conditional and dictionary forms.

sentences.japanese: 荷物は軽ければ軽いほど、運びやすいです。
sentences.english: The lighter the luggage, the easier it is to carry.
sentences.nuanceNote: い-adjective: ければ + dictionary adjective + ほど.

sentences.japanese: 説明は簡単なら簡単なほど、分かりやすいです。
sentences.english: The simpler the explanation, the easier it is to understand.
sentences.nuanceNote: The adjective before ほど uses な. The first conditional can also be expressed with であれば.

quiz.question: 荷物は（　　）ほど、旅行は身軽で快適になる。
quiz.translation: The less luggage you have, the lighter and more comfortable your trip becomes.
quiz.grammarFocus: い-adjective (〜ければ)〜ほど
quiz.ruleHint: V-ば + V-辞書形 + ほど | い-adj ければ + い-adj + ほど | な-adj なら + な-adj な + ほど | Noun + であればあるほど

explanations.reason: Correct! い-adjective proportional formula: 少なければ + 少ない + ほど.
Incorrect. 少ないなら少ない does not combine in standard correlative pair.
Incorrect. て-form cannot form this correlative formula.
Incorrect. と does not match the ほど correlative construction.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 18 (PDF p. 41). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ついでに (While at It / Seizing Opportunity for a Side Task)
meaning: While executing primary task A, seizing the convenient opportunity to perform secondary side task B: 'While you're at it / On the way'.
connection: Noun + の / Verb (辞書形 / た形) + ついでに
nuance: 〜ついでに expresses taking advantage of the opportunity created by a primary action to conveniently accomplish a secondary task: "while doing primary action ~, take the chance to do secondary action ... as well". FORMATION (Printed p. 19): ・Noun + の + ついでに (散歩のついでに、ポストに手紙を入れてきた: While out for a walk, I dropped a letter in the post). ・Verb (辞書形 / た形) + ついでに (買い物のついでに本屋に寄った; 出張で行ったついでに観光した). PRIMARY VS SECONDARY ACTION CONSTRAINT (p. 19): Clause A represents the main, pre-planned primary action. Clause B represents an incidental, secondary action that is carried out opportunistically because of A. Reversing the priority creates pragmatically unnatural Japanese.
keyTakeaway: 〜ついでに: "while at it / taking opportunity of primary action A to do secondary B". Formation: Noun+の / Verb(dict/ta) + ついでに. A is the primary goal; B is the incidental side action.

sentences.japanese: 郵便局へ切手を買いに行くついでに、コンビニで公共料金を支払ってきた。
sentences.english: While heading to the post office to buy stamps, I stopped by the convenience store and paid utility bills.
sentences.literal: Post-office stamps buy go while-at-it, convenience-store utility-bills paid.
sentences.nuanceNote: Side errand during post office trip.

sentences.japanese: 銀行へ行くついでに、郵便局にも寄ります。
sentences.english: While I am going to the bank, I will also stop at the post office.
sentences.useLabel: Secondary task during a planned trip
sentences.nuanceNote: The bank visit is the main purpose; the post-office stop is an added convenience.

sentences.japanese: 部屋を掃除したついでに、窓も拭きました。
sentences.english: While I was at it after cleaning the room, I wiped the windows too.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vたついでに can refer to the opportunity created by doing the main task.

quiz.question: 散歩の（　　）、ポストにこの手紙を投函してきてくれませんか。
quiz.translation: While you're out taking a walk, would you mind dropping this letter into the mailbox for me?
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + の + ついでに (Incidental side-task)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-た + ついでに | Noun + の + ついでに

explanations.reason: Correct! 散歩のついでに means conveniently posting the letter while already out on a walk.
Incorrect. たびに means every single time you walk.
Incorrect. うちに means before the walk ends.
Incorrect. 最中に means in the middle of walking.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 18 (PDF p. 41). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜くらいだ / 〜ほどだ (Expressing Extreme Degree: To the Extent That)
meaning: To the extent that; so … that; a comparison showing degree.
connection: Noun / Verb (plain) / い-adj / な-adj + な + くらいだ / ほどだ
nuance: 〜くらいだ / 〜ほどだ expresses an extreme metaphorical degree: "to the extent that ~, in which ~ is an illustrative, vivid example of what could have happened, but did not actually occur". FORMATION (Printed p. 22): ・Noun / Verb (plain form) / い-adj / な-adj + な + くらいだ / ほどだ / くらい / ほど. ・涙が出るほど痛かった (It hurt so much that tears came out). ・倒れそうなほど疲れた (I was so exhausted that I felt like collapsing). ・お腹が痛くなるくらい大笑いした (Laughed so hard my stomach ached). IDIOMATIC EXTENSION: 〜かと思うほど: "so [adjective] that I even wondered if..." (まるで夢かと思うほど嬉しかった: so happy I wondered if it was a dream).
keyTakeaway: 〜くらいだ / 〜ほどだ: Expresses extreme metaphorical degree ("so intense that ~ almost happened"). Formations: Noun / Verb / い-adj / な-adj + な + くらいだ / ほどだ. Idiom: 〜かと思うほど.

sentences.japanese: 昨日の富士山頂からの日の出は、息をのむほど美しかった。
sentences.english: Yesterday's sunrise from the summit of Mt. Fuji was breathtakingly beautiful to the point of gasping.
sentences.literal: Yesterday's Mt-Fuji summit sunrise, breath swallow extent beautiful-was.

tokens.meaning: to the extent of taking one's breath away

sentences.nuanceNote: Breathtaking beauty on mountain summit.

sentences.japanese: 声が出ないくらい驚きました。
sentences.english: I was so surprised that I could not speak.
sentences.useLabel: Degree illustrated by a possible action
sentences.nuanceNote: くらい gives a concrete indication of the degree of surprise.

sentences.japanese: 昨日は倒れるかと思うほど疲れました。
sentences.english: Yesterday I was so tired that I thought I might collapse.
sentences.nuanceNote: ほど can express an extreme degree without saying the comparison event actually happened.

quiz.question: 昨夜はあまりに仕事が忙しくて、猫の手も借りたい（　　）だった。
quiz.translation: Last night work was so overwhelmingly busy that I was in a state where I'd welcome even a cat's paw to help.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜くらいだ (Extreme metaphorical degree)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-ない + くらいだ / ほどだ | Noun + くらい / ほど

explanations.reason: Correct! 猫の手も借りたいくらいだ is the idiomatic expression for extreme desperation for help.
Incorrect. ばかり means only / just.
Incorrect. ところ means temporal phase.
Incorrect. わけ means logical reason.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 45). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜くらい…はない / 〜ほど…はない (Superlative: Nothing Is As... As X)
meaning: Subjective superlative declaring that entity X is unsurpassed in quality Y: 'Nothing is as [adjective] as X / There is nobody quite as [adjective] as X'.
connection: Noun + くらい / ほど + [Noun] + はない / はいない
nuance: 〜くらい…はない / 〜ほど…はない expresses a subjective superlative: "~ is the most ... of all / nothing/nobody is as ... as ~". FORMATION (Printed p. 22): ・Noun + くらい / ほど + [Noun] + はない (or いない for animate persons). ・健康ほど大切なものはない (Nothing is as important as health). ・彼くらい頼りになる先輩はいない (There is no senior colleague as dependable as him). ・母の手料理くらい美味しいものはない (Nothing is as delicious as my mother's home cooking). SUBJECTIVE CONSTRAINT (p. 22): This pattern expresses the speaker's personal subjective conviction or emotional evaluation; it CANNOT be used to state objective factual superlatives (*富士山ほど高い山は日本にない is unnatural in formal factual contexts; use 日本で一番高い山 instead).
keyTakeaway: Noun + くらい / ほど + [Noun] はない / いない: Subjective superlative ("nothing/nobody is as ... as X"). Expresses speaker's personal feeling, not an objective factual statistic.

sentences.japanese: 仕事で大汗をかいた後の一杯の冷たい水ほど、美味しいものはない。
sentences.english: There is nothing quite as delicious as a glass of cold water after sweating heavily at work.
sentences.literal: Work-at big-sweat shed after one-glass cold water extent, delicious thing none.
sentences.nuanceNote: Superlative personal evaluation of cold water.

sentences.japanese: 私には、家で休むほど幸せな時間はありません。
sentences.english: For me, no time is as happy as resting at home.
sentences.nuanceNote: A negative comparison expresses a subjective highest evaluation, not a measured universal fact.

sentences.japanese: 今日は昨日ほど寒くありません。
sentences.english: Today is not as cold as yesterday.
sentences.nuanceNote: XはYほど…ない compares two items. This is not necessarily a superlative among all items.

quiz.question: 私にとって、家族と一緒に過ごす時間（　　）大切なものはありません。
quiz.translation: For me, there is nothing as precious as the time I spend together with my family.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + ほど…はない (Unsurpassed superlative)
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + くらい / ほど + [Noun] はない (Negative predicate at the end!)

explanations.reason: Correct! 〜ほど [大切なもの] はない establishes the superlative evaluation.
Incorrect. ばかり means only / just.
Incorrect. きり means only / limit.
Incorrect. とおり means in accordance with.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 45). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜くらいなら / 〜ぐらいなら (Rather Than Suffer X, I Would Prefer Y)
meaning: If forced to endure an unacceptable condition X, I would far rather do alternative Y (even if Y is also drastic).
connection: Verb (辞書形) + くらいなら / ぐらいなら、[〜方がいい / 〜ましだ]
nuance: 〜くらいなら / 〜ぐらいなら expresses choosing a preferable alternative over an abhorrent or undesirable situation: "if ~ is the case, you are better off doing ... / rather than suffer ~, I would prefer ...". FORMATION (Printed p. 23): ・Verb (辞書形) + くらいなら / ぐらいなら + [Clause B with 〜方がいい / 〜方がましだ]. ・途中で諦めるくらいなら、最初からやらない方がいい (Rather than giving up halfway, you're better off not starting at all). ・あんな奴に謝るくらいなら、部活を辞めた方がましだ (Rather than apologizing to that jerk, I'd rather quit the club!). ・生活水準を下げるくらいなら、残業した方がいい (Rather than lowering my standard of living, I'd rather work overtime). PRAGMATIC CONSTRAINTS: Expresses subjective judgment of personal values; clause B typically features evaluation markers: 〜方がいい (better to), 〜方がましだ (preferable / less bad), or 〜たい (want to).
keyTakeaway: V(辞書形) + くらいなら / ぐらいなら: "rather than suffer undesirable X, I would prefer Y". Clause B typically concludes with 〜方がいい / 〜方がましだ / 〜たい.

sentences.japanese: 彼に頭を下げて頼むくらいなら、自分で失敗したほうがまだましだ。
sentences.english: Rather than bow my head and beg him for help, I would far rather fail on my own.
sentences.literal: Him-to head lower begging rather-than, by-myself failed better is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Strong refusal of humiliation in preference of independent struggle.

sentences.japanese: そんなに長く待つくらいなら、別の店に行きます。
sentences.english: Rather than wait that long, I will go to another shop.
sentences.nuanceNote: The speaker judges waiting to be the worse option and chooses an alternative.

sentences.japanese: 嫌な仕事を続けるくらいなら、収入が減っても転職したいです。
sentences.english: Rather than continue a job I dislike, I want to change jobs even if my income falls.
sentences.nuanceNote: The alternative need not be ideal; it is preferred to the rejected situation.

quiz.question: あんな失礼な人に謝る（　　）なら、仕事を辞めたほうがいい。
quiz.translation: Rather than apologize to such a rude person, I'd rather quit my job.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-る + くらいなら (Preferential aversion)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 + くらいなら / ぐらいなら

explanations.reason: Correct! 謝るくらいなら expresses 'Rather than apologize, I'd prefer quitting'.
Incorrect. ほどなら is ungrammatical in this comparative preference structure.
Incorrect. ばかりなら does not express 'rather than'.
Incorrect. だけになら is incorrect.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 45). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜に限る (Nothing Beats / Best Choice)
meaning: Nothing beats X; X is the best choice or best thing to do.
connection: Noun / Verb (辞書形 / ない形) + に限る
nuance: 〜に限る expresses the speaker's personal conviction that something is the absolute best choice or most effective method: "~ is the best / nothing beats ~". FORMATION (Printed p. 23): ・Noun + に限る (映画は映画館で見るに限る: For movies, seeing them in a theater is best; 暑い日は冷たい麦茶に限る). ・Verb (辞書形) + に限る (風邪をひいた時は、温かくして寝るに限る: When sick with a cold, nothing beats keeping warm and sleeping). ・Verb (ない形) + に限る (危険な場所には近寄らないに限る: The best policy is not to approach dangerous areas). SUBJECTIVE CONVICTION BAN (p. 23): Strictly expresses the speaker's personal opinion and advice. It CANNOT be used to assert objective truths or scientific facts.
keyTakeaway: Noun / Verb(辞書形/ない形) + に限る: "nothing beats X / X is the absolute best choice". Strictly expresses the speaker's personal subjective conviction, never an objective factual law.

sentences.japanese: 風邪を引いたときは、温かいスープを飲んで早く寝るに限る。
sentences.english: When you catch a cold, nothing beats drinking hot soup and getting to sleep early.
sentences.literal: Cold caught when, hot soup drink early sleep is-best.
sentences.nuanceNote: Universal folk wisdom framed as speaker's top recommendation.

sentences.japanese: 暑い日は冷たい麦茶に限ります。
sentences.english: On a hot day, nothing beats cold barley tea.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nに限る gives a subjective best choice, not an access restriction.

sentences.japanese: 疲れたときは、早く寝るに限ります。
sentences.english: When you are tired, the best thing is to go to bed early.
sentences.nuanceNote: Dictionary verb + に限る recommends an action.

sentences.japanese: 体調が悪いときは、無理をしないに限ります。
sentences.english: When you feel unwell, it is best not to push yourself.
sentences.nuanceNote: Vない + に限る recommends refraining from the action.

quiz.question: 「早く寝るのが一番よい」という意味です。疲れた日は、早く寝るに（　　）。
quiz.translation: On a tiring day, the best thing is to go to bed early.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-る + に限る (Supreme choice)
quiz.ruleHint: N / V dictionary / Vない + に限る

explanations.reason: に限る gives the subjective best choice.
限って is a connective form and does not complete this sentence.
限りな is not this verb form.
限ら is an unfinished stem.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 22 (PDF p. 45). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜反面 (On the Flip Side: Coexisting Contradictory Aspects)
meaning: Presents two opposing, contradictory qualities coexisting simultaneously within the exact same person, product, or phenomenon: 'Convenient, but on the flip side, expensive'.
connection: Plain form (+ な/である for な-adj, + である for Noun) + 反面
nuance: 〜反面 expresses the coexistence of two contrasting, contradictory sides (positive and negative) within the VERY SAME entity, situation, or phenomenon: "on the flip side / on the other hand". FORMATION (Printed p. 24): ・Plain form (+ な/である for な-adj, + である for Noun) + 反面. ・都会の生活は便利な反面、ストレスも多い (Urban life is convenient, but on the flip side, stress is high). ・薬は病気を治す反面、副作用があることもある (Medicine cures illness, but on the flip side, can have side effects). ・一人暮らしは気楽な反面、寂しさを感じることもある (Living alone is carefree, but on the flip side, can feel lonely). CORE CONSTRAINT: Subject in both halves must refer to the SAME object/situation, highlighting its internal dual nature.
keyTakeaway: 〜反面: Coexisting opposite aspects (merits vs demerits) of the SAME entity ("on the flip side"). Formations: Verb/い-adj plain + 反面; な-adj + な/である反面; Noun + である反面.

sentences.japanese: 都会の生活は刺激的で便利な反面、人との温かい触れ合いが少ない。
sentences.english: While urban living is stimulating and convenient, on the flip side, warm human connections are few.
sentences.literal: Urban living stimulating convenient flip-side, people-with warm connection few.

tokens.meaning: convenient, but on the flip side

sentences.nuanceNote: Balancing urban convenience against social alienation.

sentences.japanese: この部屋は日当たりがいい反面、夏は暑くなります。
sentences.english: This room gets good sunlight, but on the other hand it becomes hot in summer.
sentences.nuanceNote: One feature has both a benefit and a drawback.

sentences.japanese: 新しい生活が楽しみな反面、不安もあります。
sentences.english: I am looking forward to my new life, but I also feel anxious.
sentences.nuanceNote: The two feelings coexist; な-adjective + な反面.

quiz.question: 一人暮らしは自由で気楽な（　　）、病気の時は非常に心細い。
quiz.translation: While living alone is free and carefree, on the flip side, when you are sick you feel terribly lonely.
quiz.grammarFocus: な-adj + な + 反面 two sides of same coin
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + 反面 (な-adj takes な/である, Noun takes である)

explanations.reason: Correct! 気楽な反面 contrasts the freedom against the loneliness of the same living situation.
Incorrect. ついでに means side task.
Incorrect. とたんに means instant surprise trigger.
Incorrect. かぎりに is ungrammatical here.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 24 (PDF p. 47). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜かわりに (In Exchange For / Compensation / Instead Of)
meaning: 1) In exchange for doing or accepting X, compensating with Y ('I'll teach you English in exchange for Japanese lessons'). 2) Instead of regular X, doing alternate Y.
connection: Plain form (+ な for な-adj, + の for Noun) + かわりに
nuance: 〜かわりに expresses trade-off compensation or proxy substitution: FORMATION (Printed p. 25): ・Plain form (+ な for な-adj, + の for Noun) + かわりに. (1) Trade-off / Balanced Compensation (p. 25): ・"On the one hand A, but in return / compensation for it, equivalent B holds." ・この仕事は大変なかわりに、給料が非常に高い (This job is grueling, but in return, the pay is very high). ・駅から遠いかわりに、家賃がとても安い (Far from the station, but in return, rent is cheap). (2) Mutual Exchange: ・日本語を教えてもらうかわりに、英語を教えてあげる (In return for learning Japanese, I will teach you English). (3) Proxy Substitution (Instead of): ・病気の部長のかわりに、私が会議に出席した (In place of the sick manager, I attended the meeting).
keyTakeaway: 〜かわりに: (1) Trade-off / compensation ("disadvantage A, but in return, compensating advantage B"); (2) Exchange of favors; (3) Proxy substitution ("in place of / instead of"). Noun takes の.

sentences.japanese: 英語を教えてもらうかわりに、彼女に美味しい手料理をご馳走した。
sentences.english: In exchange for having her teach me English, I treated her to delicious home cooking.
sentences.literal: English taught-get in-exchange, her-to delicious home-cooking treated.

tokens.word: 教えてもらうかわりに
tokens.reading: おしえてもらうかわりに

sentences.nuanceNote: Reciprocal favor trade.

sentences.japanese: 今日は母のかわりに、私が料理を作ります。
sentences.english: Today I will cook instead of my mother.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nのかわりに replaces a person in a role.

sentences.japanese: この仕事は大変なかわりに、給料が高いです。
sentences.english: This job is demanding, but the pay is high in return.
sentences.nuanceNote: な-adjectiveなかわりに balances a drawback with compensation.

sentences.japanese: 買い物を手伝うかわりに、日本語を教えてください。
sentences.english: In return for my helping with the shopping, please teach me Japanese.
sentences.nuanceNote: The first action is offered in exchange for the second.

quiz.question: この仕事は残業が多くて大変な（　　）に、給料は非常に高い。
quiz.translation: In exchange for this job having lots of overtime and being tough, the salary is exceptionally high.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜かわりに reciprocal trade-off
quiz.ruleHint: Plain modifier + かわりに; Nの / な-adjectiveな + かわりに

explanations.reason: Correct! 大変なかわりに balances tough working conditions with high financial compensation.
Incorrect. ついで means taking opportunity for side errand.
Incorrect. とおり means in accordance with.
あまり can describe excessive degree leading to a result; it does not express the compensating trade-off intended here.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 24 (PDF p. 47). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜に対して (In Contrast To / While X Is..., Y Is...)
meaning: In contrast to / whereas; also toward a target in a different use.
connection: Noun + に対して | Clause (plain form + の) + に対して
nuance: 〜に対して / 〜のに対して clearly contrasts two different, separate entities or actions: "unlike ~, ... / in contrast to ~, whereas ...". FORMATION (Printed p. 24): ・Noun + に対して (兄に対して弟は: in contrast to older brother, younger brother is...). ・Clause (plain form + な/である for な-adj, + な/である/の for Noun) + のに対して (都市部で人口が増加しているのに対して、地方では過疎化が進んでいる: Whereas urban population grows, rural population declines). ・兄が活発なのに対して、弟はおとなしい (Whereas older brother is lively, younger brother is quiet). DISTINCTION FROM 反面: 反面 contrasts dual aspects of the SAME entity; 〜に対して contrasts TWO DISTINCT subjects/entities.
keyTakeaway: 〜に対して / 〜のに対して: Contrasts TWO DIFFERENT entities/subjects ("whereas X is..., in contrast Y is..."). Contrasts with 反面 which examines internal duality of a single entity.

sentences.japanese: 都市部で人口が急増しているのに対して、地方では過疎化が深刻化している。
sentences.english: In contrast to urban areas where the population is skyrocketing, depopulation is becoming severe in rural regions.
sentences.literal: Urban-areas-in population rapidly-increasing whereas, rural-regions-in depopulation severe-becoming.

tokens.word: 急増しているのに対して
tokens.reading: きゅうぞうしているのにたいして
tokens.romaji: kyuuzou shite iru no ni taishite

sentences.nuanceNote: Contrasting socioeconomic trends between metropolis and countryside.

sentences.japanese: 兄は静かなのに対して、弟はよく話します。
sentences.english: My older brother is quiet, whereas my younger brother talks a lot.
sentences.nuanceNote: A clause is nominalized with の before に対して. This compares different subjects.

sentences.japanese: この店の店員は客に対して親切です。
sentences.english: The staff at this shop are kind toward customers.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nに対して identifies the target of an attitude; it does not mean in contrast to here.

quiz.question: 昨日は大雨だった（　　）に対して、今日は雲一つない快晴だ。
quiz.translation: In contrast to yesterday which had heavy downpours, today is clear skies without a single cloud.
quiz.grammarFocus: 普通形 + のに対して (Contrasting clauses)
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + に対して | 普通形 (な-adj + な/である, Noun + である) + のに対して

explanations.reason: Correct! Plain clause + のに対して is required when contrasting entire predicative clauses.
Incorrect. ことに対して is unidiomatic here.
Incorrect. ものに対して is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. わけに対して does not form this comparative pattern.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 24 (PDF p. 47). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜に比べて (Compared With / Relative To)
meaning: Establishes a baseline entity X against which another entity Y is measured and evaluated.
connection: Noun + に比べて / に比べると
nuance: 〜に比べて / 〜に比べると uses Noun as a comparative benchmark to evaluate a difference in degree or quality: "compared with / relative to". FORMATION (Printed pp. 24-25): ・Noun + に比べて / Noun + に比べると. ・去年に比べて、今年は物価がかなり上がっている (Compared to last year, prices have risen significantly this year). ・兄に比べて弟の方が背が高い (Compared to the older brother, the younger brother is taller). ・以前に比べると、町がずいぶん静かになった (Compared to before, the town has become much quieter). FOCUS: Focuses on comparative degree measurement against a baseline standard.
keyTakeaway: Noun + に比べて / に比べると: "compared with / relative to Noun". Uses Noun as a baseline benchmark to measure a difference in degree or quality.

sentences.japanese: 今年の夏は、例年に比べて格段に猛暑日が続いている。
sentences.english: Compared to ordinary years, extremely hot days are continuing at a markedly higher frequency this summer.
sentences.literal: This-year summer, average-years-to compared remarkably heatwave-days continuing.
sentences.nuanceNote: Climatic comparison against historical baseline.

sentences.japanese: 去年に比べて、今年の冬はずっと雪が多い。
sentences.english: Compared to last year, this winter has far more snow.
sentences.nuanceNote: Noun + に比べて evaluates the current situation against a prior baseline standard.

sentences.japanese: 電車を利用するのは、車を運転するのに比べて、到着時間の予測が立てやすい。
sentences.english: Taking the train makes arrival times much more predictable compared to driving a car.
sentences.nuanceNote: Verb-plain + のに比べて cleanly contrasts two nominalized action clauses.

quiz.question: 去年と（　　）、今年は涼しいです。
quiz.translation: Compared with last year, this year is cool.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + に比べて (Comparative benchmark)
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + に比べて / に比べ

explanations.reason: と比べて links the comparison to the main clause.
比べる needs a different following structure.
比べたの cannot connect directly to this clause.
比べます does not connect the clauses as written.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 24 (PDF p. 47). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜一方で・〜というより
meaning: Contrast coexisting aspects or choose a more accurate description.
connection: Plain form + 一方で | Word / Plain form + というより (むしろ)
nuance: This card covers two high-frequency comparative discourse expressions: (1) 〜一方で (On One Hand... On the Other Hand, p. 24): ・Plain form (+ な/である for な-adj, + である for Noun) + 一方(で). ・Presents two opposing sides, dual simultaneous tendencies, or concurrent contrasting phenomena ("while at the same time on the other hand"): ・政府は景気回復を発表する一方で、国民の不安は高まっている (While the government announces economic recovery, on the other hand, public anxiety is rising). ・会議で自分の意見をはっきり言う一方で、他人の意見も尊重する (Speaks his mind, while at the same time respecting others). (2) 〜というより (Rather Than Say X, It's More Like Y, p. 25): ・Word / Plain form + というより (often accompanied by むしろ). ・Indicates that expression Y is more accurate, appropriate, or fitting than expression X: ・あの人は指導者というより、友達のようだ (More like a friend than an instructor). ・冷たいというよりむしろ涼しい (Cool rather than cold). ・美人というより可愛い (Cute rather than beautiful).
keyTakeaway: 〜一方で: Dual concurrent opposing trends ("while A, at the same time B"). 〜というより: Nuance correction ("rather than call it X, it is more like Y"). Often paired with むしろ.

sentences.japanese: この部屋は狭いというより、物が多すぎるのです。
sentences.english: Rather than the room being small, it has too many things in it.

sentences.japanese: この町は便利な一方で、家賃が高いです。
sentences.english: This town is convenient, while rents are high.
sentences.nuanceNote: な-adjective + な一方で links coexisting aspects.

sentences.japanese: 彼は怒っているというより、困っているようです。
sentences.english: He seems troubled rather than angry.
sentences.nuanceNote: というより replaces a less accurate description with a more fitting one.

quiz.question: あの人は学者（　　）、むしろ優れた実業家と言ったほうがふさわしい。
quiz.translation: Rather than calling that person a scholar, it's more appropriate to say he is an accomplished businessman.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜というより (Rather than X, more like Y)
quiz.ruleHint: X というより Y expresses that Y is a more accurate description than X.

explanations.reason: Correct! 〜というより reframes the description: rather than a scholar, an entrepreneur.
Incorrect. 一方で contrasts two existing co-present realities, rather than choosing a more fitting label.
Incorrect. 反面 contrasts two sides of the same entity.
Incorrect. わりに expresses disproportionate expectation ('considering that').

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 24 (PDF p. 47). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ためだ / 〜ために (Objective Cause: Due to / Owing to)
meaning: Formal written and broadcast expression stating an objective cause or reason: 'Due to X, consequence Y resulted'.
connection: Noun + の / な-adj + な / Verb/い-adj (plain) + ため(に) / ためだ
nuance: 〜ためだ / 〜ために expresses objective causality: "because of ~ / due to ~, ... resulted". FORMATION (Printed p. 30): ・Noun + の + ため(に) / Plain form (+ な/である for な-adj, + の/である for Noun) + ため(に) / ためだ. ・大雪のため、電車が大幅に遅れました (Due to heavy snow, trains were delayed). ・事前の準備が不十分だったため、失敗した (Failed because prior preparation was inadequate). ・申請手続きが複雑なために、時間がかかった (Took time due to complex procedures). REGISTER & VOLITION RESTRICTION (p. 30): Slightly formal written/spoken register. Clause B CANNOT be a speaker request, command, or volitional invitation (*雨が降っているため、傘を持っていきなさい is ungrammatical; must use から instead).
keyTakeaway: 〜ため(に) / ためだ: Objective cause/consequence ("due to / because of"). Formal register. Connections: Noun+の / な-adj+な / Verb plain + ために. Ban on requests/commands in clause B.

sentences.japanese: 強風と大雨のため、全便の飛行機が見合わせとなっております。
sentences.english: Due to strong winds and heavy rain, all flights are currently suspended.
sentences.literal: Strong-wind and heavy-rain due-to, all-flights airplane suspended become.
sentences.nuanceNote: Formal public transportation announcement.

sentences.japanese: 大雪のため、電車が遅れています。
sentences.english: Trains are delayed because of heavy snow.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nのため identifies a cause. This is not a purpose someone intends to achieve.

sentences.japanese: 事故があったために、道路が通行止めになりました。
sentences.english: The road was closed because there had been an accident.
sentences.nuanceNote: Past factual clause + ために gives a cause; compare a deliberate purpose such as 留学するために貯金する.

quiz.question: 道路工事のため（　　）、通行止めです。
quiz.translation: The road is closed because of construction.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + の + ため (Formal objective cause)
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + ため（に） (な-adj takes な, Noun takes の: 大雪のために)

explanations.reason: ために introduces the cause.
ためを is not this cause linker.
ためが does not connect these clauses.
ためと is not this cause linker.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 30 (PDF p. 53). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ことから (Origin of Name, Judgment, or Fact: Arising from the Fact That)
meaning: Points to the historical origin, observable characteristic, or evidential cue that led to a name, reputation, or deduction: 'Named so / Inferred because of X'.
connection: Plain form (+ な/である for な-adj, + である for Noun) + ことから
nuance: 〜ことから expresses that an observable fact ~ serves as the origin, reason, or clue for a name, a judgment, or a known truth: "arising from the fact that ~ / from the evidence that ~". FORMATION (Printed p. 30): ・Plain form (+ な/である for な-adj, + である for Noun) + ことから. (1) Origin of Names/Titles: ・富士山が見えることから、この町は富士見町と呼ばれている (Because Mt. Fuji is visible, this town is called Fujimi-cho). ・形が富士山に似ていることから、「小富士」と呼ばれている (Called "Little Fuji" because of its shape). (2) Basis for Deduction/Discovery: ・道が濡れていたことから、昨夜雨が降ったと分かった (From the fact that the roads were wet, we knew it rained). RESTRICTION (p. 30): Clause B cannot express speaker volition, requests, or commands.
keyTakeaway: 〜ことから: Observable fact serves as the origin of a name or basis of a deduction ("arising from the fact that / called X because..."). Formations: Plain form (+ な for な-adj, + である for Noun) + ことから.

sentences.japanese: 道が濡れていることから、昨夜雨が降ったことが分かる。
sentences.english: From the fact that the roads are wet, we can deduce that it rained last night.
sentences.literal: Roads wet-are fact-from, last-night rain fell fact understand.

tokens.meaning: from the fact that they are wet

sentences.nuanceNote: Physical evidence serving as deductive basis.

sentences.japanese: 桜の木が多いことから、この通りは桜通りと呼ばれています。
sentences.english: This street is called Sakura Street because it has many cherry trees.
sentences.nuanceNote: An observed fact explains how a name arose.

sentences.japanese: 電気が消えていることから、店は閉まっていると判断しました。
sentences.english: From the fact that the lights were off, I judged that the shop was closed.
sentences.nuanceNote: ことから identifies the evidence supporting a judgment, not just a personal excuse.

quiz.question: 名前の由来を説明します。富士山が見える（　　）から、富士見坂と呼ばれています。
quiz.translation: The slope is called Fujimizaka because Mount Fuji can be seen from it.
quiz.grammarFocus: Clause + ことから (Origin of name)
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + ことから (な-adj takes な/である, Noun takes である)

explanations.reason: A plain clause + ことから gives the basis for the name.
ことのから does not form this pattern.
ことにから incorrectly stacks particles.
ことをから does not form this pattern.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 30 (PDF p. 53). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜のだから / 〜んだから (Since It Is an Acknowledged Reality)
meaning: Since that is the situation; given that …
connection: Plain form (+ な for な-adj/Noun) + のだから / んだから
nuance: 〜のだから / 〜んだから indicates that fact ~ is an acknowledged, established reality known to both parties, and therefore consequence ... naturally follows: "since it is an undeniable reality that ~, naturally ...". FORMATION (Printed p. 31): ・Plain form (+ な for な-adj, + な for Noun) + のだから / んだから. ・世界は広いのだから、色々な人がいるのは当然だ (Since the world is vast, of course there are diverse people). ・あなたはもう高校生なんだから、自分の部屋は自分で掃除しなさい (Since you're in high school, clean your own room!). ・全員が全力を尽くしたのだから、悔やむことはない (Since everyone did their best, there's no need to regret). CRITICAL PRAGMATIC CONTRAST (p. 31): Unlike other cause patterns (ため, せい, ことから) which ban volitions, Clause B here EXPLICITLY expresses speaker judgment, personal resolve, strong advice, or commands/requests!
keyTakeaway: 〜のだから / んだから: "since it is an acknowledged reality that...". Crucial rule: Clause B EXPLICITLY expresses speaker judgment, advice, requests, or commands (やりなさい, 悔やむことはない).

sentences.japanese: まだ子供なのだから、失敗してもくよくよ悩む必要はありません。
sentences.english: Since you are still a child, there is no need to brood over your mistakes.
sentences.literal: Still child is-since, fail even worry necessity is-not.
sentences.nuanceNote: Appealing to youth as a compassionate ground for reassurance.

sentences.japanese: 明日は試験なのだから、今夜は早く寝たほうがいいです。
sentences.english: Since you have an exam tomorrow, you should go to bed early tonight.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nなのだから treats the premise as relevant and supports advice.

sentences.japanese: 十年も住んでいたのだから、この町に詳しいでしょう。
sentences.english: Since they lived here for ten years, they probably know the town well.
sentences.nuanceNote: The conclusion can be an expectation, not only a command. Tone can make the reminder sound insistent.

quiz.question: 自分で決めたこと（　　）だから、最後まで諦めずにやり通しなさい。
quiz.translation: Since this is something you decided for yourself, carry it through to the end without giving up.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + なのだから / なんだから shared premise
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + のだから / んだから (な-adj / Noun takes な: 好きなのだから, 子供なのだから)

explanations.reason: Correct! Noun こと connects via なん to だから (ことなんだから / ことなのだから).
Incorrect. だんだから is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. のんだから is nonsensical.
Incorrect. いんだから is invalid.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 30 (PDF p. 53). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜おかげで vs 〜せいで (Grace of / Due to Fault of)
meaning: Expresses causal attribution: おかげで attributes a positive outcome to a benefactor; せいで blames an adverse outcome on a scapegoat.
connection: Noun + の / Plain form (+ な for な-adj) + おかげで (positive) | せいで (negative)
nuance: Shin Kanzen Master N3 contrasts positive gratitude against negative blame: FORMATION (Printed p. 31): ・Noun + の / Plain form (+ な for な-adj) + おかげ(で) vs せい(で) / せいだ. (1) 〜おかげで ("Thanks to...", Positive): ・Expresses gratitude for a beneficial, desirable influence or favor (先生の熱心なご指導のおかげで合格できた: Passed thanks to teacher's enthusiastic guidance; 薬を飲んだおかげで治った). (2) 〜せいで ("Because of / Due to fault of...", Negative): ・Assigns blame or criticism for an unfavorable, undesirable outcome (睡眠不足のせいで試合で力を出せなかった: Couldn't perform due to lack of sleep; 昨夜窓を開けて寝たせいだ: Because I slept with window open). RESTRICTION (p. 31): Neither pattern can be used with sentences expressing requests, commands, or volitional intentions.
keyTakeaway: 〜おかげで: gratitude for positive outcome ("thanks to"). 〜せいで: blame for negative outcome ("due to fault of / because of"). Noun takes の. Ban on commands/requests in clause B.

sentences.japanese: 先生が熱心に教えてくださったおかげで、無事に合格できました。
sentences.english: Thanks to my teacher teaching me so passionately, I was able to pass safely.
sentences.literal: Teacher passionately taught thanks-to, without-trouble could-pass.

tokens.word: 教えてくださったおかげで
tokens.reading: おしえてくださったおかげで

sentences.nuanceNote: Heartfelt gratitude for mentorship.

sentences.japanese: 連日の夜更かしのせいで、朝から頭痛がひどい。
sentences.english: Because of staying up late night after night, I've had a terrible headache since morning.
sentences.literal: Consecutive-days staying-up-late fault-due-to, morning-from headache severe.
sentences.nuanceNote: Attributing bodily distress to personal poor habit.

sentences.japanese: 友達が手伝ってくれたおかげで、早く終わりました。
sentences.english: Thanks to my friend's help, I finished early.
sentences.nuanceNote: The speaker evaluates the effect positively and attributes it to the help.

sentences.japanese: 夜更かししたせいで、授業中眠くなりました。
sentences.english: Because I stayed up late, I became sleepy during class.
sentences.nuanceNote: せいで attributes an unwanted result; the blamed cause can be one's own action.

quiz.question: 台風の（　　）で、楽しみにしていた旅行が急遽キャンセルになった。
quiz.translation: Because of the typhoon, the trip I had been eagerly anticipating was cancelled at short notice.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + のせいで (Negative causal attribution)
quiz.ruleHint: 普通形 (な-adj + な, Noun + の) + おかげで / せいで

explanations.reason: Correct! せいで is required because cancelling an eagerly awaited trip is a negative/regrettable outcome.
Incorrect. おかげで implies a favorable/happy outcome.
Incorrect. ためで is ungrammatical (must be 台風のため, without で).
Incorrect. ことで is not used for blaming disastrous disruptions.

title: 〜によって・〜による：原因
meaning: A cause or means, depending on context.
connection: Noun + によって、[Clause] | Noun + による + Noun
nuance: Noun + によって / Noun + による + Noun indicates a direct, objective cause or causal agency that produced a significant change, mishap, accident, or occurrence: "caused by / due to / as a result of". FORMATION (Printed p. 30): ・Noun + によって (Clause modifier) ・Noun + による + Noun (Noun modifier) ・地震によって多くの古い木造家屋が倒壊した (Many wooden houses collapsed due to the earthquake). ・スマートフォンの不注意による事故が増加している (Accidents caused by smartphone inattention are increasing). ・台風による被害が広がっている (Damage caused by the typhoon is spreading). FORMAL CONSTRAINT (p. 30): Formal news and documentary register. Not used for states or speaker requests/volitions.
keyTakeaway: Noun + によって = causal clause modifier ("due to earthquake"). Noun + による + Noun = causal noun modifier ("accidents caused by inattention"). Formal reporting register for disasters/accidents.

sentences.japanese: 強風によって木が倒れました。
sentences.english: A tree fell because of the strong wind.

sentences.japanese: 台風によって、多くの家が被害を受けました。
sentences.english: Many houses were damaged by the typhoon.
sentences.nuanceNote: によって identifies the cause of the damage.

sentences.japanese: 地震による被害を調べています。
sentences.english: We are investigating damage caused by the earthquake.
sentences.nuanceNote: による modifies the following noun; によって normally connects to a predicate.

quiz.question: 先日の記録的な台風（　　）、多くの鉄道路線が終日運休となった。
quiz.translation: Due to the record-breaking typhoon the other day, many train lines were suspended all day.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜によって (Formal Cause / Reason)
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + によって specifies an external formal cause or natural agent.

explanations.reason: Correct! 台風によって marks the natural cause leading to train suspension.
Incorrect. にとって marks evaluative standpoint ('from the perspective of').
Incorrect. について introduces a topic of discussion/study ('about').
Incorrect. に対して marks a target of action or sharp contrast.

sourceReference: Section starts on printed p. 30 (PDF p. 53). Original revision notes; not a transcription.

title: 〜ては / 〜では (Negative Inevitable Consequence)
meaning: If that condition holds, an undesirable result follows or something cannot be done.
connection: 動て形 + は | い形くて + は | な形・名 + では | 普通形（な形だ-・名だ-）+ のでは
nuance: 【Shin Kanzen Master N3 p. 32 正式規則】「〜という事実（仮定の状況）から、…という悪い結果が予想される。」Given that (or assuming) condition A holds, an undesirable result B will inevitably occur. 後ろの節（…）はマイナスの意味を持つ表現に限定され、話者の希望・意向を表す文や、相手への働きかけ（指示・依頼・命令・勧誘）の文は絶対に来ない。
keyTakeaway: Condition A inevitably leads to negative result B. Strictly limited to negative outcomes. Volitions, requests, and commands are strictly banned in clause B.

sentences.japanese: 手術をしないで放っておいては、命にかかわる。
sentences.english: Leaving it unattended without surgery will endanger one's life.
sentences.literal: Surgery without-doing leaving-alone if, life to relates.
sentences.nuanceNote: SKM N3 verbatim sentence 1: grave consequence endangering life.

sentences.japanese: 無責任な態度をとっていては、信用を失います。
sentences.english: If you maintain such an irresponsible attitude, you will lose everyone's trust.
sentences.literal: Irresponsible attitude taking if, trust lose.
sentences.nuanceNote: SKM N3 verbatim sentence 2: cautionary warning against continued irresponsible attitude.

sentences.japanese: 家を建て始めるのがこんなに遅れては、年内に仕上がらない。
sentences.english: With the start of house construction delayed this much, it will not be finished within the year.
sentences.literal: House build start this-much delaying if, within-year not-finish.
sentences.nuanceNote: SKM N3 verbatim sentence 3: inevitable scheduling failure due to delay.

sentences.japanese: 毎日こんなに遊んでいては、来月の大学入試に合格できませんよ。
sentences.english: If you spend every day playing around like this, you will never pass next month's university entrance exam.
sentences.literal: Every-day like-this playing if, next-month's exam pass cannot.
sentences.nuanceNote: Warning against persistent idleness.

sentences.japanese: 毎晩そんなに遅く寝ては、体に悪いですよ。
sentences.english: If you go to bed that late every night, it is bad for your health.
sentences.nuanceNote: ては introduces a condition evaluated negatively in the following clause.

sentences.japanese: この字では、小さすぎて読めません。
sentences.english: With writing like this, it is too small to read.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nでは presents the existing condition as inadequate for the desired result.

quiz.question: こんなに高く（　　）、買えません。
quiz.translation: If it is this expensive, I cannot buy it.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + では negative consequence conditional
quiz.ruleHint: V-て + は | い-adj くて + は | な-adj / Noun + では

explanations.reason: 高い becomes 高くては.
高くには is not this construction.
高くでは is not the required adjective te-form.
高くとは is not the required conditional form.
